water_harvesting_conservation__asset_thr.mechanism: Drought harms the investment mainly by leaving it without water or unbuilt. In Kenya, a drought season's poor rainfall generated very little runoff and the earth dam barely held any water [ev_climate_shock_barr05_6]. In Tunisia, drought caused a shortfall in the spate-irrigation and water-recharge works established in the governorate of Medenine, where only 15 were built against a target of 95 [ev_drought_hazard_iegtun13_2].
water_harvesting_conservation__asset_thr.conditionality: Neither unit measures structural damage to built works: the Kenyan dam was intact but empty, a loss of function for that season, and the Tunisian figure comes from a single ex-post review of project completion data on works that were never built [ev_climate_shock_barr05_6, ev_drought_hazard_iegtun13_2]. Units about benefits shrinking in drought are effect units recording a benefit shortfall, not damage, and practitioner coping ratings are not counted here.

water_harvesting_conservation__asset_thr.mechanism: Heavy rain moderately damages water-harvesting and conservation works. In China, storms caused widespread damage to terraces, with few local funds for repair [ev_climate_shock_iegchn07_7]; in Algeria, terraces and other traditional works were badly damaged or destroyed by extreme rain in recent years and are rebuilt after each event [ev_climate_shock_roose17_2_av], stone lines are overtopped by storms above 50 mm [ev_climate_shock_roose17_1_av], and unmaintained banquette networks breached in chains under long torrential rain [ev_climate_shock_arab04_1_av]. In a Kenyan trial, tied ridges collapsed in heavy rain and had to be rebuilt within the season [ev_climate_shock_ndun23_1_av]; in Morocco, earth bunds are overtopped in the biggest storms [ev_climate_shock_roos10_1_av]. A review of terraces worldwide reports riser collapse and landslides that can turn into debris flows in very heavy storms [ev_climate_shock_arna15_8_av, ev_climate_shock_arna15_9_av], poorly built vineyard terraces in Spain slid after a single storm [ev_climate_shock_wei16_2_av], and check dams often fail in extreme rain [ev_climate_shock_luca21_1_av]. Practitioner ratings agree: pits and bunds in Niger, terraces in Rwanda and Cape Verde and check dams in Nepal are rated as not coping well with local rainstorms [ev_asset_extreme_rainfall_wocat_1219_2014_local_rainstorm, ev_asset_extreme_rainfall_wocat_1613_2014_local_rainstorm, ev_asset_extreme_rainfall_wocat_1614_2014_local_rainstorm, ev_asset_extreme_rainfall_wocat_1616_2014_local_rainstorm, ev_asset_extreme_rainfall_wocat_1652_2014_local_rainstorm, ev_asset_extreme_rainfall_wocat_1553_2012_local_rainstorm, ev_asset_extreme_rainfall_wocat_1573_2013_local_rainstorm, ev_asset_extreme_rainfall_wocat_1493_2011_local_rainstorm].
water_harvesting_conservation__asset_thr.conditionality: Damage varies by design and upkeep. Many practitioners rate their works as coping well, for example in Tunisia, Eritrea, China, Kenya, Yemen and Uganda [ev_asset_extreme_rainfall_wocat_1013_2011_local_rainstorm, ev_asset_extreme_rainfall_wocat_1333_2010_local_rainstorm, ev_asset_extreme_rainfall_wocat_1455_2011_local_rainstorm, ev_asset_extreme_rainfall_wocat_1537_2012_local_rainstorm, ev_asset_extreme_rainfall_wocat_1560_2013_local_rainstorm, ev_asset_extreme_rainfall_wocat_1587_2013_local_rainstorm], and some in Thailand, Bangladesh and Jordan as coping very well [ev_asset_extreme_rainfall_wocat_4281_2018_local_rainstorm, ev_asset_extreme_rainfall_wocat_4284_2018_local_hailstorm, ev_asset_extreme_rainfall_wocat_5770_2020_local_rainstorm, ev_asset_extreme_rainfall_wocat_5860_2021_local_rainstorm]. Several failures are tied to missing maintenance as much as to the rain [ev_climate_shock_arab04_1_av, ev_climate_shock_luca21_1_av]. Most units are practitioner ratings without damage records; the measured findings are few and site-specific, and several are cited second-hand.

water_harvesting_conservation__asset_thr.mechanism: In Algeria a poorly maintained banquette network fails in a chain reaction during torrential and prolonged rains, the smallest unrepaired breach spreading sliding through the whole network [ev_climate_shock_arab04_1_av]. In Morocco staggered earth bunds (tabia) in Morocco store the runoff of rains below 50 mm, but in the biggest storms the excess overtops the bunds and gullies the slope [ev_climate_shock_roos10_1_av].
water_harvesting_conservation__asset_thr.conditionality: Both are expert or survey statements without damage counts; the Algerian failure is explicitly tied to poor maintenance, and the Moroccan statement implies the bunds hold for ordinary rains and fail only in the largest storms [ev_climate_shock_arab04_1_av, ev_climate_shock_roos10_1_av].

water_harvesting_conservation__asset_thr.mechanism: In high-income settings, two monitored structures give opposite local-rainstorm records. In Germany, small field-border detention ponds that temporarily stored 200-500 cubic metres of runoff per event never failed over the monitoring period [ev_climate_shock_fien05_1_av]. In Spain, a global synthesis of terracing found poorly structured vineyard terraces in Priorat suffered severe landslides after only a single rainstorm, causing substantial damage to plants and drainage systems [ev_climate_shock_wei16_2_av].
water_harvesting_conservation__asset_thr.conditionality: The two units disagree because they describe different kinds of structure: the German ponds are purpose-built storage works that coped, while the Spanish case is terracing the reviewers single out as poorly built. The German no-failure record only covers the flood sizes observed during its monitoring period, and neither unit states how severe the triggering rainstorm was, so no single direction is stated for this income group.

water_harvesting_conservation__asset_thr.mechanism: Storms cause extensive damage to terraces on China's Loess Plateau with few local funds to repair it, and WOCAT compilers judge pits, bunds and trenches in Niger, radical terraces in Rwanda, gully-plugging check dams in Nepal and ripper tillage in Zambia not to cope well with local rainstorms [ev_climate_shock_iegchn07_7, ev_asset_extreme_rainfall_wocat_1219_2014_local_rainstorm, ev_asset_extreme_rainfall_wocat_1553_2012_local_rainstorm, ev_asset_extreme_rainfall_wocat_1493_2011_local_rainstorm, ev_asset_extreme_rainfall_wocat_1139_2013_local_rainstorm].
water_harvesting_conservation__asset_thr.conditionality: Other compilers in Tunisia, Eritrea, Kenya, Yemen, Uganda, India, Madagascar and Ethiopia judge coping as good, and those in Burkina Faso, Bangladesh and Somalia as moderate; the Haiti and Bangladesh terrace sheets judge coping with landslides as very good [ev_asset_extreme_rainfall_wocat_1013_2011_local_rainstorm, ev_asset_extreme_rainfall_wocat_1537_2012_local_rainstorm, ev_asset_extreme_rainfall_wocat_7778_2026_local_rainstorm, ev_asset_extreme_rainfall_wocat_3223_2017_landslide]. All units except the Loess Plateau observation are practitioner judgements without damage records, and for field-level practices a not-well rating describes exposure of fields rather than damage to a structure.

water_harvesting_conservation__asset_thr.mechanism: Heavy storms damage the structures themselves. A review of farming terraces finds that soil saturation from very heavy storms, or runoff accumulating behind the walls, is a determining factor in the failure and movement of terrace risers, and that with heavy rainfall the shallow landslides normally confined to small parts of a terrace can become debris flows affecting the entire terraced hillside [ev_climate_shock_arna15_8_av, ev_climate_shock_arna15_9_av]. A worldwide review of check dams notes that cases of check-dam inefficacy are common and often associated with structure failures in response to extreme rainfall events or lack of maintenance [ev_climate_shock_luca21_1_av].
water_harvesting_conservation__asset_thr.conditionality: Both sources are reviews describing failure modes, not measurements of how often or how badly structures fail, so the strength is not quantified; the check-dam statement is the authors' assertion and couples extreme rainfall with lack of maintenance, so the causes are not separated [ev_climate_shock_luca21_1_av]. Terrace riser failure is also tied to runoff accumulating behind the walls, which drainage and upkeep influence [ev_climate_shock_arna15_8_av].

water_harvesting_conservation__asset_thr.mechanism: Among upper-middle-income contexts, exposure to local rainstorms varies by site: projects in China reported their structures cope well [ev_asset_extreme_rainfall_wocat_1455_2011_local_rainstorm, ev_asset_extreme_rainfall_wocat_1522_2010_local_rainstorm], and a project in Thailand reported coping very well [ev_asset_extreme_rainfall_wocat_4281_2018_local_rainstorm].
water_harvesting_conservation__asset_thr.conditionality: This is not universal: a project in Cape Verde reported its structure copes not well with local rainstorms [ev_asset_extreme_rainfall_wocat_1573_2013_local_rainstorm]. Part of this effect is off-site (downstream or landscape scale) rather than on the adopting farm.

water_harvesting_conservation__asset_thr.mechanism: WOCAT compilers rate bench terraces in Bangladesh as coping moderately with forest fire and well with land fire, and stone check walls and check dams in India as coping well with forest fire [ev_asset_fire_wocat_4284_2018_forest_fire, ev_asset_fire_wocat_4284_2018_land_fire, ev_asset_fire_wocat_5210_2019_forest_fire].
water_harvesting_conservation__asset_thr.conditionality: All units are practitioner ratings from two technology sheets with no observed damage; earth and stone works offer little to burn, so any fire effect would fall on vegetation on or around them.

water_harvesting_conservation__asset_thr.mechanism: Flood damages the water-harvesting investment itself by overwhelming or breaching the structure. In Ethiopia, boulder-faced log check dams designed to be more resistant to abrasive flows still had 37.9% fail after a high-magnitude runoff event [ev_check_dam_failure_fran21_2]. On China's Loess Plateau, a single large flood — more than 200 mm of rain — damaged 20% of the main check dams in the Wuding River watershed [ev_climate_shock_shi19_3]. In Tunisia, a project reported the structure copes not well with general river flooding [ev_asset_flood_wocat_1013_2011_general_river_flood].
water_harvesting_conservation__asset_thr.conditionality: Not every structure is equally exposed: in Jordan, a project reported the same kind of structure copes very well with flash flooding [ev_asset_flood_wocat_5770_2020_flash_flood], showing vulnerability depends heavily on flood type and local design, not on water harvesting as a single risk category. Part of this effect is off-site (downstream or landscape scale) rather than on the adopting farm.

water_harvesting_conservation__asset_thr.mechanism: In low- and lower-middle-income contexts, flood damage to water-harvesting structures is severe and recurring. In Ethiopia, boulder-faced log check dams designed to resist abrasive flows still had 37.9% fail after a high-magnitude runoff event [ev_check_dam_failure_fran21_2]. Projects in Tunisia and Niger both reported their structures cope not well with general river flooding [ev_asset_flood_wocat_1013_2011_general_river_flood, ev_asset_flood_wocat_1219_2014_general_river_flood].
water_harvesting_conservation__asset_thr.conditionality: Exposure is not uniform even within this income band: in Ethiopia, a different project reported its structure copes very well with flash flooding [ev_asset_flood_wocat_6716_2023_flash_flood], so the severe class reflects general river flood exposure more than every flood type. Part of this effect is off-site (downstream or landscape scale) rather than on the adopting farm.

water_harvesting_conservation__asset_thr.mechanism: A review of terraces names torrential rain, together with the collapse of walls and vegetation strips and use after abandonment, among the conditions that degrade terraces [ev_erosion_hazard_willem21_3]. WOCAT compilers judge a check dam for land in China and stone-wall terraces in Cabo Verde to cope well with river floods, and marab floodplain agriculture and mechanised Vallerani micro-catchments in Jordan to cope very well with flash floods [ev_asset_flood_wocat_1455_2011_general_river_flood, ev_asset_flood_wocat_1573_2013_general_river_flood, ev_asset_flood_wocat_5770_2020_flash_flood, ev_asset_flood_wocat_5860_2021_flash_flood]. On China's Loess Plateau, sediment-filled check dams are vulnerable to large floods: heavy rain on 26 July 2017 in Suide and Zizhou counties caused a large flood that damaged 20% of the main check dams [ev_climate_shock_shi19_3].
water_harvesting_conservation__asset_thr.conditionality: The pool is small: apart from the review and the Loess Plateau damage count, it consists of practitioner judgements from documented technology sheets rather than measured damage, and the review ties damage to abandonment as much as to rainfall. The Loess Plateau damage hit dams already filled with sediment, so it is partly a design-life and maintenance effect [ev_climate_shock_shi19_3]. The Jordanian ratings carry no damage signal at all.

water_harvesting_conservation__asset_thr.mechanism: The WOCAT compiler for mechanised Vallerani micro water harvesting in Jordan records that the technology copes very well with extreme winter conditions [ev_asset_frost_wocat_5860_2021_extreme_winter_conditions].
water_harvesting_conservation__asset_thr.conditionality: The evidence is too thin to state a frost sensitivity: one practitioner rating from an upper-middle-income country outside the target band, with no observed damage and no frost event described, so it does not show the works go undamaged elsewhere [ev_asset_frost_wocat_5860_2021_extreme_winter_conditions]. What is missing is a second independent source or one observed account of frost damage or its absence.

water_harvesting_conservation__asset_thr.mechanism: The WOCAT compiler for gabions and rock check dams in Somalia rates the technology as coping moderately with heatwaves [ev_asset_heat_stress_wocat_7778_2026_heatwave].
water_harvesting_conservation__asset_thr.conditionality: This rests on a single practitioner rating with no stated reason or observed damage, for a structure of stone and wire that heat would affect mainly through the vegetation around it [ev_asset_heat_stress_wocat_7778_2026_heatwave].

water_harvesting_conservation__asset_thr.mechanism: Slope failure damages terraces where slopes are unstable or terraces are abandoned: in the Tizi Ouzou region of Algeria 19% of banquettes on marls and clays were damaged by landslides and as many by gullying, and in Mediterranean regions over 50% of abandoned terraces were vulnerable to gully erosion and landslides that collapse the dry-stone walls [ev_climate_shock_arab04_2_av, ev_climate_shock_wei16_1_av]. Among WOCAT compilers, stone check walls and check dams in India are rated as coping only moderately with landslides [ev_asset_landslide_wocat_5210_2019_landslide].
water_harvesting_conservation__asset_thr.conditionality: Other compilers rate stone lines in Tunisia, a masonry check dam in Ethiopia and a continuous bench terrace for tea in Thailand as coping well, and vetiver-hedge bench terraces with trees in Haiti and bench terraces on hilly slopes in Bangladesh as coping very well [ev_asset_landslide_wocat_6610_2022_landslide, ev_asset_landslide_wocat_6716_2023_landslide, ev_asset_landslide_wocat_4281_2018_landslide, ev_asset_landslide_wocat_3223_2017_landslide, ev_asset_landslide_wocat_4284_2018_landslide]. The damage figures are secondary citations tied to marl and clay substrates and to abandonment, not to maintained terraces, and the ratings come from a small set of technology sheets rather than measurements [ev_climate_shock_arab04_2_av, ev_climate_shock_wei16_1_av].

water_harvesting_conservation__asset_thr.mechanism: Sediment trapped behind water-harvesting structures slowly fills them, so they lose storage and soak up less water; the damage is real but builds up slowly, so it is rated slight. Sedimentation is described as perhaps the main reason sand dams fail [ev_asset_failure_ritc21_3]. In Tigray, Ethiopia, dams designed to last 30 years were set to fill in 4.4 to 5.7 years [ev_asset_siltation_saru19_1], and 50% of Ethiopian reservoirs studied were on course to lose their useful life before half their design period [ev_asset_siltation_saru19_2]. In Zambia, 8 of 10 reservoirs lost storage to silt and 3 lost over half their capacity [ev_asset_siltation_saru19_4]; 61% of Tigray micro-dams had benefits threatened by silt [ev_climate_shock_gebr18_5]; and in India 31% of earthen dams silted up within five years [ev_erosion_hazard_iegind11_12]. Check dams filled to more than 80% of their capacity within four years in Arizona [ev_sediment_retention_poly14_1_av] and fill quickly under heavy sediment loads in China [ev_climate_shock_shi19_4]; small Moroccan hill dams lose 0.5 to 1% of their capacity each year [ev_sediment_retention_roos10_1_av]. Silt on the floor of check dams and percolation tanks in India lowers how much water soaks into the ground [ev_climate_shock_dash17_4, ev_climate_shock_mass14_4, ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_glen12_11_av]. In the field, stone bunds in Tigray trap less sediment once the space behind them fills [ev_climate_shock_gebr05_3_av], and in Burkina Faso larger half-moons of 2 and 3 m clog with a crust that cuts infiltration [ev_soil_permeability_zour25h1_8].
water_harvesting_conservation__asset_thr.conditionality: The loss is gradual and can be managed with regular desilting: in Kenya, sand dams lost an estimated 10-25% of storage to silt, which the authors judge is not the main limit on their success [ev_asset_siltation_neuf17_1], while in India desilting has to be repeated during a single programme [ev_asset_siltation_verm19_1]. Several sources tie failure as much to the lack of upkeep as to silt itself: in Morocco, gabions had nearly lost their function four years after the project ended, with no maintenance system in place [ev_erosion_hazard_iegmar09_2], and check-dam benefits fade as the dams fill [ev_sediment_retention_luca21_1_av]. Many findings are cited second-hand and the Indian tank finding is a model [ev_climate_shock_mass14_4]. The silt comes from erosion upstream, so the threat depends on the wider catchment, not just the structure.

water_harvesting_conservation__asset_thr.mechanism: In semi-arid zones, sediment settles inside water-harvesting structures and clogs them. A Kenyan sand-dam assessment estimated an average decrease in water storage of 10-25 percent due to siltation [ev_asset_siltation_neuf17_1]. In semi-arid Arizona rangeland, loose-rock check dams retained sediment and were filled to more than 80 percent of their capacity [ev_sediment_retention_poly14_1_av]. In northern Burkina Faso, the larger 2- and 3-metre half-moon pits showed lower infiltration than control plots, which the authors attribute to a settling crust of suspended sediment clogging the soil during sedimentation [ev_soil_permeability_zour25h1_8].
water_harvesting_conservation__asset_thr.conditionality: The Kenyan assessment itself concludes siltation is not the major constraint on sand-dam performance and is not an inherent limitation of the technology [ev_asset_siltation_neuf17_1]. The Arizona figure measures the check dams filling with retained sediment (the function the dams are built for) rather than damage, over a multi-year record on loose-rock rangeland structures, a different design from most water-harvesting works [ev_sediment_retention_poly14_1_av]. The Burkina Faso finding is specific to the larger half-moon sizes against the control, and measures an infiltration loss, not a storage or structural loss [ev_soil_permeability_zour25h1_8].

water_harvesting_conservation__asset_thr.mechanism: In high-income settings, two well-monitored case studies show water-harvesting structures silting up over a few years. In Germany, small field-border detention ponds needed dredging after their first year, when upslope erosion control was not yet fully effective, but needed no further dredging afterwards [ev_climate_shock_fien05_2_av]. In Arizona, loose-rock check dams on a semi-arid rangeland watershed were filled to more than 80% of their storage capacity within four years [ev_sediment_retention_poly14_1_av].
water_harvesting_conservation__asset_thr.conditionality: Both cases describe siltation building up over years rather than a single event, and both attribute part of the siltation to how well upslope erosion is controlled — in the German case, the dredging need fell away once on-site erosion control became effective [ev_climate_shock_fien05_2_av]. The Arizona figure describes the check dams doing their job (trapping sediment) rather than failing, and both sites are temperate/dryland, high-income contexts rather than the LIC/LMIC target.

water_harvesting_conservation__asset_thr.mechanism: No unit describes how wind damages the works; the row rests on WOCAT compiler judgements of how terraces, bunds, pits, check dams, sand dams and spate systems cope with local windstorms and tropical storms. Most are judged to cope well, while progressive bench terraces in China and fascine vegetative check dams in Madagascar are judged not to cope well [ev_asset_wind_cyclone_wocat_1522_2010_local_windstorm, ev_asset_wind_cyclone_wocat_6478_2022_tropical_storm].
water_harvesting_conservation__asset_thr.conditionality: All units are practitioner judgements from documented technology sheets, not measurements; compilers for bench terraces in Bangladesh and gabion works in Somalia judge coping as moderate, and the Vallerani system in Burkina Faso is judged to cope very well [ev_asset_wind_cyclone_wocat_4284_2018_tropical_storm, ev_asset_wind_cyclone_wocat_7778_2026_local_windstorm, ev_asset_wind_cyclone_wocat_1528_2012_local_windstorm]. For field-level practices such as pits and bunds a rating describes exposure of fields rather than damage to a structure.

water_harvesting_conservation__biodivers.mechanism: In Burkina Faso the proximity of zai pits on bare, crusted land raises germination and seed dispersal, so herbaceous and woody species re-establish on formerly barren fields, and users of small reservoirs in Ghana perceive greener surroundings and improved biodiversity [ev_biodiversity_outcome_roose93_1, ev_biodiversity_outcome_zoug14_1, ev_biodiversity_outcome_kabo04_1, ev_biodiversity_outcome_veno12_1]. WOCAT compilers give a mechanism with each rating: in Somalia improved soil moisture and reduced erosion supported more plant and grass species, and restored vegetation and water availability improved habitat for livestock and small wildlife; in Bhutan the soil became suitable for more diverse crops [ev_biodiversity_outcome_wocat_7778_2026_plant_diversity, ev_biodiversity_outcome_wocat_7778_2026_animal_diversity, ev_biodiversity_outcome_wocat_7778_2026_habitat_diversity, ev_biodiversity_outcome_wocat_6891_2023_plant_diversity]. Embrapa reports that crops, vegetable gardens and orchards on the humid fringes of its barraginhas in Brazil bring back fauna that had disappeared for lack of food [ev_biodiversity_outcome_mira19_3]. A CILSS regional synthesis adds that, on Burkina Faso's Central Plateau, soil and water conservation works (zaï, demi-lunes, stone bunds and permeable rock dams) had a positive impact on the reconstitution of woody vegetation and floristic richness, with 60 species recorded on treated sites [ev_biodiversity_outcome_botreij09_25].
water_harvesting_conservation__biodivers.conditionality: The class is set by the sub-practice vote: the in-field and runoff-storage rows are slight, and the terracing row is conflicting, because a Bhutan compiler rating of more diverse crops stands against an Israeli finding of lost herbaceous species on machine-built terraces; the pooled evidence alone would read stronger [ev_biodiversity_outcome_wocat_6891_2023_plant_diversity, ev_biodiversity_outcome_stav20_9]. The WOCAT units are compiler ratings from technology sheets in Somalia and Bhutan, not measurements, and the Somali sheet supplies separate plant, animal and habitat ratings; the Bhutan rating refers to more diverse crops rather than wild species [ev_biodiversity_outcome_wocat_6891_2023_plant_diversity]. The literature units are descriptive species counts or user perceptions with no untreated comparison, and the zai counts partly restate the same earlier observation [ev_biodiversity_outcome_kabo04_1, ev_biodiversity_outcome_zoug14_1, ev_biodiversity_outcome_roose93_1]. The barraginha fauna finding is an adopter-reported indicator in Embrapa's self-assessment of its own technology, and the gain comes through the gardens and orchards on the humid fringe rather than the basin itself [ev_biodiversity_outcome_mira19_3]. The harm comes from how the works are built: in Israel, earthen contour bench terraces built with heavy machinery strip the soil's A-horizon, and these earthworks have been suggested to reduce herbaceous species richness (Stavi et al., 2015, cited in the later Stavi et al. review) [ev_biodiversity_outcome_stav20_9]. That is a regional synthesis citing a national study team's report rather than a direct measurement, and the untreated-site comparator count sits on the following page of the source and cannot be quoted alongside this passage, so only the treated-site count is reported here [ev_biodiversity_outcome_botreij09_25].

water_harvesting_conservation__biodivers.mechanism: Consecutive years of zai planting pits on formerly bare, barren soil in central Burkina Faso were followed by the re-establishment of herbaceous species and of trees and shrubs.
water_harvesting_conservation__biodivers.conditionality: Both units are secondary citations of earlier zai field observations from Burkina Faso, probably overlapping, reporting species counts on treated land without an untreated comparison or a biodiversity index; the strength of the effect is not quantified.

water_harvesting_conservation__carbon_se.mechanism: Terracing and mulching raise soil carbon by keeping organic matter and sediment on the slope. A meta-analysis of over a thousand paired observations in China found straw mulching raised soil organic carbon by 10.74% to 22.63% depending on region [ev_soil_organic_carbon_zhang26h2_1], and terracing raised soil organic carbon by 60.96% and 14.11% in two regions after 11 to 20 years, and by 33.91% and 53.73% in two other regions after 21 to 30 years [ev_soil_organic_carbon_zhang26h2_10].
water_harvesting_conservation__carbon_se.conditionality: The gain is not universal: in Mexico, infiltration trenches were found to have actually decreased nitrogen and carbon content while increasing bulk density [ev_soil_organic_carbon_locat20_2], and in Burkina Faso, zai pits showed no significant change in soil fertility properties in the short term, even though biomass production had increased [ev_soil_organic_carbon_roose93_1]. Measured harm (maladaptation) — the practice worsening this outcome for some adopters — appears in 1 source. Within this family, micro-catchment systems score strongest and runoff-catchment weakest, so the roll-up states moderate rather than the pooled strong.

water_harvesting_conservation__carbon_se.mechanism: In semi-arid settings the practices add carbon removals mainly through soil storage: organic matter concentrated in zaï pits raised soil organic matter content from 1 to 1.4 percent on soils treated 3 and 5 years earlier in Burkina Faso, and farms using zaï and/or rock bunds there had more soil carbon than a control farm [ev_soil_organic_carbon_kabo04_1, ev_soil_organic_carbon_sawa11h1_3]. Check dams on China's Loess Plateau store carbon in the sediment trapped behind them, and that storage increases with time at both check dam and watershed levels [ev_carbon_sequestration_luca21_1].
water_harvesting_conservation__carbon_se.conditionality: The gain is rated slight because no unit states how large the carbon removal is per hectare or per year: the zaï figure is an organic-matter content change cited second-hand from an earlier study, the Burkina Faso farm comparison is a soil-fertility test against a single control farm, and the Loess Plateau statement is a review citation [ev_soil_organic_carbon_kabo04_1, ev_soil_organic_carbon_sawa11h1_3, ev_carbon_sequestration_luca21_1]. Soil organic matter and trapped sediment stand in for a measured carbon stock change, and carbon in check-dam sediment partly moves carbon eroded from upslope rather than removing new carbon from the air.

water_harvesting_conservation__carbon_se.mechanism: In Burkina Faso, soil and water conservation techniques (rock bunds, zai, and combinations with compost manure) raised soil carbon and nitrogen content and lowered the carbon-to-nitrogen ratio compared with untreated control farms [ev_soil_organic_carbon_sawa11h1_3]. In the Canary Islands, gavias runoff-harvesting fields showed higher organic carbon than adjacent uncultivated soil, though the difference across the sampled plots (n = 40–41) was not large enough to be statistically significant [ev_soil_organic_carbon_roose17_2].
water_harvesting_conservation__carbon_se.conditionality: The evidence pool here is limited to these two sources, so the class should be read as indicative rather than well established.

water_harvesting_conservation__carbon_se.mechanism: In low-income settings the pathway is zai pits building soil organic matter over time, with organic matter and nitrogen higher on fields treated for several years.
water_harvesting_conservation__carbon_se.conditionality: Both units are zai in Burkina Faso and measure soil organic matter, a proxy for carbon; one is a secondary citation of an earlier study and the other, a controlled trial, found no significant change in organic matter after two years.

water_harvesting_conservation__carbon_se.mechanism: A meta-analysis of over a thousand paired observations in China found straw mulching raised soil organic carbon by 10.74% to 22.63% depending on region [ev_soil_organic_carbon_zhang26h2_1], and terracing raised soil organic carbon by 60.96% and 14.11% in two regions after 11 to 20 years, and by 33.91% and 53.73% in two other regions after 21 to 30 years [ev_soil_organic_carbon_zhang26h2_10].
water_harvesting_conservation__carbon_se.conditionality: The gain is not universal: in Mexico, infiltration trenches were found to have actually decreased nitrogen and carbon content while increasing bulk density [ev_soil_organic_carbon_locat20_2]. Measured harm (maladaptation) — the practice worsening this outcome for some adopters — appears in 1 source.

water_harvesting_conservation__catchment.mechanism: Water harvesting raises catchment water yield mainly by recharging groundwater: in Maharashtra, India, a modelling study found rainwater-harvesting structures increased groundwater recharge by 16%, equivalent to about 2% of local annual rainfall [ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_glen12_4], and hydrological modelling of contour ridges in Morocco estimated a 50% increase in recharge [ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_willem21_1].
water_harvesting_conservation__catchment.conditionality: But the same capture that recharges groundwater can take water away from people downstream: a global river-basin model found rainwater harvesting raising crop production by 35% while reducing average annual river flows by 18%, with reductions of up to 80% in a single river basin [ev_water_yield_glen12_10]; and an Indian watershed study found runoff falling by about 60% while recharge rose by only 5% [ev_water_yield_glen12_2]. A separate theoretical study found the impact on watershed water levels may be minimal beyond the immediate vicinity of the structure [ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_glen12_8]. Measured harm (maladaptation) — the practice worsening this outcome for some adopters — appears in 6 sources. Within this family, spate and terracing systems point positive while cross-family, in-situ and runoff-catchment readings disagree internally, so the roll-up states conflicting evidence rather than the pooled positive.

water_harvesting_conservation__catchment.mechanism: In the Sahel, stone bunds, zaï and half-moons applied at watershed scale increase ground water level [ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_zoug14_1], and in Burkina Faso levels of water in wells have improved, which the source links not to higher rainfall but to SWC measures that control surface runoff and improve infiltration [ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_kabo04_1]. On China's Loess Plateau, a large campaign of check-dam construction carried out since the 1970s to retain floodwater and intercept soil sediments reduced streamflow by approximately 39% [ev_water_yield_luca21_1]. In Burkina Faso, cited studies show soil and water conservation techniques improving the availability of ground water in many villages, especially large rock bunds known as digues filtrantes [ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_sawa11h1_6].
water_harvesting_conservation__catchment.conditionality: Both sides are real findings in semi-arid land, and what separates them is the outcome measured, the place and the scale of the works. The gain is groundwater and well levels on and around treated Sahelian fields and watersheds [ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_zoug14_1, ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_kabo04_1]; the loss is streamflow below a campaign of check dams built at very large scale in China to retain floodwater [ev_water_yield_luca21_1]. For a downstream user the Chinese finding is the relevant one; for a farmer near the works the Sahelian one is. Neither side compares with and without the works at catchment scale: the Sahelian units are cited statements, the 39% is cited by a review from another study, and in Burkina Faso the number of wells with water year round has not increased significantly since SWC began [ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_kabo04_2]. A further Burkina Faso statement, cited from another study with no figures, also sits on the gain side [ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_sawa11h1_6].

water_harvesting_conservation__catchment.mechanism: Check dams and percolation tanks raise catchment water yield by detaining monsoon runoff so it infiltrates to the aquifer rather than running off downstream. In Rajasthan, India, check dams, measured against no-dam conditions (the runoff otherwise flowing on down the ephemeral stream), added recharge of 33 mm over their combined catchment in an average year and 17 mm in a year the authors called 'dry' [ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_dash17_1, ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_dash17_2]. In Andhra Pradesh, a small percolation tank — managed aquifer recharge (MAR) by an earth weir across an intermittent stream — sent 57 to 63 percent (average 61 percent) of its stored water to the hard-rock aquifer rather than losing it to evapotranspiration [ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_mass14_1], and tank percolation supplied 40 percent of the water pumped from nearby irrigation boreholes in both a rainfall-deficit year [ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_mass14_2] and a normal-rainfall year, when it reached seven additional boreholes [ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_mass14_3].
water_harvesting_conservation__catchment.conditionality: Both dam figures are measured recharge added by the structure, with no-dam conditions used only as the counterfactual, not an actually measured case; the authors put 'dry' in quotation marks, since mean rainfall was similar in both years and the real difference was rainfall intensity and dry-spell length rather than a named drought [ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_dash17_1, ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_dash17_2]. The percolation-tank figures come from one tank at one site; most of the percolated water is drawn back by boreholes close to the tank, so the recharge benefit is local, and the paper itself flags its percolation-efficiency estimate as in the high range of earlier regional estimates [ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_mass14_1]. The borehole-contribution shares rest on an electrical-conductivity mixing analysis built on stated assumptions about tank-water and aquifer-water conductivity [ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_mass14_2, ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_mass14_3]. All five units are irrigated cropping systems in India; the mechanism is not yet shown for rainfed systems.

water_harvesting_conservation__catchment.mechanism: In Niger, runoff-harvesting techniques were found to have raised the water level in village wells by about 14 metres between 1994 and 2004 [ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_botreij09_18]. In Burkina Faso's Mossi villages, water infiltrating through shallow, crusted soils treated with runoff-harvesting pits was observed feeding the water table in the wells of many villages [ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_roose17_1].
water_harvesting_conservation__catchment.conditionality: The size of the benefit is not well established: the Niger figure comes from villagers' own accounts rather than a controlled study, and the authors who reported it call for a proper study to confirm it.

water_harvesting_conservation__catchment.mechanism: In mixed crop–livestock settings the evidence is thin and points both ways. On the recharge side, recharge in Ethiopia's Mendae catchment rose from 8 mm before water-harvesting interventions to 107.7 mm after, by water balance (Negusse et al. 2013, cited in a review) [ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_gebr18_11], and Embrapa says its barraginhas in Brazil help recharge groundwater by raising the water table and revitalise springs and rivers [ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_mira19_6]. On the other side, studies cited in the same review (Garg et al. 2012; Gates et al. 2011) found water outflows from treated catchments halved against untreated ones, a potential loss for downstream users [ev_water_yield_gebr18_9].
water_harvesting_conservation__catchment.conditionality: What separates the sides is where the water is measured: the gains are recharge within the treated catchment, the loss is outflow leaving it, so both can hold at once and the row cannot say whether downstream users gain or lose. Every unit is a second-hand citation or an agency's self-assessment of its own technology [ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_gebr18_11, ev_water_yield_gebr18_9, ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_mira19_6].

water_harvesting_conservation__catchment.mechanism: Capturing runoff upstream moves water from the stream into the ground. On the recharge side, works that hold water on the land let it infiltrate and raise local water tables: in Maharashtra a groundwater model of 16 observation wells found an overall increase in recharge from rainwater harvesting of 16% (Gore et al., 1998, cited by Glendenning et al.), well measurements near structures put recharge at about 3–8% of rainfall (Badiger et al., 2002), and in Ethiopia's Mendae catchment a water balance gave groundwater recharge of 107.7 mm after water harvesting against 8 mm before (Negusse et al., 2013, cited by Gebremeskel et al.) [ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_glen12_4, ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_glen12_1, ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_gebr18_11]. Terraces in the Mandara mountains are reported to recharge the water table by 15 to 25% of rainfall (Hiol Hiol and Mietton, cited by Roose), modelling of contour ridges in Morocco estimates a 50% rise in recharge (cited by Willems et al.), and check dams and other structures in Saurashtra were estimated to add 480 million cubic meters of recharge per annum (Jain, 2012, cited by Verma and Shah) [ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_roose06_1, ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_willem21_1, ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_verm19_1]. In Rajasthan piezometers recorded groundwater rising in 16 of 21 non-desert districts by an average of 1.42 meters, and after tank desilting in Telangana a state survey found levels up in 22 of the 31 districts [ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_verm19_3, ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_verm19_2]; a water budget for Uttarakhand's watershed project put aquifer recharge 3.3 percent above baseline [ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_utk22_5]. Rising well levels are also reported around stone bunds, zaï and half-moons in Burkina Faso, earth and stone bunds in Mauritania, spate and conservation structures in Yemen, filled check dams (Frankl et al., 2016; Lucas-Borja et al., 2018), sand dams (Hut et al., 2008), and Ethiopian public-works watersheds where a better water table allowed small-scale irrigation [ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_kabo04_1, ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_zoug14_1, ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_sawa11h1_6, ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_mrt14_1, ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_yem12_1, ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_yem12_2, ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_fran21_1, ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_biaz12_27, ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_eth16_7], and a Burkina Faso farm-pond study treats seepage from the reservoir as recharge rather than lost water [ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_foxr03_8]. On the outflow side, the same capture reduces the water that leaves the catchment: a GIS and water-balance study estimated that watershed development including more rainwater harvesting would cut runoff by approximately 60% while raising recharge by only 5% (Sharma and Thakur, 2007), a global model suggested rainwater harvesting would reduce annual river flows by 18% on average and by up to 80% in a single basin (Wisser et al., 2010), and in Andhra Pradesh it was suggested to cause basin closure (Calder et al., 2008), all cited by Glendenning et al. [ev_water_yield_glen12_2, ev_water_yield_glen12_10, ev_water_yield_glen12_5]. Outflows from treated catchments have been found halved compared with untreated ones (Garg et al., 2012; Gates et al., 2011, cited by Gebremeskel et al.), reviews cite decreased runoff generation harming downstream systems, a Rajasthan model found rainwater harvesting reducing streamflow, and in Morocco mechanised bunds considerably reduce the water collected in downstream hill reservoirs (Albergel et al., 2004, cited by Roose et al.) [ev_water_yield_gebr18_9, ev_water_yield_dile13_9, ev_water_yield_glen12_7, ev_water_yield_roos10_1].
water_harvesting_conservation__catchment.conditionality: Studies disagree on the direction because they measure different water. The recharge side counts water entering the ground near the works; the outflow side counts water leaving the catchment for downstream users, and the same capture can raise the first while lowering the second, as in the watershed where runoff fell by about 60% and recharge rose by only 5%, with most of the change going to evapotranspiration [ev_water_yield_glen12_2]. Scale and intensity separate them too: several studies find limited or no downstream impact from small-scale water storage even when implemented widely (Evenari et al., 1971; Schreider et al., 2002; Sreedevi et al., 2006; De Winnaar and Jewitt, 2010; Andersson et al., 2011) [ev_water_yield_rock10_1, ev_water_yield_dile13_10], a theoretical model found the effect on water levels minimal beyond the immediate vicinity of a structure (Neumann et al., 2004) [ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_glen12_8], while the large flow reductions come from intensive watershed development, basin-wide models and mechanised bunds. Siltation of the structures can also reverse basin closure by letting downstream flows rise again [ev_water_yield_glen12_5]. The recharge gains are not secure: in Burkina Faso a reconnaissance of 59 villages found that the number of wells with water year-round had not increased significantly since soil and water conservation began [ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_kabo04_2]; in India the survey data showed more recharge in treated areas but had no untreated sites, and tube-well pumping encouraged by subsidised electricity has possibly wiped out the gains [ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_iegind11_3, ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_iegind11_4]. Most units on both sides are second-hand citations, models or self-reported project results (the Uttarakhand, Mauritania and Yemen figures come from World Bank completion reports), and few measure both recharge and downstream flow in the same catchment. This row is for downstream users and basin planners; spring and stream discharge gains near treated watersheds are local supply and are reported in the water stress rows, not here.

water_harvesting_conservation__catchment.mechanism: Upstream capture can both add to and take from downstream water. On China's Loess Plateau, a large campaign of check-dam construction carried out since the 1970s to retain floodwater and intercept soil sediments reduced streamflow by approximately 39% [ev_water_yield_luca21_1]. On the other side, Embrapa says its barraginhas in Brazil help recharge groundwater by raising the water table and revitalise springs and rivers [ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_mira19_6], and in the Peruvian Andes a few studies have observed catchment-level changes such as reduced quick runoff or increased aquifer recharge, which the source calls plausible but not generalisable [ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_locat20_1].
water_harvesting_conservation__catchment.conditionality: This row is for downstream users and basin planners: it asks what capturing water upstream does to the water that reaches streams and reservoirs below, not whether the farm that captures it has more. The sides now conflict, and what separates them is what is measured and at what scale: the loss is streamflow below a check-dam campaign at very large scale built to retain floodwater [ev_water_yield_luca21_1], while the gains are recharge and water-table statements for small dispersed basins and trenches [ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_mira19_6, ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_locat20_1]. In the Peruvian Andes trenches had little effect on increasing baseflow, with hydrogeological characteristics key to explaining their impact [ev_water_regulation_locat20_1]. None of this is a measured project comparison: the 39% is a secondary citation in a global review, the Peruvian statements are a review's summary, and the barraginha statement is Embrapa's self-assessment of its own technology [ev_water_yield_luca21_1, ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_locat20_1, ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_mira19_6].

water_harvesting_conservation__cost_per_.mechanism: In a Kenyan catchment, low-cost water measures built around sand dams are estimated to have given more than 100,000 people better access to water within 10 years at an investment of about 35 USD per capita [ev_project_cost_lasage08_1]. A separate account of sand dams in Kenya's Kitui District gives a similar material cost: about US$8,000 per dam on average, an investment of US$35 to 50 per person served [ev_project_cost_pauw08_1].
water_harvesting_conservation__cost_per_.conditionality: This is a single estimate from a single study, with no stated currency year, expressed per person gaining water access rather than per farmer or household, so it covers the water-access benefit only [ev_project_cost_lasage08_1]. The Kitui figure is the implementing NGO's own programme cost, reported by the organisation rather than independently audited, and the community's own labour and the local stone, sand and water it contributes are not costed [ev_project_cost_pauw08_1]. The two sand-dam cost estimates, from different Kenyan districts and different sources, agree closely on the per-capita order of magnitude.

water_harvesting_conservation__cost_per_.mechanism: The pooled costs are up-front establishment or treatment costs per hectare. In Ethiopia, the initial investment in terracing was equivalent to US$ 46.51 per hectare in the first year of construction, with about US$ 48.8 per hectare needed to maintain it over the first three years [ev_project_cost_adgo13_8]. Indian watershed projects treated sub-watersheds at US$261 and US$217 per hectare [ev_project_cost_iegind11_10, ev_project_cost_iegind11_11], and spate systems in Yemen averaged USD 800-1200 per hectare to build, of which farmers paid 15-20% [ev_project_cost_yem12_8]. WOCAT compilers report establishment costs per hectare of 147.30 USD for gully works in Somalia, 345 and 1293 USD for technologies in Jordan and 2000 USD in Uzbekistan [ev_project_cost_wocat_7778_2026_establishment, ev_project_cost_wocat_5860_2021_establishment, ev_project_cost_wocat_5770_2020_establishment, ev_project_cost_wocat_7553_2025_establishment]. At the high end, rehabilitating pre-Columbian andenes in Peru cost USD 2,200 per hectare, and a review tabulates terracing costs in China of 1918 to 4045 USD per hectare, rising with the original slope from 5 to 25 degrees [ev_project_cost_fao13c_1, ev_project_cost_wei16_1]. At the low end, mechanised Vallerani micro-catchment bunds in Jordan's Badia cost an average of 20-30 US dollars per hectare to build, about 3 hectares per hour [ev_project_cost_tats21_3].
water_harvesting_conservation__cost_per_.conditionality: The small cost class reflects the lower figures from Ethiopia, India, Yemen and Somalia; the Peru and China costs come from upper-middle-income settings, and the Jordan, Uzbekistan, Peru and China figures sit well above the rest [ev_project_cost_wocat_5770_2020_establishment, ev_project_cost_wocat_7553_2025_establishment, ev_project_cost_fao13c_1, ev_project_cost_wei16_1]. These are establishment costs, not costs per hectare restored, and the spread is wide because the technologies differ from hand-built terraces to engineered spate systems; the Ethiopian terracing figure is for terraces built with unpaid community labour decades ago [ev_project_cost_adgo13_8]. WOCAT figures are the compiler's own cost tables converted to USD with the sheet's exchange rate, not market prices. The India costs are described by the evaluator as high by national norms, the Peru figure is a 1994 assessment cited secondhand, and the Chinese terracing costs are a secondary table showing that steeper land costs more to terrace [ev_project_cost_iegind11_10, ev_project_cost_fao13c_1, ev_project_cost_wei16_1]. The Jordanian figure is cited second-hand from two other studies and covers only the mechanised bund construction, not the seedlings, planting or fencing established alongside it [ev_project_cost_tats21_3].

water_harvesting_conservation__cost_per_.mechanism: In low- and lower-middle-income settings the pooled per-hectare costs are up-front establishment and treatment costs. An independent evaluation of two World Bank-supported India watershed projects reports treatment unit costs of US$261 per hectare in the Integrated Watershed Development Project and US$217/ha in the Karnataka project [ev_project_cost_iegind11_10, ev_project_cost_iegind11_11]. A Yemen completion report gives average investment costs for spate systems of USD 800- 1200/ha, of which the farmer's 15-20% share comes to US$ 150-200/ha [ev_project_cost_yem12_8]. Two WOCAT technology sheets add compiler-reported establishment costs: 2000.00 USD per hectare for orchard terraces in Uzbekistan, a total spread over 1.6 ha [ev_project_cost_wocat_7553_2025_establishment], and 147.30 USD per hectare for gabion and rock check-dam gully control in Somalia, a total spread over 160 ha [ev_project_cost_wocat_7778_2026_establishment].
water_harvesting_conservation__cost_per_.conditionality: The figures measure different things: watershed treatment cost per hectare treated in India, spate-system investment in Yemen, and WOCAT compilers' own cost tables converted with each sheet's exchange rate, which are not market prices; none is a cost per hectare of degraded land restored, and no price-year adjustment is made across them. The India evaluator calls the US$261 per hectare cost high by Indian standards, and the US$217/ha cost below the central government norm [ev_project_cost_iegind11_10, ev_project_cost_iegind11_11]; the Yemen report calls the farmer contribution comparatively high [ev_project_cost_yem12_8]. The Somali figure spreads a whole gully-control package over the treated area, which keeps it low per hectare, while the Uzbek terrace figure is a small orchard plot, so the spread from 147.30 to 2000.00 USD per hectare reflects practice and denominator as much as cost. All four countries are in the low- or lower-middle-income target band.

water_harvesting_conservation__cost_per_.mechanism: In upper-middle-income settings the pooled per-hectare costs are a 1994 rehabilitation cost for Andean terraces in Peru from an FAO manual and Jordanian WOCAT sheets for a floodplain marab system costed over its ten hectares and mechanised Vallerani micro-catchment trenching costed per hectare [ev_project_cost_fao13c_1, ev_project_cost_wocat_5770_2020_establishment, ev_project_cost_wocat_5860_2021_establishment]. A review adds terracing costs from China of 1918 to 4045 USD per hectare, rising with the original slope from 5 to 25 degrees [ev_project_cost_wei16_1]. Mechanised Vallerani micro-catchment bunds in the same income band cost an average of 20-30 US dollars per hectare to build [ev_project_cost_tats21_3].
water_harvesting_conservation__cost_per_.conditionality: The Peruvian figure is a nominal 1994 cost for rehabilitating existing terraces rather than building new ones, and the Jordanian figures are the compilers' own cost tables converted at the sheets' stated rates, not market prices; all three sit outside the low- and lower-middle-income target band [ev_project_cost_fao13c_1, ev_project_cost_wocat_5770_2020_establishment, ev_project_cost_wocat_5860_2021_establishment]. The Chinese figures are a secondary table and include socioeconomic costs alongside machinery and labour [ev_project_cost_wei16_1]. That figure is cited second-hand and covers bund construction only, not the seedlings or fencing established with it [ev_project_cost_tats21_3].

water_harvesting_conservation__cost_redu.mechanism: Water harvesting changes farm and programme costs in both directions. Practices that remove a step save money: in Mozambique labour costs were $153 per hectare for basins against $173 for conventional tillage, and in Ethiopia mulching reduced weed density and labour costs for weeding [ev_project_cost_kida19_5, ev_project_cost_sime15h2_1]. Better siting saves on construction: in Karnataka, land-resource-inventory planning avoided unnecessary structures, so works cost INR 14,228 per hectare against INR 18,739 under the conventional programme, a drop of 30 percent [ev_project_cost_kar20_5]. Practices that add earthworks raise costs: switching from flat-land production to tied ridges, with or without grass strips, increased the cost of production in Ghana's Nandom area [ev_project_cost_dalt14_2]. In Ghana, the share of small dams rehabilitated for less than USD 5,000 per irrigated hectare was 25% under government and 12% under development partners [ev_project_cost_veno12_1].
water_harvesting_conservation__cost_redu.conditionality: Studies disagree because they cost different practices. The savings come where the practice removes a step, such as tillage or hand weeding, or where planning avoids building structures; the increase comes where the practice adds ridging [ev_project_cost_kida19_5, ev_project_cost_sime15h2_1, ev_project_cost_kar20_5, ev_project_cost_dalt14_2]. The Karnataka saving is against another conservation programme, not against doing nothing, and comes from a World Bank completion report [ev_project_cost_kar20_5]; the Ghana dam figures describe a spread of rehabilitation costs between implementers rather than a saving or an overrun [ev_project_cost_veno12_1]; the Mozambique basins also carry residue retention and herbicide weed control, and the Ethiopian statement gives no figure [ev_project_cost_kida19_5, ev_project_cost_sime15h2_1]. Cost evidence is ordinal here: read the row as which practices tend to cut or add costs, not as a price.

water_harvesting_conservation__cost_redu.mechanism: In-field water-harvesting practices both cut and raise the cost of production, depending on what they replace. Basins in Mozambique cost $153 per hectare in labour against $173 for conventional tillage [ev_project_cost_kida19_5]. Switching from flat-land production to tied ridges, with or without grass strips, raised the cost of production at Nandom in Ghana [ev_project_cost_dalt14_2].
water_harvesting_conservation__cost_redu.conditionality: What separates the two is whether the practice replaces tillage work or adds construction on top of it [ev_project_cost_kida19_5, ev_project_cost_dalt14_2]. The Mozambique basins bundle basin digging with residue retention and herbicide weed control, and the Ghana cost rise is stated without a figure [ev_project_cost_kida19_5, ev_project_cost_dalt14_2]. The row rests on two units from two sources; more costed comparisons for rainfed cropping are missing.

water_harvesting_conservation__cost_redu.mechanism: Studies disagree on whether the practices lower or raise what farmers and projects pay. On the saving side: in Karnataka, planning structures from a land-resource inventory cut construction cost to INR 14,228 per hectare against INR 18,739 under the comparison programme, a drop of 30 percent [ev_project_cost_kar20_5]; in Mozambique, labour for the basin practice averaged $153 against $173 per hectare under conventional tillage [ev_project_cost_kida19_5]; and in Ethiopia mulching reduced labour costs for weeding [ev_project_cost_sime15h2_1]. On the cost side: in Ghanaian trials, switching from flat-land production to tied ridges with or without grass strips increased the cost of production [ev_project_cost_dalt14_2]; and in Ghana most rehabilitated small dams cost USD 5,000 or more per irrigated hectare, with only 25% of government and 12% of donor-rehabilitated dams below that [ev_project_cost_veno12_1].
water_harvesting_conservation__cost_redu.conditionality: What separates the sides is whether the practice removes work or adds a structure. The savings come from basins that replace conventional tillage, mulch that suppresses weeds and better siting of structures, which save labour or construction cost [ev_project_cost_kida19_5, ev_project_cost_sime15h2_1, ev_project_cost_kar20_5]; the cost increases come from building ridges or rehabilitating dams [ev_project_cost_dalt14_2, ev_project_cost_veno12_1]. The Mozambique saving is bundled with reduced tillage, residue retention and herbicide weed control, so it is not a pure capture effect [ev_project_cost_kida19_5]. The Karnataka saving is a planning-efficiency comparison between programmes rather than a with-and-without contrast, and the Ghana dam costs are thresholds from a review rather than a comparison with an alternative [ev_project_cost_kar20_5, ev_project_cost_veno12_1]. For scoping, expect labour savings from in-field moisture practices and added establishment costs for built structures.

water_harvesting_conservation__drought__.mechanism: Water harvesting structures capture and store rainfall runoff so crops have water to draw on between rains. A meta-analysis of water-harvesting technologies across semi-arid Africa and Asia found yield improvements significantly higher in years when rainfall was below 330 mm than in years above that threshold [ev_crop_yield_boum16_4]. In Cambodia, a farm pond was reported to provide enough water even during drought [ev_drought_hazard_wocat_2844_2017_drought_impacts], and in Burkina Faso a project recorded that during years of extreme drought, plants reduced their growth but most survived on the stored soil water [ev_drought_hazard_wocat_1528_2012_drought_impacts].
water_harvesting_conservation__drought__.conditionality: This benefit does not hold once drought turns severe: a review of dryland water-management strategies notes that crop yields cannot be sustained during a true meteorological drought the way ordinary dry spells can be bridged, and different coping mechanisms are needed [ev_crop_yield_rock10_2]. Measured harm (maladaptation) — the practice worsening this outcome for some adopters — appears in 1 source, and part of the benefit happens off-site (downstream or landscape scale) rather than on the adopting farm.

water_harvesting_conservation__drought_h.mechanism: In semi-arid Brazil, water from runoff-harvesting ponds applied as supplemental irrigation during in-season dry spells has reduced crop-loss risk in years of irregular rainfall, and water stored in production cisterns can reduce livestock mortality in severe droughts [ev_drought_hazard_brito07_10, ev_drought_hazard_castro22_2]. water_harvesting_conservation__drought_h.conditionality: Against this, subsurface dams tended to dry out in a rainless year and small ones do not withstand long dry spells; these units record no benefit when storage is exhausted, a shortfall rather than damage [ev_drought_hazard_cirilo03_2, ev_drought_hazard_cirilo03_3]. water_harvesting_conservation__drought_h.conditionality: The measured effect is on satellite greenness and productivity indices over whole watersheds, not on yields or household outcomes, and comes from a programme bundling water harvesting with other land-management works, so its share is not isolated and the strength is not stated as a size for the practice [ev_drought_hazard_cons22_1]. At the mild end the buffering thins: the EVI model still detects a small significant effect but the GOSIF-GPP model shows none [ev_drought_hazard_cons22_3, ev_drought_hazard_cons22_4]. The Rift Valley finding is a field observation of which plots wilted during mild dry spells, not a tested yield contrast [ev_drought_hazard_sime15h2_1]. The barraginha statement is Embrapa's self-assessment of its own technology, with no normal-year reference, from a Brazilian setting rather than the East African zones this row covers [ev_drought_hazard_mira19_8].

water_harvesting_conservation__drought_h.mechanism: Zai pits in Burkina Faso reduce the impact of dry spells of a few weeks when soil water storage is sufficient, cisterns in China are reported to mitigate frequent droughts, and public-works watershed interventions in Ethiopia improved drought resilience by raising water availability. WOCAT compilers for Vallerani micro-catchments, ponds, check dams, terraces, stone lines and water-spreading weirs judge drought impacts reduced through stored water, infiltration and soil moisture retention, and households in a Rwandan land husbandry and water harvesting project proved more resilient than controls to the 2016 drought and recovered faster.
water_harvesting_conservation__drought_h.conditionality: Most units are practitioner judgements or assertions without a drought metric, including a lender evaluation in China with no measurement; the Rwanda comparison against controls is reported second-hand in a completion report. In Ethiopia vegetation greenness still followed local drought severity, and the Haiti compiler notes the impact has not yet been measured. In Tunisia, consecutive drought years limited soil-conservation benefits, a unit recording no benefit rather than damage [ev_drought_hazard_iegtun13_1].

water_harvesting_conservation__drought_h.mechanism: In Brazil's semi-arid interior, a review notes that water stored in cisterns can help reduce animal mortality even in the most severe droughts [ev_drought_hazard_castro22_2]. In the Peruvian Andes, terraced maize plots fared better than sloped fields during a 2002 dry spell, reducing the risk of crop failure from drought [ev_drought_hazard_post05_1].
water_harvesting_conservation__drought_h.conditionality: The benefit still has a ceiling: in Brazil's semi-arid interior, underground dams were observed drying up entirely during a rainless year, showing storage can be exhausted once drought turns severe enough [ev_drought_hazard_cirilo03_2].

water_harvesting_conservation__establish.mechanism: Pooled costs are up-front construction costs per structure: village ponds or tanks and dry-stone check dams (the latter per cubic metre of masonry) from a World Bank watershed project in Himachal Pradesh, India, and compiler-reported WOCAT establishment costs for a farm pond with irrigation system in Cambodia, a set of check dams and walls in India, a 200 m vetiver line in Haiti, a fascine line in Madagascar and a haffir in Somalia. In Ethiopia, cited second-hand, sand dam construction costs about 12,000 US dollars per dam [ev_project_cost_lasa13_6].
water_harvesting_conservation__establish.conditionality: The WOCAT figures are each compiler's own cost table summed and converted with the sheet's exchange rate, and the India project figures are self-reported from project monitoring in rupees converted at one rate; none are market prices. A structure means very different things across the pool, from a fascine line of a few metres to a haffir of about 5100 square metres, and the per-cubic-metre check-dam figure is per volume of masonry, so the pooled cost class is a loose summary rather than a comparable unit cost. The Ethiopian sand-dam figure is a second-hand citation with no stated currency year, and a dam-based unit cost is not directly comparable to the pooled pond, check-dam and line-structure figures already in this row [ev_project_cost_lasa13_6].

water_harvesting_conservation__fire__all.mechanism: The only unit argues that terraces limit fire by removing fuel: on intensively tended terraces all crop residues are grazed off as soon as harvests end, so bush fires have little to spread on [ev_fire_hazard_roose06_1].
water_harvesting_conservation__fire__all.conditionality: Data deficient: the row rests on a single expert estimate whose authors say there is no experimental work on terraces behind it [ev_fire_hazard_roose06_1]. What is missing is a second independent source or any measured fire outcome (burnt area, fire frequency or spread) on treated against untreated land. The argued effect depends on grazing keeping biomass down rather than on the structures themselves, so it says nothing about practices without that management.

water_harvesting_conservation__flood__al.mechanism: Water-harvesting and soil-conservation works slow runoff and spread it before it gathers into floods, giving a moderate reduction in flood impact. In Tunisia, a catchment treated with contour stone walls, terraces and gully structures saw the volume and peaks of average and larger floods fall by about 50% [ev_flood_hazard_bergaoui00_1], with peaks strongly cut and flood times lengthened [ev_flood_hazard_bergaoui00_2, ev_flood_hazard_bergaoui00_3]. A review of infiltration trenches in mountain areas found they cut runoff by 46.4% on average [ev_runoff_reduction_locat20_1]. Stone bunds lower peak runoff at the foot of the slope in Burkina Faso [ev_flood_hazard_roose94_1], and terraces on small mountain plots cut runoff and flood peaks [ev_flood_hazard_roose06_1]. Check dams cut flooding and peak flow in Iran and held up against strong floods in Italy [ev_flood_hazard_luca21_1, ev_flood_hazard_luca21_2], and small dams in Morocco damped the damage of serious floods in 2002-2003 [ev_flood_hazard_roos10_1]. Treated ravines in Haiti slowed cyclone floods [ev_flood_hazard_roose17_2], and in India compacted hill terraces limited damage from a major flood and landslides [ev_flood_hazard_utk22_7]. Users of small reservoirs in Ghana name flood control as a benefit [ev_flood_hazard_veno12_1], and practitioner ratings from Burkina Faso, Kenya, Tunisia, Ethiopia, Uzbekistan and Somalia also report less flooding [ev_flood_hazard_wocat_1528_2012_flood_impacts, ev_flood_hazard_wocat_1537_2012_flood_impacts, ev_flood_hazard_wocat_6610_2022_downstream_flooding, ev_flood_hazard_wocat_6715_2023_downstream_flooding, ev_flood_hazard_wocat_6716_2023_flood_impacts, ev_flood_hazard_wocat_7553_2025_flood_impacts, ev_flood_hazard_wocat_7778_2026_flood_impacts].
water_harvesting_conservation__flood__al.conditionality: Some structures make flooding worse. In Niger, diversion banquettes visibly increased peak flows downstream [ev_flood_hazard_heusch95_1]; a review warns that larger sand dams raise the risk of flooding, erosion and seepage [ev_flood_hazard_ritc21_1]; and an expert synthesis warns of serious gullying and larger peak flows when diversion dikes break, about once in 4 to 10 years [ev_flood_hazard_roose94_3]. Strong floods are where the benefit fades: check dams had little effect against extreme floods, especially when badly designed or not maintained [ev_flood_hazard_luca21_3]; in Tunisia the volume of large and average floods did not change significantly, only their timing [ev_runoff_reduction_bergaoui00_4, ev_runoff_reduction_bergaoui00_7]; and in Morocco the flood-peak cut held only where floods were not too strong [ev_flood_hazard_roose17_3]. Most of the support is expert statements, second-hand findings and practitioner ratings; the Tunisian catchment is the main measured result. The sub-practices differ: in-field structures do best, runoff-catchment and floodwater-spreading systems are moderate, and terracing evidence conflicts. water_harvesting_conservation__flood__al.mechanism: Among high-income contexts the flood evidence is small but points the same way. In Germany, small dry detention ponds built into field borders stored storm runoff behind a raised earth embankment and lowered peak runoff leaving the field by a factor of three [ev_flood_hazard_fien05_1]. A global review of check-dam literature reports that artificial sequences of check dams in the northern Italian Alps withstood flood events with return periods of about 7 to 25 years without failing [ev_flood_hazard_luca21_2].
water_harvesting_conservation__flood__al.conditionality: Both units describe structures coping with floods they were tested against, not a measured percentage reduction, and both are temperate, high-income settings (Germany, Italy) rather than the LIC/LMIC target; the German pond's own authors say its effect is untested beyond the flood sizes observed during the monitoring period and expect it to work less well in larger events [ev_flood_hazard_fien05_1].

A global review of check-dam literature reports that artificial sequences of check dams in the northern Italian Alps withstood flood events with return periods of about 7 to 25 years without failing [ev_flood_hazard_luca21_2].
water_harvesting_conservation__flood_haz.conditionality: Both units describe structures coping with floods they were tested against, not a measured percentage reduction, and both are temperate, high-income settings (Germany, Italy) rather than the LIC/LMIC target; the German pond's own authors say its effect is untested beyond the flood sizes observed during the monitoring period and expect it to work less well in larger events [ev_flood_hazard_fien05_1].

water_harvesting_conservation__flood_haz.mechanism: Structures that hold runoff on the slope or in the channel lower flood peaks: a check-dam review cites check dams in Iran mitigating flooding and significantly reducing peak flow, a review of Andean terraces reports that hydrological modelling and field measurements indicate a reduction in peak flow, and Embrapa describes its barraginhas, small runoff-retention basins dug along runoff paths in Brazil, as mitigating floods while recharging groundwater by infiltration [ev_flood_hazard_luca21_1, ev_flood_hazard_willem21_1, ev_flood_hazard_mira19_7].
water_harvesting_conservation__flood_haz.conditionality: None of the units says how large the reduction is, so the strength is not quantified. The terrace review itself calls the impact on peak flow uncertain given the scarcity of catchment-level studies, the Iranian result is a secondary citation in a review, and the barraginha statement is Embrapa's self-assessment of its own technology; all are catchment or downstream effects rather than flood losses avoided on the adopting farm, and the row covers upper-middle-income settings only [ev_flood_hazard_willem21_1, ev_flood_hazard_luca21_1, ev_flood_hazard_mira19_7].

water_harvesting_conservation__food_inse.mechanism: Water harvesting and soil and water conservation reduce food insecurity mainly by raising and steadying harvests and by putting stored water on gardens. In the Brazilian semi-arid, subsurface dams gave families more fruit and vegetables and, by most interviewees' account, more food overall, and production cisterns allow daily irrigation of gardens in households that had not grown or eaten vegetables before [ev_food_security_cirilo03_6, ev_food_security_arsky20_6]; in Burkina Faso, runoff cisterns irrigate small gardens and water livestock, improving food security in the lean season [ev_food_security_roose94_1]. In the field, planting basins (zai pits) raised the odds of a Kenyan plot meeting the household maize requirement to 421.75 against 1.67 in the control, and ground cover raised those odds in Malawi's El Nino season [ev_food_security_boil19_2, ev_food_security_boil19_1]. Household food security rises in proportion to the area of a farm improved with bunds, and beneficiaries of Rwanda's terracing project showed drastically improved food consumption scores against a comparison group [ev_food_security_zoug14_1, ev_food_security_rwa18_5]. WOCAT compilers rate food self-sufficiency as improved and the risk of production failure as lowered, and say why: enough stored water to irrigate during drought in Cambodia, better soil moisture in Ethiopia, more cultivable land and crop diversity in Bhutan, more productive fodder and crops in Burkina Faso, and rehabilitated gullies and farmland in Somalia [ev_food_security_wocat_2844_2017_risk_of_production_failure, ev_food_security_wocat_6715_2023_risk_of_production_failure, ev_food_security_wocat_6891_2023_food_security_selfsufficiency, ev_food_security_wocat_6891_2023_risk_of_production_failure, ev_food_security_wocat_1528_2012_food_security_selfsufficiency, ev_food_security_wocat_1528_2012_risk_of_production_failure, ev_food_security_wocat_7778_2026_food_security_selfsufficiency]. In Ethiopia's Anjene catchment, farmers recalled that before terracing the community was highly food insecure and migrated in search of food even in minor droughts, and that terraces improved crop production and reduced seasonal migration [ev_food_security_adgo13_11]. Ethiopian farmers who adopted rainwater-harvesting irrigation properly improved their dietary status (Desta 2004, cited in a review) [ev_food_security_biaz12_26]. A landscape review of in-situ rainwater harvesting across African drylands rates food security — yields in bad years and the bridging of dry spells — as a benefit with a 'Good' evidence basis [ev_food_security_vohl09_4]. A CILSS regional synthesis adds a further perception survey: in 2005-2006 surveys in Niger, 70 percent of people in villages with natural-resource-management investment reported an improvement in food security, against only 1 percent in control villages [ev_food_security_botreij09_20].
water_harvesting_conservation__food_inse.conditionality: The gains depend on the rainfall year, on where the works are built and on practice choice. In Niger, farm families with soil and water conservation produced an estimated surplus of 70 percent in good rainfall years but a deficit of 28 percent in low-rainfall years [ev_food_security_kabo04_1]; in Malawi's El Nino season, banking lowered the odds of meeting the maize requirement from 0.19 to 0.054 [ev_food_security_boil19_3]. Independent evaluations of Ethiopian programmes found communal, mostly off-farm watershed works did not raise food security, possibly because the programmes were short [ev_food_security_abate21_4, ev_food_security_arega24_1], and compilers record no change for vetiver terraces in Haiti, where land users must wait for degraded soil to recover [ev_food_security_wocat_3223_2017_food_security_selfsufficiency]. Much of the literature is cited second-hand or qualitative, and the Brazilian findings include Embrapa's assessment of its own technology and programme reviews [ev_food_security_mira19_2, ev_food_security_castro22_3]. The class is moderate because the sub-practices differ, from slight for cross-family evidence to strong for in-field practices. A gain in a good season does not by itself show the practice protects food supply through drought. The Anjene account rests on farmer recall and group discussions, and the dietary finding is second-hand with no magnitude [ev_food_security_adgo13_11, ev_food_security_biaz12_26]. That rating is the review's own qualitative evaluation across several cited sources, not a single measured contrast [ev_food_security_vohl09_4]. The same synthesis also records a null result: in Burkina Faso's bad 2007 harvest, households in heavily treated villages still bought cereal at the market, 26 kilograms per person on average against 38 kilograms in lightly treated villages, a gap the authors read as the yield advantage not translating into greater food security that year [ev_food_security_botreij09_21].

water_harvesting_conservation__food_inse.mechanism: Harvested water and held soil moisture raise harvests and diversify diets: in semi-arid Kenya planting basins (zai pits) raised the odds of a plot meeting the household maize requirement to 421.75 against 1.67 in the control, bunds improve household food security in proportion to the farm area they cover, and Burkina Faso farms applying manure or soil and water conservation techniques on over half their plots are cited as more food secure [ev_food_security_boil19_2, ev_food_security_zoug14_1, ev_food_security_sawa11h1_5]. In semi-arid Brazil stored production water allows daily irrigation of vegetable gardens and fruit trees for families who previously did not grow or eat vegetables, subsurface dams gave families more access to fruit and vegetables and more food overall, reviews of production-cistern experiments stress their importance for food security, and a systematic review cites significant improvements in food security indicators among adopters of rainwater-harvesting ponds in Burkina Faso [ev_food_security_arsky20_6, ev_food_security_cirilo03_6, ev_food_security_castro22_3, ev_food_security_silv26_1].
water_harvesting_conservation__food_inse.conditionality: The gain depends on rain: Niger farm families with soil and water conservation produced an estimated surplus of 70 percent in years of good rainfall but still had an estimated deficit of 28 percent in low-rainfall years, so the practice does not secure food in dry years [ev_food_security_kabo04_1]. The only sized result is the Kenyan odds ratio, which has a wide confidence interval and comes from an above-average rainfall season [ev_food_security_boil19_2]. The Brazilian units are implementer perceptions, a seven-family interview study and a review of experiments run by the technology's developer, the Burkina Faso farm statement bundles manure with the conservation works, and the systematic review's citation is contradicted by its own table [ev_food_security_arsky20_6, ev_food_security_cirilo03_6, ev_food_security_castro22_3, ev_food_security_sawa11h1_5, ev_food_security_silv26_1].

water_harvesting_conservation__food_inse.mechanism: In rainfed cropping, in-field water capture and higher yields reduce food insecurity by helping plots meet household staple needs. In Malawi's El Nino season, adding ground cover raised the odds of a plot meeting the household maize requirement from 0.12 to 0.475 [ev_food_security_boil19_1, ev_food_security_boil19_3].
