In Burkina Faso, higher yields are cited as improving household food security, especially on farms that apply manure or some kind of soil and water conservation on over half of their plots [ev_food_security_sawa11h1_5].
water_harvesting_conservation__food_inse.conditionality: The strong class rests on a single odds-ratio study, and the same study shows practice choice can reverse the result: in that El Nino season banking reduced the odds of meeting the maize requirement to 0.054 against 0.19 in the control [ev_food_security_boil19_3]. The Burkina Faso statement is cited second-hand and does not separate manure from soil and water conservation [ev_food_security_sawa11h1_5]. The evidence is thin and both studies are from semi-arid African settings, so the size of the effect elsewhere in rainfed cropping is uncertain.

water_harvesting_conservation__food_inse.mechanism: Works that raise and steady crop output reduce the times a household runs short of food. In Ethiopia's Anjene catchment, which two decades earlier was highly eroded and highly food insecure, with people migrating in search of food in times of even minor droughts, the introduction of fanya juu terraces improved crop production and so reduced seasonal migration of farmers [ev_food_security_adgo13_11]. In Brazil, adopters of Embrapa's barraginhas, small semicircular runoff-retention basins, identified food security as the technology's greatest impact, because it guarantees quantity, quality and diversity of food [ev_food_security_mira19_2].
water_harvesting_conservation__food_inse.conditionality: Both units say food security improved but neither says by how much: the Ethiopian finding rests on farmer recall and group discussions about the period before and after terracing, and the terraces were maintained for decades with community labour alongside fertiliser use on cereals [ev_food_security_adgo13_11]. The Brazilian finding is an adopter rating in Embrapa's own impact assessment of its technology, not a measured food-security indicator [ev_food_security_mira19_2]. A measured household food-security comparison with untreated farms is needed to state a size.

water_harvesting_conservation__food_inse.mechanism: In upper-middle-income semi-arid Brazil, stored water lets families grow food close to home: once production water is stored it allows daily irrigation of gardens, beds and fruit trees, and most families had not even been in the habit of growing and eating vegetables before [ev_food_security_arsky20_6]. Families with subsurface dams gained more varied diets, mainly through more access to fruit and vegetables, and most of those interviewed reported more food available [ev_food_security_cirilo03_6]; a review of Embrapa experiments judges irrigation of small beds from production cisterns important for household food security [ev_food_security_castro22_3], and adopters of barraginha runoff basins identified food security, in quantity, quality and diversity, as the technology's greatest impact [ev_food_security_mira19_2].
water_harvesting_conservation__food_inse.conditionality: The gain is rated slight because no unit gives a size of effect: the evidence is qualitative interviews, an expert account of a cistern programme, a review of the research institute's own experiments, and an adopter-rated indicator in Embrapa's self-assessment of its own technology [ev_food_security_cirilo03_6, ev_food_security_arsky20_6, ev_food_security_castro22_3, ev_food_security_mira19_2]. All of it comes from semi-arid Brazil and works through garden irrigation and diet diversity rather than staple-crop supply, so it describes household storage for home production, not field-scale harvesting.

water_harvesting_conservation__heat_stre.mechanism: There is not enough evidence to rate an effect on heat stress. A review of quasi-experimental studies reports that the impact of soil and water conservation is especially significant in areas with temperature shocks or lower rainfall [ev_crop_yield_mala24_5]. By contrast, a modelling team judges that harvesting rain will likely not protect crops from the more frequent lethal high temperatures expected in the semi-arid tropics, especially the Sahel [ev_crop_yield_lebel15_2].
water_harvesting_conservation__heat_stre.conditionality: The review groups temperature shocks with low rainfall and names no specific practice or size of effect, so it does not isolate heat-stress losses [ev_crop_yield_mala24_5]. The second paper is the authors' judgement, not a measurement or model result [ev_crop_yield_lebel15_2]. What is missing is a measured heat-stress comparison with and without the practice.

water_harvesting_conservation__heat_stre.mechanism: A maize meta-regression finds conservation agriculture performs better relative to conventional practice under drought and/or heat stress, and a review of quasi-experimental studies reports that the impact of soil and water conservation is especially significant in areas with temperature shocks or lower rainfall [ev_crop_yield_stew18_2, ev_crop_yield_mala24_5].
water_harvesting_conservation__heat_stre.conditionality: Neither unit separates heat from drought: the meta-regression frames them together and the review groups temperature shocks with low rainfall, without naming specific practices or giving a magnitude, so no unit isolates heat-stress losses [ev_crop_yield_stew18_2, ev_crop_yield_mala24_5]. The meta-regression is restricted to maize under conservation agriculture, so it speaks to in-field residue and tillage practices rather than to storage structures [ev_crop_yield_stew18_2].

water_harvesting_conservation__productio.mechanism: Soil and water conservation structures raise farm production mainly by conserving moisture and nutrients on the plot over time. In Ethiopia's Blue Nile basin highlands, households that adopted sustainable land and water management technologies early saw 15.2% higher value of production by 2010 [ev_agricultural_production_value_schmidt12_1], and plots that received the investment in the first period saw 20.6% higher production value than matched plots that did not [ev_agricultural_production_value_schmidt12_4]. A review of more than a hundred Ethiopian soil-and-water-conservation studies found stone and soil bunds raising crop yield by up to 10% in Tigray [ev_crop_yield_adim16_8]. A continental model of in situ rainwater harvesting for rainfed maize across Africa finds that, where it steadies yields, the mean potential yield gain is 9 to 39% under the climate of the 1990s, rising to 14–50% by the 2050s depending on the climate model [ev_crop_yield_lebel15_1].
water_harvesting_conservation__productio.conditionality: The same structures can cost yield before they pay off: the same review found soil and stone bunds reducing crop yield by up to 7% in the first few years after construction [ev_crop_yield_adim16_7], and in semi-arid Tanzania, stone bunds were found to reduce maize yield by 13% [ev_crop_yield_adim16_9]. In Ethiopia's high-rainfall Amhara region, a farm survey found no significant yield difference between conserved and non-conserved plots, with the point estimate actually negative, and the authors suggest moisture conservation may contribute to waterlogging, weeds and pests in wetter areas [ev_agricultural_production_value_kass08_2]. Measured harm (maladaptation) — the practice worsening this outcome for some adopters — appears in 13 sources. The Africa-wide maize gain is a model, not a field measurement, and the same authors judge that rainwater harvesting will likely not protect yields against the more frequent lethal high temperatures expected in the Sahel [ev_crop_yield_lebel15_1, ev_crop_yield_lebel15_2].

water_harvesting_conservation__productio.mechanism: In the tropical highlands, soil and water conservation has measured yield gains and measured yield losses, depending on the practice. Gains: an Ethiopian synthesis finds mean grain-yield gains of 322 kg per hectare for stone bunds, 554.3 for tied ridges and 629.2 for mulching, stone and soil bunds raising yields by up to 10% in Tigray, and stone bunds raising soil total nitrogen from 0.16 to 0.20% [ev_crop_yield_adim16_1, ev_crop_yield_adim16_3, ev_crop_yield_adim16_4, ev_crop_yield_adim16_8, ev_soil_nitrogen_adim16_1]; in a Kenyan highland trial, tied ridges in long rains with dry spells gave 4.10 against 3.15 t of maize per hectare with manure and fertiliser, and 2.53 against 1.82 t without inputs (not significant), and tended to give less variable yields [ev_crop_yield_ndun23_3, ev_crop_yield_ndun23_1, ev_yield_stability_ndun23_1]; in Peru, 2 to 4-year old bench terraces gave 20% greater yields than adjacent sloping fields [ev_crop_yield_wei16_4]. In the Ethiopian highlands, fields with long-established fanya juu terraces and grass strips yielded 0.95 against 0.49 t of teff, 1.86 against 0.61 t of barley and 1.73 against 0.77 t of maize per hectare on adjacent un-terraced farms, and the terraces improved the water productivity of the three crops by at least 100% [ev_crop_yield_adgo13_1, ev_crop_yield_adgo13_2, ev_crop_yield_adgo13_3, ev_rain_water_productivity_adgo13_7]. Losses: in the same Ethiopian synthesis fanya juu and soil bunds were associated with yield losses of 54 to 193 kg per hectare, bunds cut yields by up to 7% in the first few years, and annual rainfall above 1000 mm affected performance negatively, which the authors suggest may be waterlogging in the furrows of structures [ev_crop_yield_adim16_2, ev_crop_yield_adim16_7, ev_crop_yield_adim16_6].
water_harvesting_conservation__productio.conditionality: The class is set by the gains. The fanya juu and soil bund losses and the finding that annual rainfall above 1000 mm affected performance negatively are held out of it, because the synthesis puts that effect down to excessive water availability (water logging) on the furrows of structures [ev_crop_yield_adim16_2, ev_crop_yield_adim16_6]: they are logged as a performance caveat — these structures should not be applied where rainfall is that heavy — rather than as production evidence. The evidence points to three things that separate gains from losses. Practice type: stone bunds, tied ridges and mulching gained, while graded and level fanya juu, soil bunds and grass strips lost yield in the Ethiopian table [ev_crop_yield_adim16_3, ev_crop_yield_adim16_2]. Rainfall: the gaining practices were studied at lower average rainfall (695.1 mm for tied ridges, 876.7 mm for mulching) than the losing bunds (1030.2 to 1454.3 mm), and rainfall above 1000 mm reduced performance [ev_crop_yield_adim16_3, ev_crop_yield_adim16_6]; practice and rainfall travel together in that table, so the two cannot be fully separated. Time: bunds lose yield in the first few years, while the long-established fanya juu terraces of the Ethiopian with-and-without survey yielded more than un-terraced fields, so fanya juu is not a losing practice everywhere [ev_crop_yield_adim16_7, ev_crop_yield_adgo13_1]. Against those terrace gains, the same paper cites Herweg and Ludi (1999) and Kassie et al. (2008) finding that fanya juu, soil and stone bunds and grass strips did not increase crop yield or biomass in the highlands of Ethiopia and Eritrea [ev_crop_yield_adgo13_12]. For a Task Team Leader the actionable reading is to match the structure to the rainfall regime, favouring in-field moisture capture in drier highlands and avoiding fanya juu and soil bunds where waterlogging is likely, and to budget for an early yield dip. At the dry end, tied ridging gave no advantage in the Kenyan short rains with meteorological droughts, since there was little rain to hold [ev_crop_yield_ndun23_2, ev_crop_yield_ndun23_4, ev_crop_yield_ndun23_5]. On quality, both sides rest mainly on the same Ethiopian synthesis of unweighted means pooled across studies; the Kenyan result is a single-site trial whose lower-variability finding was not tested, the Peruvian figure is cited in a review, and the Ethiopian terrace gains are descriptive statistics from a comparison of terraced and adjacent un-terraced farms, not a controlled trial [ev_crop_yield_adim16_1, ev_yield_stability_ndun23_1, ev_crop_yield_wei16_4, ev_crop_yield_adgo13_2].

water_harvesting_conservation__productio.mechanism: In semi-arid settings, pits (zai, tassa), stone bunds, tied furrows and subsurface dams concentrate scarce rainfall in the root zone or store it for later use, raising cereal yields and enabling harvests in drought years when untreated fields fail.
water_harvesting_conservation__productio.conditionality: Evidence mixes Sahelian field results (Burkina Faso, Niger) with Embrapa and cistern-programme sources from semi-arid Brazil, several of them self-assessments or expert statements; the Brazilian programme effects are on value of production, a proxy, and some yield gains depend on manure added to the pits.

water_harvesting_conservation__productio.mechanism: In Niger's Tahoua region, earth bench-bunds (banquettes) and contour stone bunds were found to raise fodder yield over untreated control plots [ev_forage_productivity_botreij09_16]. In Algeria's semi-arid steppe, an improved system combining stone lines with a runoff-catchment impluvium, subsoiling, mulch, fertiliser and a wheat/faba-bean rotation under apricot trees raised mean winter wheat yield from 3 quintals per hectare on the farmer's traditional plot to 27 quintals per hectare [ev_crop_yield_roose17_8].
water_harvesting_conservation__productio.conditionality: The Algerian figure comes from a single unreplicated comparison plot bundling many practices together (subsoiling, mulch, fertiliser, rotation, windbreaks), so the gain cannot be attributed to the stone lines and runoff catchment alone.

water_harvesting_conservation__productio.mechanism: In rainfed hill and watershed systems, in-situ rainwater conservation, terracing and soil and water conservation works combined with crop packages raise yields: average rainfed crop yields rose 24% and 26% against controls in Karnataka watershed phases, rainfed crop productivity rose 20.8 percent by difference-in-difference in Uttarakhand, and maize on terraced Rwandan hillsides rose from 1.5 to 2.8 tons per hectare [ev_crop_yield_iegind11_1, ev_crop_yield_utk22_1, ev_crop_yield_rwa18_7]. The DIME evaluation reported for Rwanda found the value of harvests 36 percent higher than in the control group [ev_agricultural_production_value_rwa18_3]. Outside these programmes, on-farm trials in Mozambique gave maize gains of 504 to 800 kg per hectare on planting basins and direct-seeded conservation agriculture over conventional ridge-and-furrow plots, and farmers in a Kenyan sand-dam catchment had less crop failure than in a control catchment [ev_crop_yield_thierf15_3, ev_crop_yield_lasage08_1].
water_harvesting_conservation__productio.conditionality: The Indian and Rwandan units are bundled programmes in which conservation works came with improved seed, vermicompost, crop packages or life-saving irrigation, so the share due to water harvesting is not isolated, and they are drawn from Bank completion reports or IEG reviews of them; the Rwanda maize figure is project monitoring without a control and the Uttarakhand terrace figure compares with- and without-project models [ev_crop_yield_hp17_2, ev_crop_yield_utk22_8, ev_crop_yield_iegind11_1, ev_crop_yield_rwa18_7]. In Mozambique conservation agriculture and control plots alike gave no maize or cowpea harvest in a drought season, and the Kenyan crop-failure finding comes from interviews [ev_crop_yield_thierf15_1, ev_crop_yield_thierf15_2, ev_crop_yield_lasage08_1].

water_harvesting_conservation__productio.mechanism: Sand dams in Zimbabwe improved water availability, and livestock health improved at eight sites where cattle had been driven up to 20 km to the nearest water point before construction [ev_livestock_productivity_lazurko24_1].
water_harvesting_conservation__productio.conditionality: Against this, long-term Zimbabwe trials found conventional tillage yielding considerably more maize than mulched and reduced-tillage treatments in extreme seasons, with no water-conservation benefit from mulch in the 1991/1992 drought [ev_crop_yield_rusin11_7]. The livestock finding rests on respondent statements, and both findings come from Zimbabwe only.

water_harvesting_conservation__productio.mechanism: There is not enough evidence to rate the effect on rangeland production. In Jordan's Badia, contour furrows and ridges planted with saltbush (a drought-hardy fodder shrub) were reported to harvest more runoff, control erosion and considerably improve forage quantity and quality [ev_forage_productivity_stav20_5]. In Texas, United States, shrubs planted in micro-catchments survived twice as well and grew far more than those on unmodified ground [ev_forage_productivity_stav20_8]. Micro-catchment bunds in the Jordanian Badia showed no difference in topsoil nitrogen from the untreated strips between them [ev_soil_nitrogen_tats21_2].
water_harvesting_conservation__productio.conditionality: Both forage findings come from one review that cites other studies rather than measuring itself [ev_forage_productivity_stav20_5, ev_forage_productivity_stav20_8], and the only measured study found no effect and looked at soil nitrogen, not forage [ev_soil_nitrogen_tats21_2]. A second independent source, or one measured forage or livestock result, is needed before this row can be rated. The overall production row does not differ by this system in any evidence-backed way yet.

water_harvesting_conservation__productio.mechanism: In a commercial potato-growing watershed in New Brunswick, Canada, terraced fields outyielded non-terraced fields under both dry conditions (32.76 versus 32.39 tonnes per hectare) and normal conditions (34.97 versus 34.70 tonnes per hectare) [ev_crop_yield_lian19_1, ev_crop_yield_lian19_2]. In Texas, United States, shrubs planted in micro-catchments survived twice as well and grew far more than those planted on unmodified ground, a finding cited second-hand [ev_forage_productivity_stav20_8].
water_harvesting_conservation__productio.conditionality: The gain is small. The advantage reverses in wet years: in the same watershed, non-terraced fields slightly outyielded terraced fields under wet conditions (31.90 versus 31.77 tonnes per hectare), with the lowest yields of the whole series in wet years for both groups [ev_crop_yield_lian19_3]. In the Canary Islands, soil nitrogen was higher in gavias runoff-harvesting fields than in nearby uncultivated soil (0.7 versus 0.6 g/kg) [ev_soil_nitrogen_roose17_2]; this is soil fertility, not yield. The Canadian results come from one watershed. All evidence is from high-income countries (Canada, Spain, United States).

water_harvesting_conservation__productio.mechanism: Stored or concentrated water raises yields and adds harvests. In the Brazilian semi-arid, tied furrows gave 606 kg of maize per hectare against 302 kg under traditional planting, soil management in subsurface dams raised crop productivity over 22 years without salinisation, larger subsurface dams let some owners take up to 4 consecutive harvests in 12 months, and runoff retention with rescue irrigation is credited with securing fruit production in a 550 mm rainfall zone [ev_crop_yield_brito07_8, ev_crop_yield_brito07_5, ev_crop_yield_cirilo03_4, ev_crop_yield_fao13c_2]. A quasi-experimental study of a Brazilian cistern programme found a raised value of family production, and programme authors describe wider water access letting families expand and diversify production [ev_agricultural_production_value_casag22_7, ev_agricultural_production_value_arsky20_7]. Beyond Brazil, 2 to 4-year old bench terraces in Peru gave 20% greater yields than adjacent sloping fields, silt farmland behind check dams on China's Loess Plateau yields 6–10 times more than sloping farmland, and the Jordanian compiler rates fodder production up because the barley crop and its stubble feed animals [ev_crop_yield_wei16_4, ev_crop_yield_luca21_1, ev_forage_productivity_wocat_5770_2020_fodder_production].
water_harvesting_conservation__productio.conditionality: Results are not uniform. A review of infiltration trenches reports yield gains on some plots and losses on others [ev_crop_yield_locat20_1, ev_crop_yield_locat20_2]; in Algeria, farmers who lost 5 to 15% of their farmland to banquettes saw no yield improvement, and legumes grown between banquettes showed no significant gain [ev_crop_yield_arab04_1, ev_crop_yield_arab04_2]. A Brazilian farmer's subsurface dam produced no harvest in one season of adverse weather [ev_crop_yield_brito07_6]. Much of the Brazilian evidence is Embrapa or programme self-assessment, the cistern-programme author states there are no quantitative impact evaluations, and the value-of-production finding is a proxy for yield [ev_agricultural_production_value_arsky20_7, ev_agricultural_production_value_casag22_7]. The Chinese check-dam figure is a secondary citation that also notes soil salinisation on check-dam farmland, and a South African farmer's account of stable harvests concerns a residue-cover system with no capture structure [ev_crop_yield_luca21_1, ev_yield_stability_faocr11_10].

water_harvesting_conservation__recurrent.mechanism: Pooled costs are compiler-reported annual maintenance costs from WOCAT technology sheets, per hectare for sheets in Tunisia, India, Ethiopia, Yemen, Uganda, Jordan and Somalia and per structure for a farm pond in Cambodia, check dams in India, a vetiver line in Haiti, a fascine line in Madagascar and a haffir in Somalia; the cost class is set from the per-hectare sheets.
water_harvesting_conservation__recurrent.conditionality: WOCAT figures are the compiler's own cost tables for the documented technology, summed and converted to USD with the sheet's own exchange rate; they are not market prices. Older sheets treat every costed item as per hectare, and the per-hectare values run from a cent to several hundred USD per hectare per year, so the sub-dollar Uganda and India figures look like entry or conversion problems; the Jordan sheet is an upper-middle-income case.

water_harvesting_conservation__rural_pov.mechanism: Water harvesting raises rural household income mainly through higher-value production: in Ghana, net rice profit rose by 16% under soil and water conservation [ev_economic_return_mala24_1]. In Ethiopia's Lake Tana watershed, an IFAD-funded watershed project raised the income of high-participation households by 17.8% over the control group [ev_household_income_abate21_3], though the programme-wide average effect on log income was only 0.044 [ev_household_income_abate21_2].
water_harvesting_conservation__rural_pov.conditionality: The economics do not always work out: a review of Ethiopian conservation practices found negative net present values for graded fanya juu (−148 Ethiopian Birr per hectare) and graded soil bunds (−708 Ethiopian Birr per hectare), which the authors attribute to cost-benefit analyses that do not fully capture on-site and off-site benefits [ev_economic_return_adim16_4]. In Zimbabwe, conservation agriculture was found to generate less revenue than conventional tillage for maize and cowpea over a large part of the rainfall distribution [ev_economic_return_mich19_8]. In Tigray, stone-bund building and maintenance costs were found to be nearly the same as the financial benefits from yield improvement, making the economic case close to break-even [ev_economic_return_nyss07_10]. Measured harm (maladaptation) — the practice worsening this outcome for some adopters — appears in 11 sources. Within this family, micro-catchment, runoff-catchment and terracing systems point positive while cross-family and in-situ readings disagree internally, so the roll-up states conflicting evidence rather than the pooled strong positive.

water_harvesting_conservation__rural_pov.mechanism: On this AEZ's own evidence, terracing and bunding usually pay in the Ethiopian highlands: teff, barley and maize grown on long-established terraces earned incremental income of US$159, 275 and 141 per hectare per year over un-terraced farms, and terrace investment for barley had an average net present value of US$1542 over 50 years at a 10 percent discount rate, positive across the catchment [ev_economic_return_adgo13_4, ev_economic_return_adgo13_5, ev_economic_return_adgo13_6, ev_economic_return_adgo13_10]. An Ethiopian synthesis gives positive net present values of 3486.2 Birr per hectare for stone bunds, 2794.0 for bench terraces and 5283.4 for level fanya juu [ev_economic_return_adim16_1, ev_economic_return_adim16_2, ev_economic_return_adim16_3]. In Peru, a benefit of 1.96 soles was found for each sol invested in building cochas [ev_economic_return_card22_1], and modelled bench-terrace gains there could raise per capita incomes by up to 15 percent [ev_household_income_wei16_1].
water_harvesting_conservation__rural_pov.conditionality: Against this, the same Ethiopian synthesis found graded fanya juu and graded soil bunds carrying negative net present values of −148 and −708 ETB per hectare [ev_economic_return_adim16_4], and in a Kenyan highland trial net benefits in the drought-affected short rains were higher without tied ridging than with it, except under one soil treatment [ev_economic_return_ndun23_1]. Income and returns are proxies for poverty rather than a poverty measure itself, the Ethiopian net present values are unweighted means from a small set of studies, and the Peruvian per-capita figure is a modelled 'potentially... up to' estimate cited in a review rather than a measured outcome [ev_economic_return_adim16_1, ev_household_income_wei16_1].

water_harvesting_conservation__rural_pov.mechanism: In this semi-arid-AEZ evidence, water harvesting and soil and water conservation mostly raise household income and farm returns, mainly through higher yields, garden irrigation and livestock, though not always. In Zimbabwe, first-year planting-basin farmers earned a maize gross margin of 473.36 US dollars per hectare against 70.60 on conventional plots without fertiliser, and the gain held in the fertilised comparison too [ev_economic_return_mazv09_1, ev_economic_return_mazv09_3]. In Burkina Faso, manual zaï and demi-lunes gave a positive net economic benefit, and groundwater rising behind stone bunds let households earn income from vegetables grown near the wells [ev_economic_return_zoug14_1, ev_economic_return_zour25h1_3, ev_household_income_zoug14_1]. A new study of decentralised irrigation, including rainwater-harvesting ponds, finds household income significantly higher among adopters [ev_household_income_silv26_1]. In Brazil, production cisterns and subsurface dams raised family farm income by about 4.6 percent, rising to nearly 11 percent once the top of the income distribution is excluded, with the clearest gains on the smallest farms, and farmers reported better family income and quality of life from a subsurface dam, though it was not their main income source [ev_household_income_casag22_1, ev_household_income_casag22_2, ev_household_income_brito07_7]. Returns to labour for zaï in Burkina Faso exceed the shadow wage [ev_economic_return_kabo04_1].
water_harvesting_conservation__rural_pov.conditionality: Against this, a Burkina Faso trial found 30-centimetre zaï running at a net loss against its own investment cost [ev_economic_return_zour25h1_4]; a single soil and water conservation measure did not cover its annual costs [ev_economic_return_zoug14_3]; and Brazil's wider production-cistern programme returned a benefit-cost ratio of 0.0858 over its evaluation window, well below one, with the Brazilian income gain turning negative on farms larger than 10 hectares and two subsurface-dam units finding the income effect almost non-existent or limited in a stagnant local economy [ev_economic_return_casag22_9, ev_household_income_casag22_6, ev_household_income_cirilo03_5, ev_household_income_cirilo03_7]. Income and farm returns are proxies for poverty, most units are farm budgets or household surveys rather than poverty measures, and none follows households over time.

water_harvesting_conservation__rural_pov.mechanism: In Algeria's semi-arid steppe, after subtracting the cost of extra inputs, farmers using an improved system with stone lines and a runoff-catchment impluvium were left with an income per hectare far higher than under traditional cropping: $7,000 against $500 [ev_economic_return_roose17_2].
water_harvesting_conservation__rural_pov.conditionality: This is a single unreplicated comparison bundling many practices together (subsoiling, mulch, fertiliser, rotation, windbreaks), so the gain cannot be attributed to the stone lines and runoff catchment alone. In southern Ethiopia, a household survey around sand dams found no clear difference in economic situation or time spent on other activities between households with and without improved water access [ev_household_income_lasa13_2].

water_harvesting_conservation__rural_pov.mechanism: In mixed crop–livestock systems, farm budgets show water capture both paying and not paying. In Zimbabwe, planting-basin conservation farming earned a first-year maize gross margin of 473.36 against 70.6 US dollars per hectare for conventional practice without fertiliser and 48.19 with fertiliser, and experienced households could earn US$866.84 per hectare against US$357.16 for a farmer using chemical fertilizer in higher rainfall [ev_economic_return_mazv09_1, ev_economic_return_mazv09_3, ev_economic_return_mazv09_2]. In semi-arid India, net returns rose with livestock and trees to US$ 586 per hectare and to US$ 857 once a farm pond was added [ev_economic_return_pals23_1]. In a Kenyan highland trial, by contrast, net benefits in the short-rains season were higher without tied ridging than with it, except under one soil treatment [ev_economic_return_ndun23_1]. Further farm-budget evidence from mixed crop-livestock systems points the same way. In Zambia, hand-hoe conservation-farming basins gave cotton gross margins 70 percent higher than conventional hand-hoe cultivation and 150 percent higher than conventional ox ploughing, and maize returns to land and peak-season labour 60 to 90 percent higher than hand-hoe tillage [ev_economic_return_hagg03_6, ev_economic_return_hagg03_7, ev_economic_return_hagg03_8]; partial budgets there found a marginal rate of return of 860 percent for switching from hand hoeing to basin digging and 360 percent from ox ploughing to basin digging [ev_economic_return_umar12_2, ev_economic_return_umar12_3]. In the Ethiopian highlands, teff, barley and maize on long-established terraces earned incremental income of US$159, 275 and 141 per hectare per year over un-terraced farms, with an average net present value for barley terracing of US$1542 over 50 years [ev_economic_return_adgo13_4, ev_economic_return_adgo13_5, ev_economic_return_adgo13_6, ev_economic_return_adgo13_10]. In Ethiopia's Tigray, agricultural income from crops and livestock was significantly higher for users than non-users of water-management techniques [ev_household_income_biaz12_18], and Brazilian small family farms saw their monthly income rise once barraginhas filled with water [ev_household_income_mira19_1]. In Kenya's Kitui District, a mixed crop-livestock sand-dam district, calculated household income held up or rose by 27,241 KSh a year for households with a dam against a fall of 38,056 KSh for those without — a difference of 65,297 KSh in a drought year [ev_household_income_pauw08_1].
water_harvesting_conservation__rural_pov.conditionality: The sides differ in season, in what is compared and in how cleanly water capture is isolated. The Kenyan loss is from a short-rains season of meteorological droughts, in a trial that compares tied ridging with and without under the same soil inputs [ev_economic_return_ndun23_1]; it is the cleanest single comparison here. The Zimbabwean gains set a package of basins, manure, fertiliser and residue against conventional practice, so the water-capture effect is mixed with nutrient supply, and the higher-rainfall figure is a sensitivity scenario with assumed yields [ev_economic_return_mazv09_1, ev_economic_return_mazv09_2]. The Indian figure comes from a farmer survey in which few farms had a pond, the pond water was also used for irrigation, and the compared farms differ in other ways [ev_economic_return_pals23_1]. The evidence therefore cannot say whether water capture alone pays in this farming system; the gains belong to packages, and the one isolated test found a loss in a drought season. All of these are farm budgets rather than measures of household poverty, and none follows households over time [ev_economic_return_mazv09_1, ev_economic_return_mazv09_2, ev_economic_return_mazv09_3, ev_economic_return_ndun23_1, ev_economic_return_pals23_1]. Against this, in Tigray stone-bund building costs about as much each year as the financial benefit from the induced yield gain, roughly breaking even [ev_economic_return_nyss07_10]. The Zambian and Ethiopian gains are farm budgets, and the Ethiopian terrace income excludes family labour and is measured on terraces maintained for decades, so it shows what an established, well-maintained system returns rather than the first years after building [ev_economic_return_hagg03_6, ev_economic_return_adgo13_4]. The Kitui income result is likewise a cross-sectional household survey with multi-year recall rather than a randomised comparison; dams were not placed at random, dam households also applied more terracing, bunds and grass lines whose effect cannot be separated, and 'calculated income' is a price-based proxy, not a measured cash amount [ev_household_income_pauw08_1].

water_harvesting_conservation__rural_pov.mechanism: In upper-middle-income settings the income gain is small. In Brazil's semi-arid Northeast, a national cistern programme raised farm income by about 4.6% compared with a matched group [ev_household_income_casag22_1], about 11% when the richest 5% of farms are left out [ev_household_income_casag22_2], and more on farms of 0-10 ha [ev_household_income_casag22_5]. Small runoff basins in Brazil raised the income of small family farms by about half a minimum wage a month [ev_household_income_mira19_1], and subsurface dams paid back several times their cost over 10 years [ev_economic_return_cirilo03_10]. In Peru, building cochas (small ponds) returned 1.96 soles per sol invested [ev_economic_return_card22_1].
water_harvesting_conservation__rural_pov.conditionality: The gain is uneven. The same Brazilian cistern programme had a benefit-cost ratio of only 0.0858, raising average yearly income by about R$424.71 against a mean of R$9,328.48 [ev_economic_return_casag22_9], and for farms over 10 hectares the effect was negative [ev_household_income_casag22_6]; outside the Northeast it was not significant [ev_household_income_casag22_4]. In other Brazilian cases subsurface dams brought almost no cash income because little was sold [ev_household_income_cirilo03_5, ev_household_income_cirilo03_7]. In Peru, bench terraces lost money when measured yields and market wages were used, but looked profitable on farmers' own estimates [ev_economic_return_post05_2, ev_economic_return_post05_3, ev_economic_return_post05_4], and a per-person income gain of up to 15% is a model figure [ev_household_income_wei16_1]. Several programmes bundle the structure with grants and training.

water_harvesting_conservation__soil_eros.mechanism: Soil and water conservation structures cut both runoff and the soil it carries. A review of Ethiopian studies found graded soil bunds reducing surface runoff by 25.2% (from 190.7 to 142.7 mm) and soil loss by 59% (from 43.6 to 17.9 tonnes per hectare) [ev_runoff_reduction_adim16_1, ev_erosion_hazard_adim16_1]; level soil bunds cut runoff by 60.1% and soil loss by 88% (from 17.5 to 2.1 tonnes per hectare) [ev_runoff_reduction_adim16_2, ev_erosion_hazard_adim16_2]; and stone bunds cut runoff by 34.4% [ev_runoff_reduction_adim16_3].
water_harvesting_conservation__soil_eros.conditionality: The benefit shrinks where rainfall itself is very low: in drought-prone areas with less than 500 mm of annual rainfall, a meta-analysis found catchment treatment had minimal effect on reducing runoff [ev_runoff_reduction_meaza22_3]. Measured harm (maladaptation) — the practice worsening this outcome for some adopters — appears in 8 sources.

water_harvesting_conservation__soil_eros.mechanism: In the Maghreb, contour structures have been reported both to hold runoff and to accelerate erosion. Staggered earth bunds (tabia) in Morocco store the runoff of all rains below 50 mm on the field [ev_runoff_reduction_roos10_1]. In Algeria, a poorly maintained banquette becomes a factor accelerating erosion, because the smallest unrepaired breach triggers a chain reaction through the whole network in torrential and prolonged rains [ev_erosion_hazard_arab04_2].
water_harvesting_conservation__soil_eros.conditionality: Two conditions separate the sides in the sources. Maintenance: the acceleration is tied explicitly to unrepaired breaches in state-built banquettes [ev_erosion_hazard_arab04_2]. Storm size: the tabia hold runoff only up to rains of 50 mm, and in bigger storms the excess overtops them and gullies the whole slope [ev_runoff_reduction_roos10_1]. The actionable reading is to plan and fund upkeep and spillways, not only construction. Elsewhere banquettes simply did not stop gullying: gullied areas on Tunisian banquette land grew by 12% between 1963 and 1973, and over 1947-1968 Algerian banquettes had no influence on the sedimentation rate of the Oued Fodda dam [ev_erosion_hazard_arab04_1, ev_sediment_retention_arab04_1]. Neither side is measured on plots: the protective statement is from an expert manual and the harmful ones are secondary citations within a national evaluation, and the two concern different structures, tabia and banquettes [ev_runoff_reduction_roos10_1, ev_erosion_hazard_arab04_2].

water_harvesting_conservation__soil_eros.mechanism: On rangeland the studies disagree, unlike the overall row, which shows a strong benefit; 2 papers name this farming system. On the benefit side, in Arizona loose-rock check dams cut the number of runoff events from small storms by 60% [ev_runoff_reduction_poly14_1], held back much of the watershed's sediment [ev_sediment_retention_poly14_1] and gave a twofold drop in sediment yield at the outlet [ev_sediment_retention_poly14_2]; and stone-terraced hillslopes in Palestine reduced runoff by 65–85% and erosion by 58–69%, a figure cited second-hand [ev_runoff_reduction_stav20_1].
water_harvesting_conservation__soil_eros.conditionality: On the harm side, abandoned runoff structures in Arizona rangeland failed about 30 years later and some sped up local gully head retreat [ev_erosion_hazard_stav20_12], and collapsing stone terraces in Israel's Negev started rill and gully erosion [ev_erosion_hazard_stav20_13]. For big storms the Arizona check dams had no significant effect on runoff volume [ev_runoff_reduction_poly14_2]. What separates the two sides is upkeep: the harm comes from structures left to fail. The harm findings come from one review citing other studies, and most of the evidence is from high-income countries.

water_harvesting_conservation__soil_eros.mechanism: In high-income countries the studies disagree. On the benefit side, a review found bench terracing cut runoff by 9% and sediment yield by 58% [ev_runoff_reduction_meko14_1]; in Arizona, loose-rock check dams cut the number of runoff events from small storms by 60% [ev_runoff_reduction_poly14_1], held back much of the watershed's sediment [ev_sediment_retention_poly14_1] and gave a twofold drop in sediment yield at the outlet [ev_sediment_retention_poly14_2]; a small Belgian pond kept trapping 68% of sediment over 33 years [ev_sediment_retention_meko14_3]; and Spanish terraces reduce runoff when maintained [ev_runoff_reduction_arna15_5].
water_harvesting_conservation__soil_eros.conditionality: On the harm side, channel beds eroded below check dams at 81% of surveyed dams in a Spanish catchment [ev_erosion_hazard_fran21_1]; abandoned runoff structures in Arizona rangeland failed and sped up local gully head retreat [ev_erosion_hazard_stav20_12]; and collapsing stone terraces in Israel's Negev started rill and gully erosion [ev_erosion_hazard_stav20_13]. For big storms the Arizona check dams had no significant effect on runoff volume [ev_runoff_reduction_poly14_2], and the Arizona sediment drop was significant only at a weak test level [ev_sediment_retention_poly14_2]. What separates the two sides is upkeep and storm size: the harm findings come from abandoned or failing structures. Most findings are cited second-hand.

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: In Tunisia, drought caused a shortfall in the spate-irrigation and water-recharge works established in Medenine, where only 15 were built against a target of 95 [ev_drought_hazard_iegtun13_2].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: The single unit comes from an ex-post review drawing on project completion data and describes an establishment-phase shortfall of works, not physical damage to structures already built.

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: On Ethiopian soil and water conservation structures, a review reports second-hand that when the drainage ditch behind a structure fills with sediment, trapping efficiency quickly decreases and the extra pressure on the structure can lead to structural failure [ev_sediment_retention_meko14_1_av].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: The evidence is too thin to state a sensitivity: a single statement cited second-hand in a review, with no rate or frequency of failure; it does describe a damage pathway, and implies the damage depends on whether ditches are cleared [ev_sediment_retention_meko14_1_av]. What is missing is a second independent source or one measured finding on how often silted structures fail.

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: On Burkina Faso's Central Plateau, a CILSS regional synthesis of natural-resource-management investment reports that soil and water conservation works (zaï, demi-lunes, stone bunds and permeable rock dams) had a positive impact on the reconstitution of woody vegetation and floristic richness, with 60 species recorded on treated sites [ev_biodiversity_outcome_botreij09_25].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: The row carries this one evidence unit from one source: a regional synthesis citing a national study team's report, not a direct measurement by the authors themselves, and the untreated-site comparator count sits on the following page of the source and cannot be quoted alongside this passage, so only the treated-site count is reported. A second independent source, or one measured finding against a stated comparator, would let this cell state a class [ev_biodiversity_outcome_botreij09_25].

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: In Burkina Faso, soils on farms using soil and water conservation techniques had higher carbon and nitrogen contents than the control farm [ev_soil_organic_carbon_sawa11h1_3], and a review cites climate-smart packages of soil and water conservation structures with biological measures boosting soil carbon stock by three to seven times over business-as-usual [ev_soil_organic_carbon_tade23h1_3].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: Only two units, neither a measured stock change against a matched control: the Burkina Faso figure is a carbon content on farms using several techniques with compost, and the three-to-sevenfold gain is a review's citation of a package that includes biological measures, very large for structures and to be read with caution [ev_soil_organic_carbon_sawa11h1_3, ev_soil_organic_carbon_tade23h1_3].

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: Watershed-scale soil and water conservation is reported to raise groundwater, used here as a component of catchment water yield: stone bunds, zaï and half-moons applied at watershed scale increase ground water level [ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_zoug14_1]; in Burkina Faso improved well levels are linked to SWC measures that control surface runoff and improve infiltration [ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_kabo04_1]; ISRO survey data record an increase in groundwater recharge in treated areas in India [ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_iegind11_3]; piezometers recorded groundwater levels rising in 16 of 21 non-desert districts with an average increase of 1.42 meters [ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_verm19_3]; the Uttarakhand water budget shows aquifer recharge up 3.3 percent and water yield from catchment areas up 4.9 percent [ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_utk22_5]; and in Ethiopia improvements in the water table made small-scale irrigation possible [ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_eth16_7]. In Burkina Faso, cited studies show soil and water conservation techniques improving the availability of ground water in many villages, especially large rock bunds known as digues filtrantes [ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_sawa11h1_6]. In Ethiopia's Mendae catchment a water balance gave groundwater recharge of 107.7 mm after water harvesting against 8 mm before (Negusse et al., 2013, cited by Gebremeskel et al.) [ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_gebr18_11]. On the other side, the same capture reduces what leaves the catchment: water outflows from treated catchments have been found halved compared with untreated catchments (Garg et al., 2012; Gates et al., 2011, cited by Gebremeskel et al.), reviews cite a decrease in runoff generation harming downstream social–ecological systems (Batchelor et al., 2003; Glendenning and Vervoort, 2011; Garg et al., 2012, cited by Dile et al.), and a global model suggested rainwater harvesting would reduce annual river flows by 18% on average and by up to 80% in a single basin (Wisser et al., 2010, cited by Glendenning et al.) [ev_water_yield_gebr18_9, ev_water_yield_dile13_9, ev_water_yield_glen12_10]. A landscape review of rainwater harvesting across African drylands also lists groundwater recharge and the filling of wells among its benefits [ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_vohl09_3]. A CILSS regional synthesis adds a further recharge observation: in Batodi, Niger, the water level in village wells rose by about 14 metres between 1994 and 2004, which the villagers attributed to the runoff-harvesting works [ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_botreij09_18].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: This row is for downstream users and basin planners: it asks what capturing water upstream does to the water that reaches streams and reservoirs below, not whether the farm that captures it has more. Studies disagree because the recharge side counts water entering the ground near treated land, while the outflow side counts water leaving the catchment, and the same works can raise the first and lower the second [ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_utk22_5, ev_water_yield_gebr18_9]. Scale and intensity also separate them: the outflow losses come from large-scale implementation and basin-wide models, while other studies find limited or no downstream impact on stream flows from small-scale storage, even when implemented widely (Schreider et al., 2002; De Winnaar and Jewitt, 2010; Andersson et al., 2011) [ev_water_yield_dile13_10, ev_water_yield_rock10_1]. The recharge gains have limits in their own sources: without data from untreated sites the Indian project impact is unclear [ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_iegind11_3], subsidised tube-well pumping has possibly wiped out any increases in recharge [ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_iegind11_4], and in Burkina Faso the number of wells with water year round has not increased significantly [ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_kabo04_2]. The Uttarakhand figures are a modelled water budget [ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_utk22_5], the outflow findings are all cited second-hand, and most other units are programme reports or cited statements; the digues filtrantes finding is cited from another study, with no figures [ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_sawa11h1_6]. That listing is the review's own qualitative evaluation across cited sources, not a measured recharge figure [ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_vohl09_3]. That well-level rise is the villagers' own attribution rather than a measurement against a comparable untreated well, and it adds to the recharge side of this row rather than resolving the conflict with the downstream-outflow evidence [ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_botreij09_18].

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: Costs are the per-hectare unit cost of watershed treatments (bunds, check dams and other soil and water conservation works) across treated area in two World Bank-supported India watershed projects.
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: Both figures come from one evaluation of bundled watershed programmes in India and are treatment costs per hectare treated, not per hectare of degraded land restored; the evaluator compares them with national budget norms rather than with outcomes.

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: Better-sited planning based on a land resource inventory avoided unnecessary structures, so construction of soil and water conservation works cost less per hectare than under the conventional integrated watershed programme.
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: Single lender completion-report figure from Karnataka, India, in local currency at stated price terms; the comparison is against another watershed programme, so it shows a saving from planning rather than the cost of SWC versus no SWC.

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: Pooled across water-harvesting structures, the benefit under drought is small. At a watershed scale, soil and water conservation works (zaï and half-moon pits, stone bunds, terraces, cisterns) raise water availability and buffer crop and rangeland productivity against drought. In Ethiopia, a large study of a national land-restoration programme found that in areas that experienced severe drought, programme effects on vegetation greenness and productivity were three times larger than the average programme effect, with increases of 16.71% in a vegetation index and 13.48% in gross primary productivity [ev_drought_hazard_cons22_1]; buffering effects were also significant under moderate drought [ev_drought_hazard_cons22_2] and, more weakly, under mild drought [ev_drought_hazard_cons22_3]. Zaï and half-moon pits in Burkina Faso retained soil moisture for 2 to 3 weeks longer, mitigating the impact of dry spells [ev_soil_water_retention_zour25h1_7]. A review of soil and water conservation technologies across multiple countries found they are particularly useful in regions with low rainfall or high climatic variability [ev_crop_yield_mala24_3], and a water-harvesting meta-analysis found significantly higher yield gains in seasons with rainfall below 330 millimetres [ev_crop_yield_boum16_4]. A continental model of in situ rainwater harvesting for rainfed maize across Africa finds that, where it steadies yields, the mean potential yield gain is 9 to 39% under the climate of the 1990s, rising to 14–50% by the 2050s depending on the climate model [ev_crop_yield_lebel15_1].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: At severe or extreme drought the measured results mostly show no benefit rather than a gain. In Niger, soil and water conservation works could not compensate when 2004 rainfall fell to only 200 to 250 millimetres, and villagers harvested nothing despite the works [ev_crop_yield_botreij09_17]; in Tunisia, four consecutive years of drought from 1998 to 2002 reduced agricultural and pastoral productivity gains and limited soil-conservation benefits [ev_drought_hazard_iegtun13_1]; and a general assessment states that crop yields cannot be sustained during a meteorological drought even where dry spells can be bridged by water-management investment [ev_crop_yield_rock10_2]. Soil and water conservation in Niger raised households' estimated surplus to 70% in good years but still left an estimated 28% deficit in low-rainfall years [ev_food_security_kabo04_1]. Only one of the studies reporting a benefit under drought gives a quantified size of effect [ev_drought_hazard_cons22_1]; the rest are qualitative statements of improved resilience. Most of the evidence is from low-income Sahelian and East African countries (Burkina Faso, Niger, Ethiopia), with programme-level evidence also from Tunisia, Brazil and China. The Africa-wide maize figure is a model, not a field measurement [ev_crop_yield_lebel15_1].

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: In rainfed cropping in the Sahel, water-harvesting pits and stone bunds give a small cushion against dry spells. In a Burkina Faso field trial, zaï pits of 30–40 cm and 1 m half-moons kept soil moist for 2–3 weeks and so softened the effect of dry spells [ev_soil_water_retention_zour25h1_7]. On Burkina Faso's Central Plateau in 2007, a season with dry spells, stone bunds combined with zaï pits raised grain yield by 118% over untreated fields [ev_crop_yield_botreij09_5], and the same regional synthesis says the gap between treated and untreated fields is larger in poor or mediocre rainfall years than in good ones [ev_crop_yield_botreij09_8]. An author's overall judgement from Burkina Faso is that these techniques have reduced households' vulnerability to drought and famine [ev_drought_hazard_sawa11h1_7].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: The benefit stops at severe drought: in Batodi, Niger, rainfall in 2004 was only 200 to 250 mm and villagers harvested nothing despite the works [ev_crop_yield_botreij09_17]. This is not a defence against late-onset or extreme drought. Only 1 of the 4 findings pointing to a benefit gives a size [ev_crop_yield_botreij09_5], and that figure is reported second-hand from project measurements; the vulnerability statement is an author's opinion, not a measurement [ev_drought_hazard_sawa11h1_7]. The soil-moisture result is a single-site trial and measures moisture, not harvests [ev_soil_water_retention_zour25h1_7]. All evidence comes from 3 sources in low-income Burkina Faso and Niger.

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: In mixed crop–livestock settings the evidence is the same as for rainfed cropping, with an Ethiopian watershed programme evaluation added. These are programme-scale or unspecified soil and water conservation packages. A review of impact studies finds such methods particularly useful in regions with low rainfall or high climatic variability, Ethiopia's PSNP public works improved watershed drought resilience by increasing water availability, and in semi-arid Brazil production cisterns can reduce animal mortality in severe drought [ev_crop_yield_mala24_3, ev_drought_hazard_arega24_4, ev_drought_hazard_castro22_2]. A water-harvesting review states that dry spells can be bridged through investments in water management [ev_crop_yield_rock10_1]. A meta-analysis of water-harvesting studies across semi-arid Africa and Asia (Bouma and colleagues) found significantly larger yield improvements in study years with rainfall below 330 mm than in wetter years, and gains in below-average rainfall years that were higher but not significant [ev_crop_yield_boum16_4, ev_crop_yield_boum16_3]. In Ethiopia, the Sustainable Land Management Programme reduced vulnerability to severe drought in treated watersheds against control watersheds, with programme effects three times larger where severe droughts occurred, and buffered moderate droughts significantly on both vegetation measures used [ev_drought_hazard_cons22_1, ev_drought_hazard_cons22_2].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: The same review states that crop yields cannot be sustained during a meteorological drought and different coping mechanisms are required [ev_crop_yield_rock10_2]. The PSNP note adds that vegetation greenness still followed local drought severity, Niger families with soil and water conservation still had an estimated 28 percent deficit in low-rainfall years, and in Tunisia four consecutive drought years limited soil-conservation benefits [ev_drought_hazard_arega24_4, ev_food_security_kabo04_1, ev_drought_hazard_iegtun13_1]. Apart from the water-harvesting meta-analysis, every unit is a bundled programme, pooled soil and water conservation or an expert review, so the share due to water harvesting is not isolated; the Brazilian statement describes potential without data [ev_drought_hazard_castro22_2]. The Ethiopian programme result is measured on remotely sensed vegetation greenness and productivity rather than crop yields, comes from a programme that bundles surface water harvesting with small-scale irrigation, gully rehabilitation, grazing control and reforestation, and under mild drought the buffering showed on the greenness index but not on the productivity measure [ev_drought_hazard_cons22_1, ev_drought_hazard_cons22_3, ev_drought_hazard_cons22_4].

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: Watershed works and production cisterns increase stored water, which improved watershed drought resilience in Ethiopia and can reduce livestock deaths in severe droughts in Brazil [ev_drought_hazard_arega24_4, ev_drought_hazard_castro22_2]. A Burkina Faso review concludes that soil and water conservation techniques helped reduce vulnerability to drought and famine [ev_drought_hazard_sawa11h1_7]. In Ethiopia, the Sustainable Land Management Programme reduced vulnerability to severe drought in treated watersheds against control watersheds, with programme effects three times larger where severe droughts occurred, and buffered moderate droughts significantly on both vegetation measures used [ev_drought_hazard_cons22_1, ev_drought_hazard_cons22_2].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: The Ethiopian public-works study bundles area closures, small-scale irrigation and soil and water conservation, the Brazilian cistern statement is framed as a potential effect, and in Tunisia consecutive drought years limited soil-conservation benefits (no benefit rather than damage) [ev_drought_hazard_iegtun13_1]. That Burkina Faso conclusion is the author's overall judgement, with no measured drought-year contrast behind it [ev_drought_hazard_sawa11h1_7]. The Ethiopian programme result is measured on remotely sensed vegetation greenness and productivity rather than crop yields, comes from a programme that bundles surface water harvesting with small-scale irrigation, gully rehabilitation, grazing control and reforestation, and under mild drought the buffering showed on the greenness index but not on the productivity measure [ev_drought_hazard_cons22_1, ev_drought_hazard_cons22_3, ev_drought_hazard_cons22_4].

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: Watershed programmes combining physical and vegetative barriers, bunds, check dams and terraces reduce runoff and soil loss: runoff dropped by 5 to 18 percent across Indian states, downstream runoff in the Karnataka catchments examined fell by 10 to 22 percent, and Ethiopian public works cut soil loss by 32.2% [ev_runoff_reduction_iegind11_6, ev_runoff_reduction_iegind11_5, ev_erosion_hazard_eth16_4, ev_erosion_hazard_arega24_3].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: All units are bundled programme results measuring runoff or soil loss as proxies for flood impact, several from Bank completion reports or perception surveys, such as 84 percent of Ethiopian respondents reporting reduced run-off [ev_runoff_reduction_eth16_2, ev_erosion_hazard_eth16_4, ev_runoff_reduction_kar20_1]. Effects at watershed scale are small or absent: Karnataka project watersheds cut runoff by 3.2 percent against conventional sites, Uttarakhand sediment yield fell only from 71.6 to 69.3 tons per ha per year, and its water-budget model showed overall surface runoff up 1.5 percent [ev_runoff_reduction_kar20_1, ev_erosion_hazard_utk22_3, ev_runoff_reduction_utk22_4].

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: Across mixed soil and water conservation and water-harvesting programmes, the reported route to lower food insecurity is higher yields and irrigated gardens. A review tabulates significantly increased food security from check dams and infiltration pits in Malawi [ev_food_security_ngur26_1]; Brazilian studies judge production-cistern irrigation of small beds feasible and important for household food security [ev_food_security_castro22_3]; and higher yields are cited as improving food security in Burkina Faso, especially on farms with soil and water conservation on over half of their plots [ev_food_security_sawa11h1_5]. A landscape review of rainwater harvesting across African drylands also rates food security — yields in bad years and the bridging of dry spells — as a benefit with a 'Good' evidence basis [ev_food_security_vohl09_4]. A CILSS regional synthesis adds a further perception survey: in 2005-2006 surveys in Niger, 70 percent of people in villages with natural-resource-management investment reported an improvement in food security, against only 1 percent in control villages [ev_food_security_botreij09_20].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: The size of the gain is limited because the supporting findings are qualitative, cited second-hand and give no size, while the independent evaluations point the other way. In Ethiopia, an impact evaluation of a bundled watershed project found no significant food-security effect for treated households at any participation level [ev_food_security_abate21_4], and public-works participation in communal soil and water investments did not translate into increased food security, possibly because of the short programme [ev_food_security_arega24_1]; both concern mostly off-farm community works. In Niger, families with soil and water conservation produced a surplus of 70 percent in good rainfall years but a deficit of 28 percent in low-rainfall years [ev_food_security_kabo04_1], so benefits may not hold in the dry years that matter most. That rating is the review's own qualitative evaluation across several cited sources, not a single measured contrast [ev_food_security_vohl09_4]. The same synthesis also records a null result: in Burkina Faso's bad 2007 harvest, households in heavily treated villages still bought cereal at the market, 26 kilograms per person on average against 38 kilograms in lightly treated villages, a gap the authors read as the yield advantage not translating into greater food security that year [ev_food_security_botreij09_21].

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: A review reports, second-hand from three cited studies, that the impact of soil and water conservation is especially significant in areas with temperature shocks or lower rainfall [ev_crop_yield_mala24_5].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: This row is data deficient: one narrative statement read second-hand from a review, which does not name specific practices, does not separate heat shocks from low rainfall, gives no magnitude and states no country; no unit measures heat-stress losses directly [ev_crop_yield_mala24_5]. A second independent source or one measured finding is needed before this row can state a direction or size.

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: Pooled across soil and water conservation technologies, large programme evaluations consistently find higher crop yield and production value where farmers have adopted water harvesting. In India, a watershed project raised average rainfed-crop yield by 24% relative to a control group in one phase and by 26% in the next [ev_crop_yield_iegind11_1], and a separate Indian project achieved a 20.8% increase in rainfed-crop productivity attributable to its interventions [ev_crop_yield_utk22_1]. In Ethiopia, early adopters of sustainable land and water management technologies had a 15.2% higher value of production years later [ev_agricultural_production_value_schmidt12_1], and a national impact evaluation found that soil and water conservation on communal land raised crop yields by 9.1% [ev_crop_yield_eth16_1]. In Mauritania, yields in humid watershed zones rose from 0.5 to more than 1.2 tonnes per hectare [ev_crop_yield_mrt14_2]. In Burkina Faso, zaï pits combined with stone lines are credited with sorghum yield increases of over 100%, and maize yield increases of over 100% when the two measures are combined [ev_crop_yield_ngur26_3], and a regional review found soil and water conservation works raising millet yields by 15% to 50% and sorghum yields by 20% to 85% depending on the region, against a considerable decline in cereal yields in control villages [ev_crop_yield_botreij09_1]. A global hydrological model found that expanding rainwater harvesting could raise crop production by 35% at river-basin scale [ev_crop_yield_glen12_9]. A continental model of in situ rainwater harvesting for rainfed maize across Africa finds that, where it steadies yields, the mean potential yield gain is 9 to 39% under the climate of the 1990s, rising to 14–50% by the 2050s depending on the climate model [ev_crop_yield_lebel15_1].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: Some evidence finds harm or no effect, and pooling many technologies together can mask which practice is responsible. A meta-analysis attributed most of its negative-yield observations to in-soil water-harvesting technologies specifically [ev_crop_yield_boum16_2], and in Ethiopia soil and stone bunds reduced crop yield by up to 7% in their first few years after construction [ev_crop_yield_adim16_7]. A separate Ethiopian evaluation found no measurable gain in crop productivity or household income from soil and water conservation promoted mainly for off-farm, community resource protection [ev_crop_yield_abate21_1]. At the extreme end of scale, the same global hydrological model that projected a 35% rise in crop production found this would come with an average 18% reduction in river flows, and a reduction of up to 80% in a single river basin, illustrating the trade-off between on-farm production gains and downstream water availability [ev_crop_yield_glen12_9]. Most of the quantified gains are from low-income countries in the Sahel and East Africa (Burkina Faso, Niger, Ethiopia, Mauritania) and lower-middle-income South Asia (India); the harm and no-effect findings are concentrated in Ethiopia. The Africa-wide maize gain is a model, and its authors judge that rainwater harvesting will likely not protect yields against the more frequent lethal high temperatures expected in the semi-arid tropics [ev_crop_yield_lebel15_1, ev_crop_yield_lebel15_2].

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: Household income and returns from mixed soil and water conservation and water-harvesting programmes have been found to rise, to stay flat and to fall. Gains run through higher yields, irrigation and diversification: a quasi-experimental study found soil and water conservation raised net rice profit in Ghana by a significant 16 per cent [ev_economic_return_mala24_1]; Brazil's production-cistern programme raised family income by about 4.6%, nearly 11% when the top of the income distribution is excluded, with larger effects on farms of 0 to 10 ha [ev_household_income_casag22_1, ev_household_income_casag22_2, ev_household_income_casag22_5]; a review of 311 Indian watershed case studies found a mean benefit-cost ratio of 2.14 and an internal rate of return of 22 percent [ev_economic_return_josh05_1, ev_economic_return_josh05_2]; Mauritanian dikes returned a financial IRR of 24% [ev_economic_return_mrt14_4]; and programme evaluations report income gains of 54% in Karnataka and 58% on the Loess Plateau over control areas [ev_household_income_iegind11_2, ev_household_income_iegchn07_6]. Losses come from costs exceeding gains: in Burkina Faso the yield increase did not cover the annual costs of single SWC measures [ev_economic_return_zoug14_3]; Ethiopian graded fanya juu and graded soil bunds had net present values of −148 and −708 ETB per hectare [ev_economic_return_adim16_4]; and the Brazilian cistern programme's benefit-cost ratio over its evaluation window was 0.0858 [ev_economic_return_casag22_9]. In Ethiopia, agricultural income from crops and livestock was significantly higher for users than non-users of micro- and macro-catchment techniques (cited in a review) [ev_household_income_biaz12_18], and in Tanzania investment in rainwater harvesting for maize, paddy rice and onion was profitable in the long term as long as farmers could afford the initial investment (Senkondo et al. 2004) [ev_economic_return_biaz12_19]. A meta-analysis valuing average maize gains at world prices puts payback of the water-harvesting investment at 4–5 years at the pooled-average gain, not accounting for capital interest [ev_economic_return_boum16_8]. On the loss side, stone rows and grass strips in Burkina Faso were not cost-effective without added nutrients because of high labour, transport and material costs (Zougmoré et al. 2004) [ev_economic_return_biaz12_24]. A landscape review of rainwater harvesting across African drylands rates household income through enhanced yields as a benefit with a 'Good' evidence basis [ev_household_income_vohl09_5].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: What separates the sides, where the evidence says it: farm size, since the Brazilian income effect was a gain on small farms but a loss on farms larger than 10 ha [ev_household_income_casag22_5, ev_household_income_casag22_6]; labour costing and the size of the initial investment, since Ethiopian household benefit-cost ratios were 0.42 to 0.78 at market wages and exceeded one only with a shadow wage and a low initial investment [ev_economic_return_schmidt12_6]; and how long benefits are counted, since the Brazilian ratio covers a short window against a long-lived asset and counts income only [ev_economic_return_casag22_9]. For a Task Team Leader, the practical points are targeting smallholders, costing household labour honestly and expecting returns to arrive over years. The largest gains are from bundled programmes with weak attribution, and the Brazilian income effects are for a cistern bundled with a productive grant and training [ev_household_income_casag22_1]; IEG calls the China income estimate not robust and notes the India gains may partly be construction wages, and a Karnataka completion report doubts its own before/after figures [ev_household_income_iegchn07_6, ev_household_income_iegind11_2, ev_household_income_kar20_3]. The losses and nulls come mostly from independent evaluations, though the Ethiopian values may omit off-site benefits [ev_economic_return_adim16_4], and a Kenyan bundle showed no effect on per capita income [ev_household_income_mala24_2]. A review's report of increased incomes from check dams and infiltration pits in Malawi is qualitative and cited second-hand [ev_household_income_ngur26_1]. Income and returns are proxies for poverty. Location and up-front cost add to the separators: the same meta-analysis puts payback at 2 years for the average Asian farmer but more than 15 years for the average African farmer, whose average maize gain is far smaller [ev_economic_return_boum16_7], the Tanzanian profitability holds only where farmers can afford the initial investment [ev_economic_return_biaz12_19], and the Burkina Faso structures paid only with nutrients added [ev_economic_return_biaz12_24]. The payback periods are modelled from average yields, and the Ethiopian and Tanzanian findings are cited second-hand [ev_economic_return_boum16_8, ev_household_income_biaz12_18]. That rating is the review's own qualitative evaluation across several cited sources, not a single measured contrast [ev_household_income_vohl09_5]. A Niger perception survey adds a weak signal on the poverty side itself: villagers perceived poverty to have decreased in 8 of 12 villages with natural-resource-management interventions, but also in 2 of 4 control villages without one [ev_rural_poverty_botreij09_22].

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: Physical SWC works under public-works and watershed programmes reduce soil loss and downstream runoff, and sediment-control dams with terraces and vegetation trap sediment in the catchment. A meta-analysis of traditional in-situ water harvesting finds soil loss cut by 58.66% and runoff by 53% on average, with soil and stone bunds reducing soil loss by 55.06% and runoff by 49.2% [ev_erosion_hazard_tefe24_1, ev_runoff_reduction_tefe24_1, ev_erosion_hazard_tefe24_4, ev_runoff_reduction_tefe24_5]; in Ethiopian catchments, stone bunds, check dams and vegetation regrowth cut sediment yield from 8.5 to 1.9 t per hectare a year [ev_erosion_hazard_meko14_1, ev_erosion_hazard_meko14_2]. Ethiopian catchment studies cited in a review report physical soil and water conservation decreasing runoff by up to 88% (Taye et al., 2015; Haregeweyn et al., 2015), and integrated catchment management at May Zeg Zeg cutting surface runoff volume by 81% (Nyssen et al., 2010) [ev_runoff_reduction_gebr18_7, ev_runoff_reduction_gebr18_8].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: Nearly all units are programme or lender reports from Ethiopia, India and China, often perception surveys or before/after comparisons; an Uttarakhand water budget showed surface runoff slightly increasing, the Karnataka runoff comparison is against another SWC programme, and IEG doubts the India runoff measurements. Effects mixing runoff and soil-loss metrics are only components of erosion risk. A catchment-restoration meta-analysis in Ethiopia finds minimal effect of catchment treatment on runoff in drought-prone areas with annual rainfall below 500 mm [ev_runoff_reduction_meaza22_3]. The Ethiopian catchment results combine structures with grazing control and vegetation regeneration and are cited in a review, so the share due to the works is not isolated [ev_erosion_hazard_meko14_1]. The 88% and 81% runoff figures are cited second-hand: the first is an upper bound, and the second is a before-and-after result for a catchment-management package rather than the structures alone [ev_runoff_reduction_gebr18_7, ev_runoff_reduction_gebr18_8].

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: Sediment-control dams, terraces and vegetation in a Loess Plateau watershed programme capture sediment each year, reducing the load reaching downstream rivers.
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: Single modelled programme-level estimate from a lender review in China, using sediment retention as a proxy for water quality.

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: Watershed treatment reduces reliance on outside supply: participating villages in India saw reduced water transportation by tanker compared with nonparticipating villages [ev_water_access_deficit_verm19_1], and an agency review credits consumption and production cisterns in semi-arid Brazil with a significant contribution to wider access to water [ev_water_access_deficit_castro22_1]. In India, discharge of springs and streams rose in treated watersheds: a sample study in Himachal Pradesh reports a 40 percent increase in water discharge in spring and stream sources [ev_water_regulation_hp17_1], and the Uttarakhand project achieved an average 21 percent increase in water discharge from perennial water sources in sampled micro-watersheds, against a target of 25 percent [ev_water_regulation_utk22_6]. Measured soil moisture adds a field route: a meta-analysis of in-situ practices finds they improve soil moisture retention by 59%, with soil/stone bunds at an SMD of 76.4% [ev_soil_water_retention_tefe24_1, ev_soil_water_retention_tefe24_3]; in Burkina Faso zaï of 30–40 cm diameter and 1-m half-moons retained moisture for 2-3 weeks through dry spells [ev_soil_water_retention_zour25h1_7]; and Indian project watersheds showed an increase in soil moisture content by 30.5 percent compared to the IWMP sites [ev_soil_water_retention_kar20_2]. Water productivity, the grain produced per unit of rain, is a route by which capture eases water stress. The water-productivity evidence points the same way: FAO compilers list improved water use efficiency among the main benefits of rainwater harvesting, the WOCAT guideline authors find that all water harvesting groups indicate improved water use efficiency, mostly high to medium, through reduced evaporation loss and better soil water availability, and a review sentence, citing earlier work, says capture approaches often lead also to higher water productivity because denser canopies shade the soil [ev_rain_water_productivity_faoslm11_1, ev_rain_water_productivity_wocwh13_1, ev_rain_water_productivity_rock10_1]. A terracing meta-analysis across China also enters here: soil moisture on terraced land was significantly higher on average by 12.4 percent relative to sloping land, with the largest improvement on grassland terraces (28.2 percent) and benefits 28.6 percent higher in semi-humid areas than in semi-arid or humid areas [ev_soil_moisture_chen20_1, ev_soil_moisture_chen20_8, ev_soil_moisture_chen20_9, ev_soil_moisture_chen20_10, ev_soil_moisture_chen20_11, ev_soil_moisture_chen20_12]. A CILSS regional synthesis adds a further recharge observation: in Burkina Faso's Oula department, 21 of 23 villages reported that wells which used to dry up every February and March now hold water year-round since the works were built, which villagers attributed to better recharge of the water table [ev_water_access_deficit_botreij09_19].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: The tanker reduction is a reported programme assessment [ev_water_access_deficit_verm19_1], and the Brazilian unit is an agency inference from census figures in an upper-middle-income context [ev_water_access_deficit_castro22_1]. The Indian spring and stream discharge figures come from World Bank completion reports, the lender's own evaluation, measured before and after without untreated comparison sites, for catchment treatment that bundles plantations, trenches, ponds and check dams with water-harvesting structures, so the gain cannot be credited to water harvesting alone [ev_water_regulation_hp17_1, ev_water_regulation_utk22_6]. Groundwater-recharge evidence, with its limits, now sits in the catchment water yield rows, which also answer what upstream capture does to water downstream. The pooled 59% covers mixed in-situ practices, and the zaï and half-moon result comes with compost in the pits, so neither credits a single structure [ev_soil_water_retention_tefe24_1, ev_soil_water_retention_zour25h1_7]. The Indian soil-moisture comparison is a project-commissioned study of a package of soil and water conservation structures [ev_soil_water_retention_kar20_2]. These are compiler and author judgements across groups, direction only, and the review sentence is second-hand; the WOCAT authors also note that some case studies indicate little to no improvement in water use efficiency [ev_rain_water_productivity_faoslm11_1, ev_rain_water_productivity_wocwh13_1, ev_rain_water_productivity_rock10_1].
