water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: The loss is gradual and can be managed with regular desilting: in Kenya, sand dams lost an estimated 10-25% of storage to silt, which the authors judge is not the main limit on their success [ev_asset_siltation_neuf17_1], while in India desilting has to be repeated during a single programme [ev_asset_siltation_verm19_1]. Several sources tie failure as much to the lack of upkeep as to silt: in Morocco, gabions had nearly lost their function four years after the project ended, with no maintenance system [ev_erosion_hazard_iegmar09_2], and check-dam benefits fade as the dams fill [ev_sediment_retention_luca21_1_av]. Many findings are cited second-hand and the Indian tank finding is a model [ev_climate_shock_mass14_4]. The silt comes from erosion upstream, so the threat depends on the wider catchment.

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: WOCAT compilers rate check dams in China and Nepal and sand dams in Kenya as coping well with local windstorms and gabion check dams in Somalia as coping moderately, while fascine (vegetative) check dams in Madagascar are rated as not coping well with tropical storms [ev_asset_wind_cyclone_wocat_1455_2011_local_windstorm, ev_asset_wind_cyclone_wocat_1537_2012_local_windstorm, ev_asset_wind_cyclone_wocat_7778_2026_local_windstorm, ev_asset_wind_cyclone_wocat_6478_2022_tropical_storm].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: All units are practitioner ratings without observed damage; the Madagascar sheet alone rates tropical storms, and it concerns a vegetative structure rather than stone or concrete [ev_asset_wind_cyclone_wocat_6478_2022_tropical_storm].

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: Water held by runoff structures supports plant growth and habitat around them: the WOCAT compiler for gabions and rock check dams in Somalia reports that improved soil moisture and reduced erosion supported the growth of different plant and grass species, and that the restored vegetation and water created better conditions for livestock and small wildlife [ev_biodiversity_outcome_wocat_7778_2026_plant_diversity, ev_biodiversity_outcome_wocat_7778_2026_habitat_diversity, ev_biodiversity_outcome_wocat_7778_2026_animal_diversity]. Users of small reservoirs in Ghana perceive greener surroundings and improved biodiversity [ev_biodiversity_outcome_veno12_1]. Embrapa reports that crops, vegetable gardens and orchards on the humid fringes of its barraginhas in Brazil bring back fauna that had disappeared for lack of food [ev_biodiversity_outcome_mira19_3].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: The gain is slight: the compiler units all come from a single Somali technology sheet and are mostly rated as slight change, the Ghana unit is a user perception, and no unit measures species or habitat [ev_biodiversity_outcome_wocat_7778_2026_animal_diversity, ev_biodiversity_outcome_veno12_1]. The Brazilian barraginha fauna finding is an adopter-reported indicator in Embrapa's self-assessment of its own technology, with no species measured [ev_biodiversity_outcome_mira19_3].

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: In Somalia, a water-harvesting project reported that improved vegetation growth increased above-ground biomass and contributed slightly to carbon storage, and that vegetation recovery helped store more carbon by absorbing carbon dioxide from the atmosphere while reduced land degradation lowered the release of stored carbon [ev_carbon_sequestration_wocat_7778_2026_biomass_above_ground_C, ev_carbon_sequestration_wocat_7778_2026_emission_of_carbon_and_greenhouse_gases].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: In the Canary Islands, organic carbon under gavias runoff-harvesting fields was higher than adjacent uncultivated soil, but the difference across the sampled plots (n = 40–41) was not statistically significant [ev_soil_organic_carbon_roose17_2], which is consistent with this family's class being only slight.

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: Check dams, sand dams and runoff-harvesting structures capture surface water that would otherwise run off, so it percolates into the ground and raises local groundwater. In India, floodwater-recession tanks recharged on average 61% of the water budget to percolation, and check dams were found to recharge an additional 33 millimetres of water across their catchment in an average year and 17 millimetres in a dry year [ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_mass14_1, ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_dash17_1]. Sand dams in Burkina Faso and Kenya are similarly credited with recharging groundwater and supplying wells for domestic use and irrigation [ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_foxr03_8, ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_biaz12_27], and sand dams more generally can raise local groundwater, though the extent of the effect is often limited in space and time [ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_ritc21_1].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: The same capture of water that recharges groundwater locally also reduces the water flowing downstream, and several studies measure this as a harm to catchment water yield. In India, a water-balance study estimated that increased rainwater harvesting at watershed scale would cut runoff by about 60% while increasing recharge by only 5% [ev_water_yield_glen12_2], and other analyses there found that even a small share of catchment area under rainwater harvesting sharply reduced the mean runoff coefficient, the share of rainfall converted to streamflow [ev_water_yield_glen09_1]. On China's Loess Plateau, decades of check-dam construction are credited with reducing streamflow by approximately 39% [ev_water_yield_luca21_1]. In Ethiopia, modelling under a high sand-dam development strategy and an extreme climate-change scenario found low-flow months rising from 18.2% of the period to 22.7% and 27.3% in two of those months, and the share of river discharge stored in sand dams in the first rainy season rising to 19.9%, compared with 9.3% under the historical reference period [ev_water_yield_lasa13_4, ev_water_yield_lasa13_5]; under a more moderate strategy with 613 sand dams, the same Ethiopian study found no change in low-flow occurrence [ev_water_yield_lasa13_3]. A separate theoretical modelling study concluded that the impact of rainwater harvesting on watershed water levels may be minimal beyond the immediate vicinity of the structure [ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_glen12_8]. Whether a project nets out as a local groundwater gain or a downstream water-yield loss depends on the scale of implementation, a few structures versus watershed-wide development, and on where the account is drawn: the same captured water that recharges a well nearby is water that no longer reaches the river. Most of the quantified harm evidence comes from India, China and Ethiopia; this is the distinction, used elsewhere in this tool, between a benefit to the adopting farm and an effect on people downstream.

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: The runoff-catchment per-hectare cost comes from one Somali WOCAT sheet on gully erosion control with gabions and rock structures, whose costed items total 23568.70 USD spread over a treated area of 160 ha [ev_project_cost_wocat_7778_2026_establishment].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: This row is data deficient: a single compiler cost table for a project-built gully-control package, spread over the whole treated area rather than the structures alone and converted at the sheet's own rate [ev_project_cost_wocat_7778_2026_establishment]. A second independent cost source is needed before the per-hectare figure can be read as typical.

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: The unit reports how often rehabilitated small dams in Ghana came in under per-irrigated-hectare cost thresholds, comparing the government irrigation authority with donor and NGO implementers.
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: This is a cost distribution by implementer for reservoir rehabilitation, not a measured cost reduction from water harvesting; treat it as context on rehabilitation cost variability.

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: Farm ponds that capture and store runoff let farmers irrigate through dry spells. In northern Burkina Faso, a cement-lined pond supplying supplemental irrigation raised sorghum grain yield from 443 to 680 kg per hectare in 1999 and from 634 to 1138 kg per hectare in 2000 [ev_crop_yield_foxr03_4, ev_crop_yield_foxr03_5]. In eastern Kenya, sand dams across seasonal riverbeds store rainy-season runoff as groundwater in the sand: households without a dam saw their income fall by 38,056 Kenyan shillings a year, while households with a dam maintained or grew their income by 27,241 shillings — a difference of 65,297 shillings in a dry year, against an investment of about $35 per capita [ev_household_income_pauw08_1].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: The same catchment approach can still fail outright: in a different part of eastern Kenya, a season classified as a complete drought produced no harvestable runoff for a farm pond's supplemental irrigation, and biomass and grain yields showed no significant difference between treatments [ev_crop_yield_barr05_5]. In Cambodia, by contrast, a pond was reported to provide enough water even during drought [ev_drought_hazard_wocat_2844_2017_drought_impacts].

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: Farm ponds that capture and store runoff let farmers irrigate through dry spells. In northern Burkina Faso, a cement-lined pond supplying supplemental irrigation raised sorghum grain yield from 443 to 680 kg per hectare in 1999 and from 634 to 1138 kg per hectare in 2000 [ev_crop_yield_foxr03_4, ev_crop_yield_foxr03_5]. In the Canary Islands, the 'gavias' runoff-harvesting system was found to store nearly 350 mm of water in the top metre of soil even in the driest years, when rainfall was below 100 mm [ev_soil_moisture_roose17_3].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: The same catchment approach can still fail outright: in eastern Kenya, a season classified as a complete drought produced no harvestable runoff for a farm pond's supplemental irrigation, and biomass and grain yields showed no significant difference between treatments [ev_crop_yield_barr05_5]. In Cambodia, by contrast, a pond was reported to provide enough water even during drought [ev_drought_hazard_wocat_2844_2017_drought_impacts].

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: Runoff-fed storage carries water into dry periods: pond water used as supplemental irrigation reduces crop-loss risk in irregular years in semi-arid Brazil, cisterns catching runoff on China's Loess Plateau are credited with mitigating frequent drought, and a review of small reservoirs counts improved drought resilience among their cited benefits [ev_drought_hazard_brito07_10, ev_drought_hazard_iegchn07_4, ev_drought_hazard_saru19_1]. WOCAT compilers for a pond in Cambodia and check dams in Somalia rate drought impacts as reduced, the Cambodian sheet noting the pond provides enough water even during drought and the Somali sheet crediting improved soil moisture retention and infiltration [ev_drought_hazard_wocat_2844_2017_drought_impacts, ev_drought_hazard_wocat_7778_2026_drought_impacts]. Stored water bridges dry spells: a water-harvesting review cites supplemental irrigation of 50–200 mm bridging critical dry spells and stabilising yields, and rainwater management is cited as letting producers avoid total crop loss in critical drought periods [ev_yield_stability_rock10_1, ev_crop_yield_silv26_2]. Indian farmers reported a 6% chance of rainy-season crop failure from aberrant rains with a farm pond against 20% in the same crop–tree–livestock system without a pond [ev_yield_stability_pals23_1]. In Zimbabwe the months water could be collected at sand-dam sites in a drought year rose from 5.8 before construction to 9.7 after [ev_water_access_deficit_lazurko24_1]. In Kenya's Kitui District, households with a sand dam saw the value of their rain-fed harvest rise by an average of 10,329 KSh a year in a drought year while households without a dam saw it fall by 39,489 KSh, which the authors link to a raised water table and the ability to apply a little irrigation during dry spells [ev_crop_yield_pauw08_1]. The same comparison found calculated household income held up or rose by 27,241 KSh a year for dam households against a fall of 38,056 KSh for those without — a difference of 65,297 KSh in that dry year [ev_household_income_pauw08_1]. In Brazil, Embrapa describes its barraginhas, small semicircular runoff-retention basins dug along runoff paths, as easing the effects of droughts on crops in the lowlands [ev_drought_hazard_mira19_8]. In Kahinda and colleagues' crop model of a rock-catchment system in semi-arid Zimbabwe, supplemental irrigation from the harvested water cut the risk of complete maize crop failure from 20% to 7% on average, and in seasons with intense intra-seasonal dry spells every treatment without supplemental irrigation failed completely while the irrigated crop kept a minimum reliable yield [ev_yield_stability_kahi07_2, ev_crop_yield_kahi07_4]. In Glendenning's water-balance model of the Arvari catchment in Rajasthan, where community structures store monsoon runoff that recharges the shallow aquifer pumped for irrigation, harvesting decreased the impacts of short-term mild drought, and over runs of consecutive below-average rainfall years the sustainability of groundwater-fed irrigation declined less than without harvesting [ev_drought_hazard_glen09_2, ev_drought_hazard_glen09_3].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: Storage is exhausted in prolonged drought: Brazilian subsurface dams tended to dry out in a rainless year and small ones do not withstand long droughts, a benefit shortfall rather than damage to the works [ev_drought_hazard_cirilo03_2, ev_drought_hazard_cirilo03_3]. The Loess Plateau claim is a qualitative assertion, the reservoir finding a vote count and the Brazilian pond statement an institutional assertion without data, and the Cambodian and Somali units are compiler ratings [ev_drought_hazard_iegchn07_4, ev_drought_hazard_saru19_1, ev_drought_hazard_brito07_10]. The supplemental-irrigation and crop-loss statements are secondary citations in reviews, the Indian pond figures come from a farmer survey reported in a preprint, and the Zimbabwe sand-dam figure rests on recall-based before-and-after interviews [ev_yield_stability_rock10_1, ev_crop_yield_silv26_2, ev_yield_stability_pals23_1, ev_water_access_deficit_lazurko24_1]. The Kitui sand-dam crop and income results are a cross-sectional household survey with multi-year recall rather than a randomised comparison; dams were not placed at random, dam households also applied more terracing, bunds and grass lines whose effect cannot be separated, and 'value of harvest' and 'calculated income' are price-based proxies rather than measured tonnage [ev_crop_yield_pauw08_1, ev_household_income_pauw08_1]. The barraginha statement is Embrapa's self-assessment of its own technology, with no measured drought contrast and no normal-year reference [ev_drought_hazard_mira19_8]. The Zimbabwe crop-failure and dry-spell results are crop-model outputs, not field measurements, and they are a bundle: runoff capture and storage are the water-harvesting part, but the yield is delivered through supplemental irrigation, so these units are discounted rather than credited in full to water harvesting [ev_yield_stability_kahi07_2, ev_crop_yield_kahi07_4]. The Arvari drought results are model outputs too; the buffer is described for short-term mild drought and as only some buffer over longer runs of dry years, and the same model shows that as harvesting increases, downstream flow decreases [ev_drought_hazard_glen09_2, ev_drought_hazard_glen09_3].

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: Ponds, cisterns and check dams store runoff for use in dry periods: pond water used as supplemental irrigation reduces crop-loss risk in irregular years in semi-arid Brazil, cisterns in China are reported to be mitigating frequent periods of drought, a review of small reservoirs counts improved drought resilience among their cited benefits, and the compiler of a Cambodian on-farm pond sheet states the pond provides enough water even during drought [ev_drought_hazard_brito07_10, ev_drought_hazard_iegchn07_4, ev_drought_hazard_saru19_1, ev_drought_hazard_wocat_2844_2017_drought_impacts]. The WOCAT compiler for gabions and rock check dams in Somalia likewise judges drought impacts reduced, citing improved soil moisture retention and water infiltration [ev_drought_hazard_wocat_7778_2026_drought_impacts]. In a Kenyan catchment with sand dams the number of people exposed to droughts fell from 420 to 0 while a control catchment stayed at 600 [ev_drought_hazard_lasage08_1]. In Brazil, Embrapa describes its barraginhas, small semicircular runoff-retention basins dug along runoff paths in pastures and croplands, as storing water in the soil by infiltration and easing the effects of droughts on crops in the lowlands [ev_drought_hazard_mira19_8]. A Burkina Faso risk analysis of a farm reservoir used for supplemental irrigation finds that all of the mild dry spells can be mitigated, which explains the more frequent zero-stress seasons under irrigation than in the control, and that severe dry spells late in the season are partly mitigated, turned into mild ones [ev_drought_hazard_fox05_7, ev_drought_hazard_fox05_6]. In Glendenning's water-balance model of the Arvari catchment in Rajasthan, where community structures store monsoon runoff that recharges the shallow aquifer pumped for irrigation, harvesting decreased the impacts of short-term mild drought, and over runs of consecutive below-average rainfall years the sustainability of groundwater-fed irrigation declined less than without harvesting [ev_drought_hazard_glen09_2, ev_drought_hazard_glen09_3].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: The class is held at moderate because few of the benefit units say how big the effect is. Most of the pool is practitioner judgements and assertions without drought-loss metrics: an expert account from Brazil, a lender evaluation in China, compiler ratings from Cambodia and Somalia, and a review that counts how often small-reservoir studies cite improved drought resilience; only a Kenyan sand-dam catchment table compares people exposed to droughts against a control catchment, and its values are likely interview-derived [ev_drought_hazard_lasage08_1]. Subsurface dams in Brazil tended to dry out in a rainless year and small ones do not withstand long dry spells, which records no benefit when storage is exhausted rather than damage to the works [ev_drought_hazard_cirilo03_2, ev_drought_hazard_cirilo03_3]. The barraginha statement is Embrapa's self-assessment of its own technology, with no measured drought contrast and no normal-year reference [ev_drought_hazard_mira19_8]. The Burkina Faso analysis marks the limit of storage: a drought year, with a probability of 0.1, cannot be mitigated because there is insufficient water to harvest, and the late severe dry spells need at least three irrigation applications while the reservoir supports only two [ev_drought_hazard_fox05_5, ev_drought_hazard_fox05_6]. The Arvari drought results are model outputs too; the buffer is described for short-term mild drought and as only some buffer over longer runs of dry years, and the same model shows that as harvesting increases, downstream flow decreases [ev_drought_hazard_glen09_2, ev_drought_hazard_glen09_3].

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: Pooled costs are construction costs per structure: village ponds or tanks and dry-stone check dams (per cubic metre of masonry) from a World Bank watershed project in Himachal Pradesh, India, and compiler-reported WOCAT establishment costs for a farm pond with irrigation system in Cambodia, a set of check dams and walls in India, a fascine line in Madagascar and a haffir in Somalia. In Ethiopia, cited second-hand, sand dam construction costs about 12,000 US dollars per dam [ev_project_cost_lasa13_6].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: The project figures are self-reported from monitoring in nominal rupees and the WOCAT figures are each compiler's own cost table converted with the sheet's exchange rate; none are market prices. The structures range from a fascine line of a few metres to a haffir of about 5100 square metres, and the per-cubic-metre figure is per volume of masonry built, not water stored, so the cost class should be read with that spread of denominators in mind. The Ethiopian sand-dam figure is a second-hand citation with no stated currency year, and a dam-based unit cost is not directly comparable to the pooled pond, check-dam and line-structure figures already in this row [ev_project_cost_lasa13_6].

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: The WOCAT compiler for stone check walls and check dams in India rates fire risk as decreased, but the sheet gives no explanation of how the structures would do this [ev_fire_hazard_wocat_5210_2019_fire_risk]. Part of any such effect would be off-site, at landscape scale rather than on the adopting farm.
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: This row is data deficient: a single practitioner rating with no stated mechanism and no measurement, for one Indian technology [ev_fire_hazard_wocat_5210_2019_fire_risk]. A second independent source or one measured finding is needed before this row can state a direction or size.

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: Small dams, check dams and treated gullies hold back and slow floodwater, giving a moderate reduction in flood impact downstream. Check dams cut flooding and peak flow in Iran and withstood strong floods in Italian mountain torrents [ev_flood_hazard_luca21_1, ev_flood_hazard_luca21_2]. Small dams in Morocco damped the damage of serious floods in 2002-2003 [ev_flood_hazard_roos10_1], treated ravine floors in Haiti slowed cyclone floods and protected towns below [ev_flood_hazard_roose17_2], and Brazilian barraginhas (small runoff basins) are described as easing floods [ev_flood_hazard_mira19_7]. Users of small reservoirs in Ghana see flood control as a major benefit [ev_flood_hazard_veno12_1], and practitioners in Kenya, Ethiopia and Somalia rate their dams, check dams and gabions as reducing floods [ev_flood_hazard_wocat_1537_2012_flood_impacts, ev_flood_hazard_wocat_6716_2023_flood_impacts, ev_flood_hazard_wocat_7778_2026_flood_impacts].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: The benefit depends on design and scale: a review warns that larger sand dams raise the risk of flooding, erosion and seepage [ev_flood_hazard_ritc21_1], and check dams had little effect against extreme floods, especially when badly designed or not maintained [ev_flood_hazard_luca21_3]. None of these findings measures flood levels before and after: they are second-hand findings, expert statements, a user survey and practitioner ratings. Much of the benefit falls downstream rather than on the farm that builds the works.

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: Dams, check dams and buffer structures slow and store floodwater before it reaches downstream farms and channels. A global review of check-dam literature reports check dams mitigating flooding and significantly reducing peak flow in Iran, and artificial sequences of check dams in the northern Italian Alps successfully withstanding flood events with return periods of about 7 to 25 years [ev_flood_hazard_luca21_1, ev_flood_hazard_luca21_2]. In Morocco, small dams played an important role in damping the damage that the serious floods of 2002-2003 at Mohammedia, Berrechid and Settat could otherwise have caused [ev_flood_hazard_roos10_1]. WOCAT compilers report the same pattern for specific structures: a Kenyan sand dam reduces flooding downstream of the dam by creating a buffer, an Ethiopian double-basin masonry check dam reduces the speed and impacts of flooding on the rehabilitated area, and Somali stone lines, gabions and rock check dams reduced runoff velocity and minimised flood-related soil erosion and gully expansion [ev_flood_hazard_wocat_1537_2012_flood_impacts, ev_flood_hazard_wocat_6716_2023_flood_impacts, ev_flood_hazard_wocat_7778_2026_flood_impacts]. Users themselves perceive the benefit: in a review of small reservoirs in Sub-Saharan Africa, farmers in northern Ghana named limiting floods during the rainy season among the major benefits [ev_flood_hazard_veno12_1]. In Germany, small dry detention ponds at field borders lowered peak runoff leaving the field by a factor of three [ev_flood_hazard_fien05_1].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: The benefit is not universal and depends on design, scale and maintenance. A review warns that larger sand dams built to maximise water storage increase the risk of flooding, erosion and seepage [ev_flood_hazard_ritc21_1], and the same check-dam review found check dams had only a minimal effect against extreme floods, especially where structures were ill-designed or not properly maintained [ev_flood_hazard_luca21_3]. Much of this evidence is about large, engineered mountain-torrent or river structures (Iran, Italy, Austria) rather than small farm-scale works, and part of the benefit is off-site — it arrives downstream of the structure rather than on the adopting farm. The Moroccan account is a technique-manual synthesis without a measured reduction figure, and the Ghanaian finding is a user perception, not a flow measurement [ev_flood_hazard_roos10_1, ev_flood_hazard_veno12_1]. The WOCAT entries are compiler ratings rather than hydrograph measurements, and the German pond's own authors describe its effect as untested beyond the flood sizes observed during the monitoring period [ev_flood_hazard_fien05_1].

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: For runoff-catchment works in mixed crop-livestock areas the evidence points to a small benefit, lower than the moderate rating for these works overall, and only 2 papers name this farming system. Treated ravine floors in Haiti slowed floods during cyclone storms and protected the plains and towns below [ev_flood_hazard_roose17_2], and Brazilian barraginhas (small runoff basins) are described as easing floods for low-lying fields [ev_flood_hazard_mira19_7].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: Both findings are authors' statements without a size or a measured comparison [ev_flood_hazard_roose17_2, ev_flood_hazard_mira19_7]. There is no evidence for severe or extreme floods. The benefit falls mostly downstream rather than on the farm that builds the works.

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: Small dams, check dams and treated gullies hold back and slow floodwater, giving a moderate reduction in flooding downstream. Check dams cut flooding and peak flow in Iran and withstood strong floods in Italian mountain torrents [ev_flood_hazard_luca21_1, ev_flood_hazard_luca21_2]. Small dams in Morocco damped the damage of serious floods in 2002-2003 [ev_flood_hazard_roos10_1], treated ravine floors in Haiti slowed cyclone floods and protected towns below [ev_flood_hazard_roose17_2], and Brazilian barraginhas (small runoff basins) are described as easing floods [ev_flood_hazard_mira19_7]. Users of small reservoirs in Ghana see flood control as a major benefit [ev_flood_hazard_veno12_1], and practitioners in Kenya, Ethiopia and Somalia rate their works as reducing floods [ev_flood_hazard_wocat_1537_2012_flood_impacts, ev_flood_hazard_wocat_6716_2023_flood_impacts, ev_flood_hazard_wocat_7778_2026_flood_impacts].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: The benefit depends on design and scale: a review warns that larger sand dams raise the risk of flooding, erosion and seepage [ev_flood_hazard_ritc21_1], and check dams had little effect against extreme floods, especially when badly designed or not maintained [ev_flood_hazard_luca21_3]. None of these findings measures flood levels before and after: they are second-hand findings, expert statements, a user survey and practitioner ratings.

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: Ponds, cisterns, subsurface dams and gully check dams store runoff for gardens, crops and livestock, widening diets and carrying households through the lean season. In Brazil, subsurface dams gave families more fruit and vegetables and more food overall, production cisterns allow daily garden irrigation, and adopters of small catchment basins rated food security as the technology's largest impact [ev_food_security_cirilo03_6, ev_food_security_arsky20_6, ev_food_security_mira19_2]. In Burkina Faso, runoff cisterns irrigate gardens and water livestock in the lean season, and adopters of rainwater-harvesting ponds showed statistically significant improvements in food-security indicators [ev_food_security_roose94_1, ev_food_security_silv26_1]; Biazin et al. cite Desta (2004) for Ethiopian farmers who adopted rainwater-harvesting irrigation properly having improved their dietary status [ev_food_security_biaz12_26], and a review counts 15 citations for improved food security [ev_food_security_saru19_1]. WOCAT compilers add that farm ponds in Cambodia keep enough water for irrigation during drought, gully check dams in Ethiopia open more rangeland for pastoralists' livestock, and gully rehabilitation in Somalia improved household food availability [ev_food_security_wocat_2844_2017_risk_of_production_failure, ev_food_security_wocat_6716_2023_food_security_selfsufficiency, ev_food_security_wocat_7778_2026_food_security_selfsufficiency].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: The literature is mostly qualitative, cited in reviews or vote counts, and gives no size of effect; much of it comes from upper-middle-income Brazil, including Embrapa's own assessment and programme reviews, so transfer to low-income settings is adjacent rather than direct [ev_food_security_mira19_2, ev_food_security_arsky20_6, ev_food_security_saru19_1, ev_food_security_silv26_1]. The Ethiopian dietary finding is a secondary citation, and the rainwater-harvesting irrigation it describes uses stored water to irrigate, at the boundary between water harvesting and irrigation [ev_food_security_biaz12_26]. The WOCAT units are practitioner judgements, and the Ethiopian gully sheet rates only a slight gain, which works through more rangeland for grazing rather than crop supply [ev_food_security_wocat_6716_2023_food_security_selfsufficiency].

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: Farm ponds that store runoff for supplemental irrigation raise yield especially when paired with fertiliser. In northern Burkina Faso, control grain yield averaged 455 kg per hectare over three years; supplemental irrigation alone raised it to 712 kg per hectare, fertiliser alone to 975 kg per hectare, and the two combined to 1403 kg per hectare — more than three times the farmer's normal yield [ev_crop_yield_foxr03_1]. The same pond raised sorghum yield from 443 to 680 kg per hectare in a 1999 dry-spell season and from 634 to 1138 kg per hectare in 2000 [ev_crop_yield_foxr03_4].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: The benefit depends on the season and on fertiliser, not water alone: in a year with well-distributed rainfall, irrigated and non-irrigated plots showed no significant yield difference, and fertiliser, not the stored water, drove the gain that year [ev_crop_yield_foxr03_3]. In eastern Kenya, supplemental irrigation combined with fertiliser helped most in poor rainfall seasons (below 300 mm) but had no or slightly negative effects in good rainfall seasons (above 350 mm), compared with fertiliser alone [ev_crop_yield_barr05_7]. In Tigray, irrigation from government-supported water-harvesting schemes was found to be risk-increasing on its own, becoming risk-reducing only in combination with improved seeds and fertiliser [ev_yield_stability_kato11_8]. Measured harm (maladaptation) — the practice worsening this outcome for some adopters — appears in 2 sources.

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: Pooled costs are compiler-reported annual maintenance costs from WOCAT technology sheets: per structure for a farm pond with irrigation system in Cambodia, check dams and walls in India, a fascine line in Madagascar and a haffir in Somalia, and per hectare for sheets in India and Somalia (the Somalia sheet spreading its total over 160 ha).
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: WOCAT figures are the compiler's own cost tables for the documented technology, summed and converted to USD with the sheet's own exchange rate; they are not market prices. The cost class is set from the per-structure figures while the value range is per hectare, and structures range from a short fascine line to a large haffir, so neither summary is a comparable unit cost.

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: Small reservoirs, sand dams, farm ponds, runoff cisterns and subsurface dams provide water for dry-season irrigation of vegetables and fruit and for livestock, shifting cropping towards higher-value crops and raising household income [ev_household_income_veno12_2, ev_household_income_ritc21_3]. In Kenya, farmers living near sand dams saw average income rise by 60% as more water in dry periods raised farm yields [ev_household_income_lasage08_1]. In the same Kitui, Kenya sand-dam district, a separate household survey found calculated income held up or rose by 27,241 KSh a year for dam households against a fall of 38,056 KSh for those without — a difference of 65,297 KSh in a drought year [ev_household_income_pauw08_1]. Reviews add that rainwater-harvesting ponds brought statistically significant gains in household income in Burkina Faso, water storage gave Ethiopian smallholders greater income security, harvested water used with precision irrigation in Ethiopia reached a net water value of up to 1.53 USD per cubic metre, and benefit-cost ratios reached up to 3.38 with payback periods of 6.8 to 12 years; Indian farms with a farm pond reported net returns of 857 USD per hectare against 586 without [ev_household_income_silv26_1, ev_household_income_silv26_2, ev_economic_return_silv26_1, ev_economic_return_silv26_2, ev_economic_return_pals23_1]. In Brazil, an Embrapa survey of some communities found small-farm incomes rose by about half a minimum wage per month after the second filling of the barraginhas [ev_household_income_mira19_1]. The Cambodian pond compiler rates farm income up because every crop yielded well once there was enough irrigation water [ev_household_income_wocat_2844_2017_farm_income]. Returns on stored runoff can be high: farm-pond supplemental irrigation of maize in Kenya gave net seasonal revenue of US$ 150 and could raise the annual return by 150% (Ngigi et al. 2005), road-catchment harvesting for paddy in Tanzania returned more than US$ 12 per person-day against US$ 3.7 for rainfed sorghum (Hatibu et al. 2006), and a Peruvian programme building 31 cochas returned 1.96 soles per sol invested (Tafur, cited in a programme review) [ev_economic_return_biaz12_20, ev_economic_return_biaz12_21, ev_economic_return_card22_1]. A Burkina Faso and Kenya model puts net profit from water harvesting with supplemental irrigation, fertiliser and an off-season tomato crop at 151–626 USD per hectare a year in Burkina Faso and 109–477 in Kenya, against at most 15 and 40–130 under current practice [ev_economic_return_fox05_3, ev_economic_return_fox05_4]. In Pakistan, maize irrigated from harvested rainwater earned 0.28 US$ net per cubic metre in the first year, with a cumulative benefit-cost ratio projected at 2.02 by the second year and 3.53 by the third, and fish farming in a farm pond earned US$ 1799 net on average, about US$ 2951 in mini-dams [ev_economic_return_waqa25_5, ev_household_income_waqa25_7]. In Rajasthan, India, modelled recharge from check dams was estimated sufficient to irrigate part of the winter crop area and judged responsible for 16 percent of farm income [ev_household_income_dash17_3].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: Most literature magnitudes are secondary citations in reviews or vote counts [ev_household_income_saru19_3, ev_household_income_veno12_3]. Sand dams are judged likely not cost-efficient for water supply, Brazilian subsurface dams produced little cash income where electricity, investment capital or an irrigation tradition were missing, and the high Brazilian benefit-cost ratios come from an upper-middle-income context [ev_economic_return_ritc21_1, ev_household_income_cirilo03_7, ev_economic_return_cirilo03_10]. The Kenyan sand-dam income rise compares a small sample of households with a control catchment [ev_household_income_lasage08_1]; the reviewed figures are reported at their upper end, the Indian pond returns come from a cross-sectional survey confounded by farm size and assets [ev_economic_return_silv26_2, ev_economic_return_pals23_1], and the barraginha income finding is Embrapa's self-assessment of its own technology from an informal survey [ev_household_income_mira19_1]. Income and returns are proxies for poverty. The returns hinge on what the water is used for and on inputs: in the Burkina Faso model the yield gain from supplemental irrigation alone does not compensate for the labour and capital invested [ev_economic_return_fox05_2], and in Pakistan pearl millet irrigated from harvested rainwater lost 0.27 US$ per cubic metre in the first year and stayed below break-even by the third [ev_economic_return_waqa25_6]. The Kenyan, Tanzanian and Peruvian returns are second-hand citations, the model profits rely on a high-value tomato crop and vary with the cost put on labour, and the Pakistani figures are projections assuming constant prices and water productivity [ev_economic_return_biaz12_20, ev_economic_return_card22_1, ev_economic_return_fox05_3, ev_economic_return_waqa25_5]. That figure is a calculation from estimated irrigable area rather than a measured income contrast, and is bundled with the well-pumping the recharge supplies [ev_household_income_dash17_3]. In a separate Ethiopian sand-dam catchment, a household survey found no clear difference in economic situation between households with and without dam access, though the authors attribute the weak contrast partly to the small number of dam-linked households surveyed [ev_household_income_lasa13_2]. The Kitui income comparison is a cross-sectional household survey with multi-year recall rather than a randomised comparison; dams were not placed at random, and dam households also applied more terracing, bunds and grass lines whose effect cannot be separated from the dam's own [ev_household_income_pauw08_1].

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: Check dams and hill reservoirs cut both runoff and the sediment it carries. On China's Loess Plateau, a decades-long check-dam campaign was found to have reduced runoff and sediment by about 15% and 85% respectively, and streamflow by about 39% [ev_runoff_reduction_luca21_2], while separately reducing erosion rates from more than 200 tonnes per hectare per year to 20–25 tonnes per hectare per year [ev_erosion_hazard_luca21_1]. In Tunisia, earth bench-bunds (banquettes) were found to retain 85 mm of runoff, enough to hold back all the rain in a normal year, cutting downstream flows by 17% and hill-reservoir inflows by 13% [ev_runoff_reduction_roose06_4].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: Not every check dam performs as well: in Haiti, a review found most gabion check dams built by other projects had no large or lasting effect on either agricultural production or gullying, attributing this to poor construction [ev_erosion_hazard_roose17_5]. Measured harm (maladaptation) — the practice worsening this outcome for some adopters — appears in 2 sources.

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: On China's Loess Plateau, a decades-long check-dam campaign was found to have reduced sediment by about 85% and runoff by about 15%, and streamflow by about 39% [ev_sediment_retention_luca21_1]; in the Wuding River watershed, simulations found check dams cutting runoff by 12% and sediment by 11.7% [ev_sediment_retention_shi19_2]. In Arizona, loose-rock check dams produced a twofold decline in sediment yield at the watershed outlet compared with an untreated watershed [ev_sediment_retention_poly14_2].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: The evidence here comes mostly from large engineered check-dam systems in China and the United States, so the size of the benefit may not transfer to smaller, less engineered runoff-catchment structures.

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: Farm ponds and sand dams raise water available for both crops and households. In northern Burkina Faso, reservoirs built for crop irrigation were also found to serve livestock and household needs during periods of domestic water scarcity [ev_water_access_deficit_foxr03_7]. In eastern Kenya, rain-and-irrigation water-use efficiency rose from 2.1 to 4.1 kilograms of grain per millimetre per hectare between the lowest and highest supplemental-irrigation treatments [ev_rain_water_productivity_barr05_9], and in Zimbabwe, a modelled rainwater-harvesting system with a rock catchment and infiltration pits found supplemental irrigation alone raising water productivity by 22% on average, from 1.75 to 2.13 kilograms per cubic metre [ev_rain_water_productivity_kahi07_1].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: The size of a sand dam limits how many people it can serve: in Kenya, at a consumption rate of 15 litres per person per day, a median-sized dam was found to support between 37 and 84 people for a four-month period, with only 57% of dams holding enough water to supply their reported number of beneficiaries for that long [ev_water_access_deficit_neuf17_1]. In a separate Burkina Faso trial, water-use efficiency showed no difference between irrigated and non-irrigated or fertilised and non-fertilised treatments in a well-distributed rainfall year [ev_rain_water_productivity_foxr03_6].

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: WOCAT compilers for gully plugging with check dams in Nepal, stone check walls and check dams in India and a masonry check dam in Ethiopia rate drainage of excess water as improved [ev_waterlogging_hazard_wocat_1493_2011_excess_water_drainage, ev_waterlogging_hazard_wocat_5210_2019_excess_water_drainage, ev_waterlogging_hazard_wocat_6716_2023_excess_water_drainage].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: All units are practitioner ratings with no stated reasoning or measurement, and the Chinese check-dam and Indian farm-pond sheets rate drainage as unchanged [ev_waterlogging_hazard_wocat_1455_2011_excess_water_drainage, ev_waterlogging_hazard_wocat_1474_2011_excess_water_drainage].

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: WOCAT compilers for check dams in India and for stone lines, gabions and rock check dams in Somalia rate the impacts of cyclones and rain storms as reduced, the Somali compiler noting the structures stabilised the landscape and reduced damage from intense rainfall and stormwater runoff [ev_wind_cyclone_hazard_wocat_5210_2019_impacts_of_cyclones_rain_storms, ev_wind_cyclone_hazard_wocat_7778_2026_impacts_of_cyclones_rain_storms].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: Both units are compiler ratings with no measurement, and the storm ratings concern rain-storm runoff damage rather than wind [ev_wind_cyclone_hazard_wocat_7778_2026_impacts_of_cyclones_rain_storms].

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: WOCAT compilers rate jessour in Tunisia and spate irrigation in Eritrea as coping well with drought, and water-spreading weirs in Ethiopia as coping moderately [ev_asset_drought_wocat_1013_2011_drought, ev_asset_drought_wocat_1333_2010_drought, ev_asset_drought_wocat_6715_2023_drought].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: All units are practitioner ratings with no observed damage data; spate systems depend on flood flows, so drought is more likely to cut their water supply than to damage the structures.

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: WOCAT compilers rate jessour in Tunisia and spate irrigation in Eritrea as coping well with local rainstorms, water-spreading weirs in Ethiopia as coping moderately, and marab agriculture in Jordan as coping very well [ev_asset_extreme_rainfall_wocat_1013_2011_local_rainstorm, ev_asset_extreme_rainfall_wocat_1333_2010_local_rainstorm, ev_asset_extreme_rainfall_wocat_6715_2023_local_rainstorm, ev_asset_extreme_rainfall_wocat_5770_2020_local_rainstorm].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: All units are practitioner ratings without observed damage or stated reasoning.

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: Spate-irrigation structures generally hold up against flood better than other water-harvesting types: projects in Sudan and Eritrea both reported their structures cope well with general river flooding [ev_asset_flood_wocat_1292_2015_general_river_flood, ev_asset_flood_wocat_1333_2010_general_river_flood], and a project in Jordan reported coping very well with flash flooding [ev_asset_flood_wocat_5770_2020_flash_flood].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: This is not universal: a project in Tunisia reported its structure copes not well with general river flooding [ev_asset_flood_wocat_1013_2011_general_river_flood]. Part of this effect is off-site (downstream or landscape scale) rather than on the adopting farm.

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: WOCAT compilers rate jessour in Tunisia and spate irrigation in Eritrea as coping well with local windstorms [ev_asset_wind_cyclone_wocat_1013_2011_local_windstorm, ev_asset_wind_cyclone_wocat_1333_2010_local_windstorm].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: Both units are practitioner ratings without observed damage or stated reasoning.

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: The compiler of a WOCAT sheet on water-spreading weirs in Ethiopia judged habitat and plant diversity slightly increased; no mechanism is described.
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: A single technology sheet supplies all units and it rated animal diversity unchanged; these are practitioner judgements, not measurements.

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: Compilers of WOCAT sheets for marab floodplain water harvesting in Jordan, water spreading in Sudan and water-spreading weirs in Ethiopia rate soil organic matter increased under these flood-spreading systems, and the Ethiopian sheet also rates emissions reduced; the sheets give no mechanism for these ratings.
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: All units are practitioner judgements with no compiler comment, not measurements; the Jordan sheet rates the gain strongly while the Sudan and Ethiopia sheets rate it as slight, and soil organic matter and emission ratings stand in for sequestration.

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: In Yemen, groundwater tables downstream of spate and conservation structures were maintained or increased, and although the main purpose of the spate irrigation systems was to capture floodwater, a large number of the beneficiary farmers interviewed indicated that groundwater levels increased considerably [ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_yem12_1, ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_yem12_2]. Groundwater is used here as a component of catchment water yield.
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: Both units come from one World Bank completion report — a results-framework comment and farmer interviews — so the evidence is self-reported, from one country, with no figure for recharge or flow [ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_yem12_1, ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_yem12_2]. No unit measures flow below the diversions.

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: Pooled costs are the up-front investment in floodwater-diversion systems: compiler-reported establishment costs per hectare from WOCAT sheets for Tunisia and Jordan (the Jordan sheet's total spread over 10 ha), and the average investment cost of spate systems under a World Bank project in Yemen, reported at USD 800-1200 per hectare with farmers contributing a 15-20% share.
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: WOCAT figures are the compiler's own cost tables for the documented technology, summed and converted to USD with the sheet's own exchange rate; they are not market prices. The cost class rests on the Tunisian sheet alone, because the Yemen completion-report range has no single value and the Jordan sheet is an upper-middle-income case; the Yemen report itself calls the farmer contribution comparatively high, and none of these is a cost per hectare restored.

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: WOCAT compilers for a floodplain marab system in Jordan and water-spreading weirs in Ethiopia rate drought impacts as reduced [ev_drought_hazard_wocat_5770_2020_drought_impacts, ev_drought_hazard_wocat_6715_2023_drought_impacts].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: Both units are compiler ratings with no comment or measurement behind them, and the Jordanian sheet is from an upper-middle-income country outside the target band [ev_drought_hazard_wocat_5770_2020_drought_impacts, ev_drought_hazard_wocat_6715_2023_drought_impacts].

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: Compilers of WOCAT sheets on marab floodplain water harvesting in Jordan and water-spreading weirs in Ethiopia judge drought impacts reduced, without describing the mechanism.
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: Only practitioner judgements from technology sheets, with no measurement; the Jordan sheet comes from an upper-middle-income context adjacent to the target.

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: In Ethiopia, a spate-irrigation structure was reported to reduce the speed and volume of downstream flooding [ev_flood_hazard_wocat_6715_2023_downstream_flooding]. In Morocco's High Atlas, farmers restoring low wadi terraces with stone walls and permeable groynes found that, where floods were frequent enough but not too strong, the stretch of wadi became stabilised, with flood peaks and sediment transport reduced [ev_flood_hazard_roose17_3].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: No evidence here covers conditions more severe than these: the pool reports no measured results at severe or extreme flood, and the Moroccan case explicitly says the stabilising effect holds only when floods are not too strong.

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: In Ethiopia, a spate-irrigation structure was reported to reduce the speed and volume of downstream flooding [ev_flood_hazard_wocat_6715_2023_downstream_flooding]. In Morocco's High Atlas, farmers restoring low wadi terraces with stone walls and permeable groynes found that, where floods were frequent enough but not too strong, the stretch of wadi became stabilised, with flood peaks and sediment transport reduced [ev_flood_hazard_roose17_3].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: No evidence here covers conditions more severe than these: the pool reports no measured results at severe or extreme flood, and the Moroccan case explicitly says the stabilising effect holds only when floods are not too strong.

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: In Ethiopia, a spate-irrigation structure was reported to reduce the speed and volume of downstream flooding [ev_flood_hazard_wocat_6715_2023_downstream_flooding]. In Morocco's High Atlas, farmers restoring low wadi terraces with stone walls and permeable groynes found that, where floods were frequent enough but not too strong, the stretch of wadi became stabilised, with flood peaks and sediment transport reduced [ev_flood_hazard_roose17_3].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: The evidence pool here is small, so the moderate class should be read as indicative rather than well established.

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: A single WOCAT compiler, for water spreading weirs in Ethiopia, rates the risk of production failure as lowered and attributes this to improved crop resilience from better soil moisture [ev_food_security_wocat_6715_2023_risk_of_production_failure].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: This cell is data deficient, not a finding of no effect: it rests on a single practitioner judgement from a documented technology sheet, with no household survey or measured change in food security [ev_food_security_wocat_6715_2023_risk_of_production_failure]. A second independent source or a measured food-security outcome for spate or floodwater-spreading systems is needed before a class can be stated.

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: Floodwater spreading and spate systems divert flood flows onto fields, and practitioners rate the gain in production as moderate. In Ethiopia, the expert is convinced crop production rose as water was harvested and spread over the farm as spate or supplementary irrigation [ev_crop_yield_wocat_6715_2023_crop_production]. Much of the gain goes to livestock: in Jordan the barley is mostly used to feed animals and the stubble is grazed, and in Eritrea crop residues are fed to livestock, both rated as a large rise in fodder [ev_forage_productivity_wocat_5770_2020_fodder_production, ev_forage_productivity_wocat_1333_2010_fodder_production]; in Ethiopia fodder and animal production rise a little with the soil and moisture kept behind the structure [ev_forage_productivity_wocat_6715_2023_fodder_production, ev_livestock_productivity_wocat_6715_2023_animal_production].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: Every finding is a practitioner rating from a technology sheet; there is no measured comparison, and the Ethiopian crop rating is stated as the expert's conviction rather than a yield comparison [ev_crop_yield_wocat_6715_2023_crop_production]. The strongest ratings are for fodder rather than food crops [ev_forage_productivity_wocat_5770_2020_fodder_production, ev_forage_productivity_wocat_1333_2010_fodder_production]. Evidence comes from 3 countries only (Eritrea, Ethiopia, Jordan).

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: The spate family's recurrent cost is the compiler's yearly maintenance table for a Jordanian marab floodplain system, costed over 10 ha and expressed per hectare per year [ev_project_cost_wocat_5770_2020_maintenance].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: This row is data deficient: one practitioner-reported figure from an upper-middle-income country, outside the target band [ev_project_cost_wocat_5770_2020_maintenance]. A second independent cost source, ideally from a low- or lower-middle-income country, is needed.

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: Floodwater-diverting systems are judged to pay back over time: compilers of WOCAT sheets for jessour in Tunisia, water spreading in Sudan, marab floodplain agriculture in Jordan and water-spreading weirs in Ethiopia rate the long-term returns on establishment as favourable or very favourable, and those for Tunisia, Jordan and Ethiopia rate long-term returns on maintenance the same way [ev_economic_return_wocat_1013_2011_costbenefit_establishment_long, ev_economic_return_wocat_1292_2015_costbenefit_establishment_long, ev_economic_return_wocat_5770_2020_costbenefit_establishment_long, ev_economic_return_wocat_6715_2023_costbenefit_establishment_long, ev_economic_return_wocat_1013_2011_costbenefit_maintenance_long, ev_economic_return_wocat_5770_2020_costbenefit_maintenance_long, ev_economic_return_wocat_6715_2023_costbenefit_maintenance_long].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: Every unit is a practitioner benefit-versus-cost judgement from a documented technology sheet, with no comment attached, not a household survey or measured income change, and poverty is reached only through a return proxy. The ratings are long-term; none speaks to the up-front cost of the works, and the Jordanian sheet comes from an upper-middle-income setting [ev_economic_return_wocat_5770_2020_costbenefit_establishment_long, ev_economic_return_wocat_5770_2020_costbenefit_maintenance_long].

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: In Morocco's High Atlas, low-terrace restoration in wadi beds was found to trap sediment before it could silt up dams downstream [ev_sediment_retention_roose17_4]. In Yemen, a project review found spate systems reduced wadi-bank damage and water-harvesting activities reduced erosion, a benefit emphasised by 64% of farmers interviewed [ev_erosion_hazard_yem12_5]. In Ethiopia, a project reported that physical barriers stop soil and water loss [ev_erosion_hazard_wocat_6715_2023_soil_loss].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: The evidence pool here is small, so the moderate class should be read as indicative rather than well established.

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: In Morocco's High Atlas, low-terrace restoration in wadi beds was found to trap sediment before it could silt up dams downstream [ev_sediment_retention_roose17_4].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: This is a single expert assertion with no measured data behind it, so a second independent source or a measured finding is needed before this cell can state a class.

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: Spate and water-spreading systems divert floodwater onto fields, and water productivity, the grain produced per unit of water, is the route by which that capture would ease water stress; the WOCAT guideline authors rate improving water productivity for the floodwater harvesting group as a gain, at the lowest step of their scale [ev_rain_water_productivity_wocwh13_2].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: This cell is data deficient, not a finding of no effect: its single unit is a group-level judgement in the WOCAT water-harvesting guidelines, direction only, with no measurement of water availability or water productivity for spate systems [ev_rain_water_productivity_wocwh13_2]. A second independent source, or any measured result on water access or water productivity under spate or water spreading, would let the cell state a class. The Yemeni groundwater reports sit in the spate catchment water yield row.

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: WOCAT compilers for marab floodplain agriculture in Jordan and water-spreading weirs in Ethiopia rate drainage of excess water as improved [ev_waterlogging_hazard_wocat_5770_2020_excess_water_drainage, ev_waterlogging_hazard_wocat_6715_2023_excess_water_drainage].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: Both units are practitioner ratings without stated reasoning or measurement, from technologies built to spread floodwater over fields [ev_waterlogging_hazard_wocat_5770_2020_excess_water_drainage, ev_waterlogging_hazard_wocat_6715_2023_excess_water_drainage].

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: The only unit is the WOCAT compiler rating for water-spreading weirs in Ethiopia, which records no change in the impacts of cyclones and rain storms, so no mechanism is evidenced [ev_wind_cyclone_hazard_wocat_6715_2023_impacts_of_cyclones_rain_storms].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: This row is data deficient: a single compiler rating from one technology sheet, with no comment or measurement, neither supports nor rules out an effect [ev_wind_cyclone_hazard_wocat_6715_2023_impacts_of_cyclones_rain_storms]. A second independent source or one measured finding is needed before this row can state a direction or size.

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: WOCAT compilers rate terraces, stone lines and stone bunds in China, Rwanda, Yemen, Cabo Verde, Uganda, Niger, Haiti and Tunisia as coping well with drought, and bench terraces in Bangladesh as coping moderately [ev_asset_drought_wocat_1522_2010_drought, ev_asset_drought_wocat_1553_2012_drought, ev_asset_drought_wocat_6610_2022_drought, ev_asset_drought_wocat_4284_2018_drought].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: All units are practitioner ratings of coping, with no observed damage or failure data.

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: Heavy rain moderately damages terraces and bunds. In China, storms caused widespread damage to terraces, with few local funds for repair [ev_climate_shock_iegchn07_7]. In Algeria, terraces and other traditional works were badly damaged or destroyed by extreme rain in recent years and are rebuilt after each event [ev_climate_shock_roose17_2_av]; stone lines are overtopped by storms above 50 mm [ev_climate_shock_roose17_1_av]; and unmaintained banquette networks breached in chains under long torrential rain [ev_climate_shock_arab04_1_av]. A review of terraces worldwide reports riser collapse and landslides that can grow into debris flows in very heavy storms [ev_climate_shock_arna15_8_av, ev_climate_shock_arna15_9_av], and poorly built vineyard terraces in Spain slid after a single storm [ev_climate_shock_wei16_2_av]. Practitioners rate terraces in Rwanda and Cape Verde and works in Niger as not coping well with local rainstorms [ev_asset_extreme_rainfall_wocat_1553_2012_local_rainstorm, ev_asset_extreme_rainfall_wocat_1573_2013_local_rainstorm, ev_asset_extreme_rainfall_wocat_1616_2014_local_rainstorm], and works in Bangladesh and Burkina Faso as coping only moderately with thunderstorms [ev_asset_extreme_rainfall_wocat_4284_2018_local_thunderstorm, ev_asset_extreme_rainfall_wocat_6729_2023_local_thunderstorm].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: Other practitioners rate their terraces as coping well, in China, Yemen, Uganda, Haiti and Bangladesh [ev_asset_extreme_rainfall_wocat_1522_2010_local_rainstorm, ev_asset_extreme_rainfall_wocat_1560_2013_local_rainstorm, ev_asset_extreme_rainfall_wocat_1589_2013_local_rainstorm, ev_asset_extreme_rainfall_wocat_3223_2017_local_rainstorm, ev_asset_extreme_rainfall_wocat_4284_2018_local_rainstorm], or very well in Thailand and Bangladesh [ev_asset_extreme_rainfall_wocat_4281_2018_local_rainstorm, ev_asset_extreme_rainfall_wocat_4284_2018_local_hailstorm]. Poor construction and missing maintenance come up repeatedly as part of the cause [ev_climate_shock_arab04_1_av, ev_climate_shock_wei16_2_av]. The review and the Algerian and Spanish findings are partly second-hand, and many units are practitioner ratings.

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: The WOCAT compiler for bench terraces in Bangladesh records that the technology copes moderately with forest fire and well with land fire [ev_asset_fire_wocat_4284_2018_forest_fire, ev_asset_fire_wocat_4284_2018_land_fire].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: The evidence is too thin to state a sensitivity: both units come from one technology sheet and are practitioner ratings, with no observed damage or fire event described, and coping moderately itself implies some damage [ev_asset_fire_wocat_4284_2018_forest_fire, ev_asset_fire_wocat_4284_2018_land_fire]. What is missing is a second independent source or one observed account of how terraces fared in a fire.

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: Banquettes lack the capacity to absorb runoff from erosive rains and overflow, diversion channels fill with eroded soil and overflow in the heaviest storms, and torrential rain collapses terrace walls or carries small terraces away in mass movements [ev_flood_hazard_heusch95_2, ev_flood_hazard_roose94_2, ev_erosion_hazard_willem21_3, ev_erosion_hazard_roose06_5]. WOCAT compilers judge radical terraces in Rwanda and contour stone bunds in Niger not to cope well with river floods, while stone-wall terraces in Cabo Verde, stone lines in Tunisia and gradoni orchard terraces in Uzbekistan are judged to cope well [ev_asset_flood_wocat_1553_2012_general_river_flood, ev_asset_flood_wocat_1616_2014_general_river_flood, ev_asset_flood_wocat_1573_2013_general_river_flood, ev_asset_flood_wocat_6610_2022_general_river_flood, ev_asset_flood_wocat_7553_2025_flash_flood].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: Failure is tied to maintenance and setting: rarely maintained diversion systems generally fail after 4 to 10 years, terrace collapse is linked to abandonment, and the Rwandan mass movement happened on terraces without trees [ev_flood_hazard_roose94_2, ev_erosion_hazard_willem21_3, ev_erosion_hazard_roose06_5]. The literature hazards are erosive rains, torrential rain and mass movements mapped to flood and come as expert and modelled statements without failure rates, and the WOCAT units are practitioner judgements from technology sheets rather than records of damage [ev_flood_hazard_heusch95_2].

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: Slope failure damages terraces where slopes are unstable or terraces are abandoned: in the Tizi Ouzou region of Algeria 19% of banquettes on marls and clays were damaged by landslides and as many by gullying, and in Mediterranean regions over 50% of abandoned terraces were vulnerable to gully erosion and landslides that collapse the dry-stone walls [ev_climate_shock_arab04_2_av, ev_climate_shock_wei16_1_av].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: WOCAT compilers judge stone lines in Tunisia and a continuous bench terrace for tea in a high sloping area of Thailand to cope well with landslides, and vetiver-hedge bench terraces with trees in Haiti and bench terraces on hilly slopes in Bangladesh to cope very well [ev_asset_landslide_wocat_6610_2022_landslide, ev_asset_landslide_wocat_4281_2018_landslide, ev_asset_landslide_wocat_3223_2017_landslide, ev_asset_landslide_wocat_4284_2018_landslide]. The damage figures are secondary citations tied to marl and clay substrates and to abandonment rather than to maintained terraces, and the ratings are practitioner judgements [ev_climate_shock_arab04_2_av, ev_climate_shock_wei16_1_av].

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: Stone bunds trap the sediment that runoff carries, and that sediment wears down their function: on Tigray cropland, Gebremichael and colleagues found that when the depression behind a bund fills with sediment its trapping efficiency strongly decreases, and considerable soil is still lost, on average 18 t per hectare a year [ev_climate_shock_gebr05_3_av]. The threat is a decline in the service the bund gives, not damage to the bund itself [ev_climate_shock_gebr05_3_av].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: The engine class is low. The row rests on a single Ethiopian study, which states that trapping falls as bunds fill but gives no measured rate for that decline. The study links the decline to lack of regular maintenance and raising of the bunds, so the threat applies to unmaintained bunds [ev_climate_shock_gebr05_3_av]. A claim that pressure on a filled bund leads to structural failure, cited to this study elsewhere, is not in it. Evidence on structural damage to terraces or bunds from sedimentation, and on how fast it happens, is missing.

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: WOCAT compilers rate stone-wall terraces in Cabo Verde and contour stone bunds in Niger as coping well with local windstorms, vetiver bench terraces in Haiti as coping well with tropical storms, and bench terraces in Bangladesh as coping moderately with both [ev_asset_wind_cyclone_wocat_1573_2013_local_windstorm, ev_asset_wind_cyclone_wocat_1616_2014_local_windstorm, ev_asset_wind_cyclone_wocat_3223_2017_tropical_storm, ev_asset_wind_cyclone_wocat_4284_2018_tropical_storm].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: All units are practitioner ratings without observed damage, and the progressive bench terrace in China is rated as not coping well with local windstorms, with no reason given [ev_asset_wind_cyclone_wocat_1522_2010_local_windstorm].

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: The sources point in opposite directions for different kinds of terrace and different kinds of diversity. The WOCAT compiler for contour stone bunds in Bhutan rates plant diversity as greatly increased, linking it to the soil becoming suitable for more diverse crops [ev_biodiversity_outcome_wocat_6891_2023_plant_diversity]. A rangeland-restoration review cites Stavi et al. (2015) from Israel suggesting that earthen contour bench terraces built by heavy machinery, which strip the soil's A-horizon from the hillslope, reduce the species richness of herbaceous vegetation, with Stavi and Argaman (2016) adding that the topsoil removal degrades soil quality [ev_biodiversity_outcome_stav20_9].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: Studies disagree, and what separates them is how the terrace is built and what is counted: hand-built stone bunds on cropland are credited with more crop diversity, while bulldozed earthen terraces on rangeland are linked to fewer wild herbaceous species [ev_biodiversity_outcome_wocat_6891_2023_plant_diversity, ev_biodiversity_outcome_stav20_9]. Neither side is a measured species or habitat comparison: the Bhutan unit is a compiler rating and the Israeli unit a cited suggestion in a review, and neither comes from the target low-income contexts. A measured biodiversity outcome on terraced land, with the construction method stated, is needed before a direction can be given.

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: A meta-analysis of over a thousand paired observations in China found terracing raised soil organic carbon across several regions: by 27%, 17.94% and 26.62% in different regions soon after construction [ev_soil_organic_carbon_zhang26h2_5], and by 60.96% and 14.11% in two further regions after 11 to 20 years, with 33.91% and 53.73% increases elsewhere after 21 to 30 years [ev_soil_organic_carbon_zhang26h2_10].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: The gains vary widely by region and by how long the terraces have been in place, so a single figure should not be read as the expected gain everywhere.

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: Terraces and contour ridges retain rainfall on slopes so part of it recharges groundwater: in Cameroon terraces would cause a groundwater recharge of 15 to 25% of rainfall, with drainage through rock fissures that could reach the piedmonts [ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_roose06_1], and hydrological modelling of contour ridges in Morocco, structures that promote the slow formation of terraces by sediment accumulation, estimates a 50% increase in recharge [ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_willem21_1]. Recharge is used here as a component of catchment water yield.
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: Recharge stands in for catchment yield; no unit measures flow leaving the catchment. The Cameroonian figure is a conditional estimate and the Moroccan figure a modelling result, both cited secondarily [ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_roose06_1, ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_willem21_1]. The Cameroonian source flags that the drainage could reach the unterraced piedmonts, a much more fragile environment [ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_roose06_1]. On-slope supply evidence for terraces is in the terracing water stress row.

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: Pooled costs are establishment costs per hectare for terraces: in Ethiopia the initial investment cost of terracing was US$ 46.51 per hectare in the first year of construction, with about US$ 48.8 per hectare more to maintain over the first three years [ev_project_cost_adgo13_8]; the WOCAT sheet for orchard terraces in Uzbekistan gives 2000 USD per hectare (a total of 3200 USD spread over 1.6 ha) [ev_project_cost_wocat_7553_2025_establishment]; rehabilitating pre-Columbian terraces (andenes) in Peru, a heavy earth- and stone-moving intervention, cost USD 2,200 per hectare in a 1994 assessment [ev_project_cost_fao13c_1]; and a review tabulates terracing costs from China of 1918 to 4045 USD per hectare (mechanisation, labour and socioeconomic costs), rising with the original slope from 5 to 25 degrees [ev_project_cost_wei16_1].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: The spread is wide and reflects what is built: the Ethiopian figure is a first-year construction cost, the Uzbek figure is the compiler's own cost table converted with the sheet's exchange rate rather than a market price, the Peru figure is a rehabilitation cost cited second-hand, and the Chinese costs are a secondary table for mechanised terracing. The Peru and Chinese units come from upper-middle-income settings, so the value range rests on the Ethiopian and Uzbek units [ev_project_cost_adgo13_8, ev_project_cost_wocat_7553_2025_establishment, ev_project_cost_fao13c_1, ev_project_cost_wei16_1].

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: Terracing and stone bunds slow runoff and let more rain infiltrate, conserving soil moisture through dry spells: in Burkina Faso, stone bunds were reported to conserve more moisture in the soil, helping alleviate water stress during dry spells [ev_soil_water_retention_zoug14_1], and separately to yield two to three times more than untreated plots in dry years [ev_crop_yield_zoug14_1_s]. In Uzbekistan, a project reported that capturing and infiltrating more water made the land less susceptible to drought [ev_drought_hazard_wocat_7553_2025_drought_impacts]. In the Peruvian Andes, terraced maize plots fared better than sloped fields during a 2002 dry spell [ev_drought_hazard_post05_1].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: The benefit is not guaranteed in the worst years: in Burkina Faso, a comparison found that in the driest year on record (1985), stone-bund-treated fields produced no more grain than untreated ones, so the treatment did not reduce the risk of famine in a particularly dry year [ev_crop_yield_roose94_2].

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: Terracing's drought buffer strengthens as dry days increase. In a nationally representative survey of Ethiopian cereal plots, terraced fields saw yields 14% lower than matched unterraced plots when dry days were few, but 17% higher when dry days were most frequent [ev_crop_yield_kosm18_5]; by consecutive dry spells instead, yields were 9% lower with few dry spells but 33% higher with the most [ev_crop_yield_kosm18_7]. In Burkina Faso, contour stone bunds with manure raised millet grain yields by 13% and sorghum grain yields by 34% over untreated control plots [ev_crop_yield_botreij09_12].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: This buffer still fails in the very driest years: in Burkina Faso, a comparison found that in the driest year on record (1985), stone-bund-treated fields produced no more grain than untreated ones, so the practice did not reduce the risk of famine in a particularly dry year [ev_crop_yield_roose94_2]. Measured harm (maladaptation) — the practice worsening this outcome for some adopters — appears in 1 source.

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: When rainfall is erratic, stone bunds conserve more moisture in the soil and ease crop water stress during dry spells, and crops behind stone bunds in Burkina Faso could yield two to three times more than control plots in dry years [ev_soil_water_retention_zoug14_1, ev_crop_yield_zoug14_1_s]. Rwandan land-husbandry project households showed greater resilience than controls to the 2016 drought and recovered faster, and the WOCAT compiler for orchard terraces in Uzbekistan rates drought impacts as reduced, noting that more water is captured and infiltrated, making the land less susceptible to droughts [ev_drought_hazard_rwa18_6, ev_drought_hazard_wocat_7553_2025_drought_impacts]. In a Peruvian bench-terrace study, farmers stated that a dry spell in the 2002 rainy season affected maize on the slopes but less so on the terraces, while 2003 had regular rainfall, and the study credits bench terraces with a water-conserving effect that reduces the risk of crop failure due to drought [ev_drought_hazard_post05_1]. Across Ethiopia's drought-season, nationally representative matched-plot data found cereal yields significantly higher on terraced than unterraced plots among plots with a high number of dry spells (plus 33 percent), the study's headline drought-buffer result [ev_crop_yield_kosm18_7], and higher but not significant among plots with a high share of dry days (plus 17 percent) [ev_crop_yield_kosm18_5]; among plots with an intermediate share of dry days, however, terraced yields were significantly lower (minus 13 percent) [ev_crop_yield_kosm18_4]. In a Canadian potato belt, terraced fields also had slightly higher yields than non-terraced fields in dry growing seasons [ev_crop_yield_lian19_1]. A CILSS regional synthesis adds two further Burkina Faso measurements from the same Central Plateau dry-spell season: contour stone bunds alone raised grain yield by 39 percent over untreated fields [ev_crop_yield_botreij09_4], and with an optimal manure application they raised grain yield by 109 percent in a rainfall-deficit year [ev_crop_yield_botreij09_12].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: Stone bunds in Burkina Faso gave no yield benefit in the driest year (1985) and so did not reduce famine risk then, which bounds the cited dry-year gain [ev_crop_yield_roose94_2, ev_crop_yield_zoug14_1_s]. The Rwandan finding comes from a bundled package whose terrace share is unknown, and the Uzbek unit is a compiler rating rather than a measurement [ev_drought_hazard_rwa18_6, ev_drought_hazard_wocat_7553_2025_drought_impacts]. The Peruvian terrace finding is the farmers' account of a single dry-spell season set against a regular season, a case study with no measured yield contrast [ev_drought_hazard_post05_1]. The Ethiopian intermediate-exposure penalty is attributed by the author to cropland lost to the terrace bench or stone riser itself rather than to water stress, and the plus-17-percent high-exposure result did not reach significance [ev_crop_yield_kosm18_4, ev_crop_yield_kosm18_5]. The Canadian comparison is a high-income, temperate commercial potato system built together with grassed waterways, so the terrace effect cannot be separated from the waterways, and the same study notes the extra soil moisture terraces conserve can depress yields in wet years [ev_crop_yield_lian19_1]. Both figures come from project tables of cited yield gains with no significance test, and the manured result already carries fertiliser alongside the bunds [ev_crop_yield_botreij09_4, ev_crop_yield_botreij09_12].

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: In Uzbekistan, a project reported that capturing and infiltrating more water made terraced land less susceptible to drought [ev_drought_hazard_wocat_7553_2025_drought_impacts].
