In the Peruvian Andes, terraced maize plots fared better than sloped fields during a 2002 dry spell, reducing the risk of crop failure from drought [ev_drought_hazard_post05_1].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: The evidence pool here is small, so the slight class should be read as indicative rather than well established.

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: The only unit is the compiler-reported establishment cost of one 200m vetiver line forming progressive bench terraces in Haiti, from a single WOCAT technology sheet's cost table converted to USD with the sheet's exchange rate [ev_project_cost_wocat_3223_2017_establishment].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: This row is data deficient: one compiler-reported figure for one structure type, not a market price or a measured project cost; a vetiver hedge line is a light, vegetative structure and is not representative of stone or earth terrace construction [ev_project_cost_wocat_3223_2017_establishment]. A second independent cost source is needed before the row can say whether terracing is cheap or costly to establish.

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: On intensively tended terraces all crop residues are grazed off as soon as harvests end, so bush fires have little fuel, and the WOCAT compiler for bench terraces in Bangladesh rates fire risk as reduced [ev_fire_hazard_roose06_1, ev_fire_hazard_wocat_4284_2018_fire_risk].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: The terrace statement is an expert estimate its authors say has no experimental basis on terraces, and the Bangladesh unit is a practitioner rating with no stated reasoning [ev_fire_hazard_roose06_1, ev_fire_hazard_wocat_4284_2018_fire_risk]. The effect depends on residues being removed by grazing.

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: Terraces and contour stone bunds slow and spread runoff on slopes: terraces lowered mean runoff and flood peaks on small mountain plots, stone bunds lower hillslope peak discharges and in high-rainfall years protect land from rapid flow in heavy rain [ev_flood_hazard_roose06_1, ev_flood_hazard_roose94_1, ev_erosion_hazard_zoug14_2]. In a semi-arid Tunisian catchment treated with dry-stone contour bunds and gully check structures, bundled with bench terraces and a catchment-wide grazing closure, the treatment's conclusion reports flood peaks and volumes falling by about 50% for mean and larger floods, and for the largest (upper-decile) floods peak discharge fell to 60-87% of its pre-treatment level [ev_flood_hazard_bergaoui00_1, ev_flood_hazard_bergaoui00_3]; a closer reading of the same paper's results table instead finds peak discharges strongly clipped but flood volume decreasing only for the envelope, most-extreme floods on record, with rise and base times nearly doubling [ev_flood_hazard_bergaoui00_2]. Compacted hill terraces with retention walls in Uttarakhand, India are credited with mitigating flood and landslide impact, and WOCAT compilers in Tunisia and Uzbekistan rate flooding as reduced, the Tunisian compiler noting stone lines and walls reduce peak flows during heavy rainfall and the Uzbek compiler that more water is trapped in the catchment [ev_flood_hazard_utk22_7, ev_flood_hazard_wocat_6610_2022_downstream_flooding, ev_flood_hazard_wocat_7553_2025_flood_impacts].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: Diversion banquettes and ditches, filed in this family, do the opposite: in Niger they raised peak discharges, and runoff-diversion systems accelerate concentration time with serious gullying risk if the dikes break [ev_flood_hazard_heusch95_1, ev_flood_hazard_roose94_3]. That Tunisian catchment paper disagrees with itself on volume: its results table for the mean flood hydrograph and for the large-flood hydrograph both report that flood volume was NOT significantly affected by the treatment, with only the peak and the timing changing [ev_runoff_reduction_bergaoui00_4, ev_runoff_reduction_bergaoui00_7] — the stronger 50% volume-reduction language in its conclusion describes the most extreme floods on record, not typical floods. Catchment-level peak-flow evidence for terraces is otherwise scarce, the Tunisian result bundles rangeland closure and gully stone-filling with the bunds [ev_flood_hazard_willem21_1, ev_flood_hazard_bergaoui00_1], the Uttarakhand claim is a Bank self-report, and the Tunisian and Uzbek units are compiler ratings [ev_flood_hazard_utk22_7, ev_flood_hazard_wocat_6610_2022_downstream_flooding, ev_flood_hazard_wocat_7553_2025_flood_impacts]. The studies disagree because they cover different structures: slope terraces and contour bunds that slow runoff in place, against diversion works that move it faster downslope.

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: Bench and progressive terraces, stone lines and contour stone bunds detain and spread runoff on slopes, lowering peak discharges and making flows last longer after rain [ev_flood_hazard_roose06_1, ev_flood_hazard_roose94_1]. A semi-arid Tunisian catchment treated with dry-stone contour bunds and gully check structures, bundled with bench terracing and a catchment-wide grazing closure, is reported in its conclusion to have cut flood peaks and volumes by about 50% for mean and larger floods, with the largest, upper-decile floods' peak discharge falling to 60-87% of its pre-treatment level [ev_flood_hazard_bergaoui00_1, ev_flood_hazard_bergaoui00_3]; its results table more specifically finds peak discharges of the most extreme floods on record strongly clipped and their volume decreased, with flood rise and base times nearly doubling [ev_flood_hazard_bergaoui00_2]. WOCAT compilers in Tunisia and Uzbekistan judge flooding reduced, the Tunisian stone-lines sheet citing lower peak flows during heavy rainfall [ev_flood_hazard_wocat_6610_2022_downstream_flooding, ev_flood_hazard_wocat_7553_2025_flood_impacts].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: The studies disagree because they cover different structures: diversion banquettes in Niger raised peak discharges, and runoff-diversion dikes speed up concentration time and risk gullying if they break, so design decides the sign [ev_flood_hazard_heusch95_1, ev_flood_hazard_roose94_3]. Catchment-scale evidence is otherwise scarce, with a review calling the terrace effect on peak flow uncertain; the Uttarakhand flood-mitigation claim is lender self-reported, and the WOCAT units are practitioner judgements rather than measurements [ev_flood_hazard_willem21_1, ev_flood_hazard_utk22_7]. The Tunisian figures are for a bundled treatment — contour bunds and gully check structures alongside bench terraces and a catchment-wide grazing closure — so no single component's share of the effect can be isolated, and the paper's own conclusion and its detailed results table frame the volume reduction differently: the largest reductions are reported for the most extreme floods on record, not for typical ones [ev_flood_hazard_bergaoui00_1, ev_flood_hazard_bergaoui00_2].

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: Terraces and stone bunds raise yields, enlarge the area that can be farmed and allow more diverse crops, and the evidence points to a large cut in food shortfall. Household food security improves in proportion to the area of a farm improved with bunds [ev_food_security_zoug14_1], and beneficiaries of Rwanda's terracing project saw drastically improved food consumption scores against a comparison group [ev_food_security_rwa18_5]. The WOCAT compiler for contour stone bunds in Bhutan writes that the larger cultivable area ensured food self-sufficiency and that clearing stones from the soil lets land users grow diverse crops throughout the year [ev_food_security_wocat_6891_2023_food_security_selfsufficiency, ev_food_security_wocat_6891_2023_risk_of_production_failure]. In Ethiopia's Anjene catchment, farmers recalled that before terracing the community was highly food insecure and migrated in search of food even in minor droughts, and that terraces improved crop production and reduced seasonal migration [ev_food_security_adgo13_11].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: Gains are slow on degraded land: the compiler for vetiver-hedge terraces in Haiti records no change in food security yet, because on very degraded land users have to wait for the soil to recover, though food security is expected to increase in the long run [ev_food_security_wocat_3223_2017_food_security_selfsufficiency]. The rating is large because the Rwandan evaluation calls the improvement drastic and the Bhutan practitioner gives the top score for lowering the risk of crop failure, but no study gives a number [ev_food_security_rwa18_5, ev_food_security_wocat_6891_2023_risk_of_production_failure]. The Bhutan and Haiti units are practitioner ratings; the Rwandan evaluation gives no magnitude, and the bund statement is an author's assertion rather than a measured result [ev_food_security_rwa18_5, ev_food_security_zoug14_1]. The Anjene account rests on farmer recall and group discussions rather than a measured comparison [ev_food_security_adgo13_11].

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: In Ethiopia's Tigray region, a farm survey found stone-bund-conserved plots had a yield premium of 412 Ethiopian Birr per hectare over non-conserved plots [ev_agricultural_production_value_kass08_1]. Nationally, terracing's drought-season effect strengthened with dry-day exposure: yields were 14% lower than matched unterraced plots when dry days were few, but 17% higher when dry days were most frequent [ev_crop_yield_kosm18_5].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: In normal years the balance can tip negative: across the same national dataset, terraced plots showed a slight but significant 9.5% reduction in cereal yield compared with unterraced plots when all exposure levels were pooled [ev_crop_yield_kosm18_1]; in semi-arid Tanzania, stone bunds reduced maize yield by 13% [ev_crop_yield_adim16_9]; and in Ethiopia's high-rainfall Amhara region, a farm survey found no significant yield difference between conserved and non-conserved plots, with the point estimate negative, which the authors link to possible waterlogging, weeds and pests in wetter areas [ev_agricultural_production_value_kass08_2]. Measured harm (maladaptation) — the practice worsening this outcome for some adopters — appears in 6 sources.

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: The only unit is the compiler-reported annual maintenance cost of one 200m vetiver line forming progressive bench terraces in Haiti, from a single WOCAT sheet's cost table converted to USD at the sheet's exchange rate [ev_project_cost_wocat_3223_2017_maintenance].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: This row is data deficient: one compiler-reported figure for one vegetative structure type, from the sheet's own cost table rather than a market price or a measured project cost, and not representative of stone or earth terrace upkeep [ev_project_cost_wocat_3223_2017_maintenance]. A second independent cost source is needed before the row can say whether terrace upkeep is cheap or costly.

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: A review of Ethiopian conservation practices found positive net present values for several terracing techniques: 2794 Ethiopian Birr per hectare for bench terraces, 3486.2 for stone bunds, and 5283.4 for level fanya juu [ev_economic_return_adim16_1, ev_economic_return_adim16_2, ev_economic_return_adim16_3].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: The economics are fragile in practice: in the Peruvian Andes, a financial cost-benefit analysis found terraces were not very efficient in most sites evaluated in 2003, profitable only where the slope field being replaced was unusually unproductive before terracing [ev_economic_return_post05_3]; and in Tigray, stone-bund building and maintenance costs were found to be nearly the same as the financial benefits from yield improvement, making the economic case close to break-even [ev_economic_return_nyss07_10]. Measured harm (maladaptation) — the practice worsening this outcome for some adopters — appears in 1 source.

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: In Tigray, Ethiopia, stone bunds trapped sediment at an average rate of 59 tonnes per hectare per year, and separately were found to have reduced sheet-and-rill soil loss from 57 to 18 tonnes per hectare per year, trapping 68% of it [ev_sediment_retention_gebr05_2, ev_erosion_hazard_gebr05_1]. A review of Ethiopian studies found stone bunds reducing surface runoff by 34.4% [ev_runoff_reduction_adim16_3].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: Terracing can also create new erosion pathways and still fail against gullying: the same Tigray stone bunds were found to increase the number of plot boundaries, which aggravates tillage erosion at an average rate of 19 tonnes per hectare per year [ev_erosion_hazard_gebr05_4]; and in Tunisia, banquettes were found not to stop the progression of gullying, with gullied areas increasing by 12% between 1963 and 1973 [ev_erosion_hazard_arab04_1]. Measured harm (maladaptation) — the practice worsening this outcome for some adopters — appears in 4 sources.

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: Terracing and retaining walls hold soil on slopes, which an evaluation in Morocco expects to reduce siltation of downstream rivers and dam storage [ev_sediment_retention_iegmar09_3]. Reviews add that fanya juu trapped 64% of sediment (80% with vetiver grass), and bench terracing cut sediment yield by 58% in a small USA watershed [ev_sediment_retention_meko14_6, ev_sediment_retention_meko14_5]. A terracing review finds terraces reasonably effective at reducing sediment transport, though about 20%–30% of sediment may still be delivered [ev_sediment_retention_arna15_6]. On Tigray cropland, Gebremichael and colleagues measured eroded soil accumulating behind stone bunds at 59 t per hectare a year across 202 plots, and a later paper by the same team reports, citing Nigussie et al. (2005), strongly decreased specific sediment yield in reservoirs whose catchments have a high density of stone bunds [ev_sediment_retention_gebr05_2, ev_sediment_retention_nyss07_13].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: The Morocco unit is an evaluator assertion; nothing on water chemistry is measured, and siltation is a component proxy [ev_sediment_retention_iegmar09_3]. The added sediment figures are secondary citations in reviews, in extreme rainfall the sediment accumulated on terraces can reach the channel [ev_sediment_retention_arna15_6], the bench-terrace figure comes from a high-income watershed, and Algerian banquettes had no influence on the sedimentation rate of a downstream dam over 1947-1968 [ev_sediment_retention_meko14_5, ev_sediment_retention_arab04_1]. The Tigray figure is on-field trapping, a component proxy for downstream water quality, part of it soil moved by tillage rather than by water, and the reservoir finding is a second-hand citation without a stated size; both come from the same research team [ev_sediment_retention_gebr05_2, ev_sediment_retention_nyss07_13].

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: Terraces and stone lines capture and retain rainwater on slopes, and stone lines contribute to increased infiltration of rainwater into the soil, thereby replenishing water resources [ev_water_access_deficit_wocat_6610_2022_water_quantity, ev_water_access_deficit_wocat_6610_2022_water_availability]. Measured soil moisture supports this: a meta-analysis gives terraces an SMD of 40.5% for soil moisture retention [ev_soil_water_retention_tefe24_6], a global terracing synthesis finds terraced sites more efficient than slopes at conserving soil water, with a mean δsm of 1.2 [ev_soil_water_retention_wei16_1], and conversion of slopeland to leveled fields in China increased moisture retention [ev_soil_water_retention_iegchn07_2]. Water productivity, the grain produced per unit of rain, is a route by which capture eases water stress. The FAO compilers rate improving water productivity for the cross-slope barrier group at the middle mark of their scale [ev_rain_water_productivity_faoslm11_3]. In Ethiopia's Anjene catchment, terraces improved the water productivity of teff, barley and maize by at least 100% against un-terraced plots [ev_rain_water_productivity_adgo13_7]. A review of farming terraces notes that the soil stays humid for longer on terraces than on sloping fields, and that a very flat terrace bed lets rain pond, reducing runoff and increasing infiltration [ev_soil_moisture_arna15_7]. In Tigray, stone bunds enhance soil moisture storage on both sides of the bund, especially on loamy and sandy soils, with 0.05–0.1 g g−1 more soil moisture at 1–1.5 m depth persisting for at least 2 months after the rainy season (Vancampenhout, 2003, reported by Nyssen et al.) [ev_soil_moisture_nyss07_4]. In Peru, farmers say the soil on bench terraces remains humid twice as long as on sloping fields [ev_soil_moisture_post05_8]. The Chinese terracing meta-analysis adds further terrace types confirmed effective for soil water storage [ev_soil_moisture_chen20_3, ev_soil_moisture_chen20_4, ev_soil_moisture_chen20_5, ev_soil_moisture_chen20_6], and in a Canadian potato belt simulated soil moisture was significantly higher on terraced than non-terraced fields [ev_soil_moisture_lian19_4].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: The Tunisian stone-line units are practitioner judgements, and catchment modelling in Peru found no difference in crop water distribution with partial terracing [ev_water_regulation_willem21_1]. Abandoned or degraded terraces worsen water regulation [ev_water_regulation_willem21_2]. The recharge estimates for terraces and contour ridges now sit in the terracing catchment water yield row. The terracing ratio is an unweighted mean across extracted cases from mixed-income countries [ev_soil_water_retention_wei16_1], and the Chinese finding comes from an independent World Bank evaluation reporting project monitoring with no control [ev_soil_water_retention_iegchn07_2]. That is a compiler judgement for a group spanning earth bunds, stone lines, vegetative strips and fanya juu terraces, direction only [ev_rain_water_productivity_faoslm11_3]. The same review cites work finding that the infiltration capacity of the soil is not particularly affected by terracing (Posthumus and Stroosnijder, 2010), so the gain comes from water held longer on the flat bed rather than a change in the soil [ev_soil_moisture_arna15_7]. The Anjene figure compares long-maintained terraces with un-terraced plots at a single catchment where farmers also use fertiliser [ev_rain_water_productivity_adgo13_7]. The Peruvian humidity finding is the farmers' account; the study could not measure it [ev_soil_moisture_post05_8]. The Tigray soil-moisture figure is an earlier study reported within Nyssen et al. [ev_soil_moisture_nyss07_4]. The Canadian comparison is modelled rather than measured and the terrace system was built together with grassed waterways, so the moisture gain cannot be separated from those [ev_soil_moisture_lian19_4].

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: Stone bunds hold runoff in the field, and in wet years this can waterlog parts of the field and harm crop production; millet behind stone bunds can suffer waterlogging when monthly rainfall exceeds 200 mm [ev_waterlogging_hazard_zoug14_1, ev_crop_yield_roose94_3].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: The harm is confined to wet years or very wet months and neither unit gives a magnitude or the share of the field affected; both are cited statements from Burkina Faso rather than measurements, so they mark a risk to watch where stone bunds are placed on soils or in seasons that already hold excess water [ev_waterlogging_hazard_zoug14_1, ev_crop_yield_roose94_3].

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: WOCAT compilers for radical terraces in Rwanda, vetiver bench terraces in Haiti and stone lines in Tunisia rate the impacts of cyclones and rain storms as reduced [ev_wind_cyclone_hazard_wocat_1553_2012_impacts_of_cyclones_rain_storms, ev_wind_cyclone_hazard_wocat_3223_2017_impacts_of_cyclones_rain_storms, ev_wind_cyclone_hazard_wocat_6610_2022_impacts_of_cyclones_rain_storms].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: All units are compiler ratings concerning rain-storm damage rather than wind, and the Haiti compiler says the impact is not yet measured [ev_wind_cyclone_hazard_wocat_3223_2017_impacts_of_cyclones_rain_storms].

water_harvesting_conservation__water_qua.mechanism: Soil and water conservation structures cut the nutrients and sediment that would otherwise wash into waterways. A review of Ethiopian studies found graded soil bunds reducing the loss of soil organic matter by up to 52%, total nitrogen by up to 48%, and available phosphorus by up to 41% [ev_nutrient_removal_adim16_1]. In Tigray, stone bunds were found to improve hydrological conditions off-site and strongly decrease sediment yield measured in reservoirs downstream of catchments with a high density of stone bunds [ev_sediment_retention_nyss07_13].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_qua.conditionality: This does not always show up downstream: in Algeria, a review found that banquettes had no influence on the sedimentation rate of the Oued Fodda dam between 1947 and 1968 [ev_sediment_retention_arab04_1]. Within this family, in-situ systems score strongest and cross-family readings weakest, so the roll-up states moderate rather than the pooled strong.

water_harvesting_conservation__water_qua.mechanism: In semi-arid catchments check dams on China's Loess Plateau are credited with cutting regional sediment export by about 85% and accounted for 37.2% to 72.2% of sediment reduction at the outlets of five catchments over 26 years, and loose-rock check dams on semi-arid USA rangeland retained 48.4% and 82.4% of watershed sediment yield [ev_sediment_retention_luca21_1, ev_sediment_retention_meko14_4, ev_sediment_retention_poly14_1].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_qua.conditionality: The USA check dams produced a twofold decline in outlet sediment per unit of peak runoff, but this was significant only at α = 0.2 [ev_sediment_retention_poly14_2]. Sediment retention is a component proxy for water quality, the Chinese figures are secondary citations in reviews, and the USA site is high-income rangeland rather than smallholder farmland [ev_sediment_retention_luca21_1, ev_sediment_retention_poly14_1].

water_harvesting_conservation__water_qua.mechanism: Among rainfed cropping systems, two structures trap most of the sediment reaching them. In Germany, small field-border detention ponds trapped 54-85% of the incoming sediment [ev_sediment_retention_fien05_1]. In the Canary Islands, gavia runoff-farming fields enclosed by earth walls receive 2 to 8 mm of sediment deposition a year from the upslope catchment, averaging 46.1 tonnes per hectare per year [ev_sediment_retention_roose17_2].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_qua.conditionality: Both units describe sediment being captured rather than released downstream, which is the service this row credits; the Canary Islands figure is sediment arriving at and settling within the cropped field itself, part of how the gavia system builds and feeds its own soil rather than a downstream water-quality measurement, and both sites are high-income (Germany, Spain) rather than the LIC/LMIC target.

water_harvesting_conservation__water_qua.mechanism: In Tigray, stone bunds trapped sediment at an average rate of 59 tonnes per hectare per year [ev_sediment_retention_gebr05_2], and were found to improve hydrological conditions off-site, decreasing sediment yield in reservoirs downstream of catchments with a high density of stone bunds [ev_sediment_retention_nyss07_13]. In Algeria's Souagui basin, gabion check dams built in an eroding gully were buried under trapped sediment after a single season [ev_sediment_retention_roose17_1].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_qua.conditionality: The evidence pool here is small, so the strength of the benefit is not well established.

water_harvesting_conservation__water_qua.mechanism: A review of sediment-trapping measures found bench terracing reducing sediment yield by 58%, rising to 79% when combined with other measures [ev_sediment_retention_meko14_5]. In Arizona, loose-rock check dams held back much of the watershed's sediment [ev_sediment_retention_poly14_1] and produced a twofold decline in sediment yield at the watershed outlet compared with an untreated watershed [ev_sediment_retention_poly14_2]. In Belgium, a 1000 cubic-metre pond with a 25-hectare catchment showed a short-term sediment-trapping efficiency of 58 to 100%, settling to 68% over a 33-year record [ev_sediment_retention_meko14_3]. In the Canary Islands, gavias fields catch on average 46.1 tonnes per hectare per year of sediment eroded from the slope above [ev_sediment_retention_roose17_2].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_qua.conditionality: The pool is small (5 findings from a few sites in Belgium, Spain and the United States, all high-income), several are cited second-hand, and the Arizona outlet result was significant only at a weak test level [ev_sediment_retention_poly14_2].

water_harvesting_conservation__water_qua.mechanism: A review of Ethiopian studies found graded soil bunds reducing the loss of soil organic matter by up to 52%, total nitrogen by up to 48%, and available phosphorus by up to 41% [ev_nutrient_removal_adim16_1]. In Tigray, stone bunds trapped sediment at an average rate of 59 tonnes per hectare per year [ev_sediment_retention_gebr05_2], and were found to improve hydrological conditions off-site, strongly decreasing sediment yield measured in reservoirs downstream of catchments with a high density of stone bunds [ev_sediment_retention_nyss07_13].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_qua.conditionality: Only 4 of the 14 units behind this cell state a numeric size for the effect, so the class is capped at moderate rather than the stronger reading the clearest examples would suggest on their own.

water_harvesting_conservation__water_qua.mechanism: On China's Loess Plateau, a decades-long check-dam campaign was found to have reduced sediment by about 85% and runoff by about 15%, and streamflow by about 39% [ev_sediment_retention_luca21_1]; in the Wuding River watershed, simulations found check dams cutting runoff by 12% and sediment by 11.7% [ev_sediment_retention_shi19_2], and in the nearby Huangfuchuan catchment, check dams were found to reduce the sediment load by 51.9% [ev_sediment_retention_shi19_8].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_qua.conditionality: This does not always show up downstream: in Algeria, a review found banquettes had no influence on the sedimentation rate of the Oued Fodda dam between 1947 and 1968 [ev_sediment_retention_arab04_1].

water_harvesting_conservation__water_str.mechanism: Terracing raises soil moisture by turning a slope into a flat surface that lets rain infiltrate instead of running off. A meta-analysis of studies across China found terraced land held 12.4% more soil moisture than sloping land on average [ev_soil_moisture_chen20_1], with the benefit varying by climate: 28.6% in semi-humid areas, 15.1% in semi-arid areas, and only 5.4% in humid areas, where soil moisture is less limiting [ev_soil_moisture_chen20_10]. In northern Burkina Faso, water-harvesting reservoirs built for crop irrigation were also found to serve livestock and household needs during periods of domestic water scarcity [ev_water_access_deficit_foxr03_7]. In a Zimbabwean cotton trial in the 2018–2019 drought season, tied contour ridges held significantly more moisture in the top 0–5 and 6–10 cm of soil than conventional tillage, though not at 11–15 cm [ev_soil_moisture_mand21_1].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_str.conditionality: The benefit can reverse at depth under trees: in the same China meta-analysis, terraces planted with forest showed drier deep soil than sloping land at 140–160 cm and 180–200 cm, which the authors attribute to deep-rooted trees drawing down water that rainfall does not replenish [ev_soil_moisture_chen20_14]. Measured harm, where the practice made water stress worse for some adopters, appears in 1 source. Overall the evidence points to a large reduction in water stress, though the size differs by climate and by type of structure. The Zimbabwe tied-ridge trial covers one drought season and found no difference in the deeper soil layer [ev_soil_moisture_mand21_1].

water_harvesting_conservation__water_str.mechanism: Terraces hold rainfall on the slope so more of it reaches the crop: in the Ethiopian highlands, fanya juu terraces improved the water productivity of the three crops studied (teff, barley and maize) by at least 100% over un-terraced plots, which the authors read as clear evidence of more efficient use of rainwater [ev_rain_water_productivity_adgo13_7].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_str.conditionality: The gain depends on there being rain to hold. In a Kenyan trial, tied ridging without organic inputs was insufficient for soil moisture conservation during meteorological drought and dry spells, since there was little or no rainwater to be held in the basins [ev_soil_water_retention_ndun23_1]. The Ethiopian figure compares long-maintained terraces with un-terraced plots at a single catchment where farmers also apply fertiliser, and the Kenyan result is for tied ridges rather than terraces, so the row rests on few sites and differing practices.

water_harvesting_conservation__water_str.mechanism: Storage and recharge structures ease water stress in semi-arid areas: production cisterns in semi-arid Brazil keep livestock watered while clay tanks are dry, an agency review credits consumption and production cisterns with a large drop in rural establishments without any water source, and subsurface dams raise water levels in existing wells used when other sources dry up [ev_water_access_deficit_arsky20_5, ev_water_access_deficit_castro22_1, ev_water_access_deficit_cirilo03_1]. In the field, pits and furrows keep rain in the root zone: in Burkina Faso zaï of 30–40 cm diameter and 1-m half-moons retained moisture for 2-3 weeks through dry spells, and zaï can retain moisture in the soil for seven to ten days after rainfall; in semi-arid Brazil tied furrows kept more soil moisture than the traditional flat system at all crop stages and depths [ev_soil_water_retention_zour25h1_7, ev_soil_water_retention_sawa11h1_8, ev_soil_water_retention_brito07_9].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_str.conditionality: Supply is bounded by storage: 57% of Kenyan sand dams would hold 4 months of water for their reported beneficiaries [ev_water_access_deficit_neuf17_1]. The Brazilian units are implementer or agency assessments, interviews or census inference from an upper-middle-income context rather than the low-income target [ev_water_access_deficit_castro22_1, ev_water_access_deficit_arsky20_5]. Well-level evidence for semi-arid bunds and zaï now sits in the catchment water yield rows. What upstream capture does to water downstream is a separate question, answered in the catchment water yield rows. The zaï and half-moon results come with compost in the pits, so the moisture gain cannot be credited to the pit alone [ev_soil_water_retention_zour25h1_7, ev_soil_water_retention_sawa11h1_8]. In the Brazilian trial deep ploughing, which is tillage alone and not a capture structure, scored as high as the tied furrows, and the trial ran a single season at a station of the agency that promotes the technology [ev_soil_water_retention_brito07_9].

water_harvesting_conservation__water_str.mechanism: In Algeria's semi-arid steppe, a bare, compacted runoff catchment (impluvium) upslope of cropped strips was found to make up for insufficient rainfall with an estimated 150 to 180 mm of additional water supply [ev_soil_moisture_roose17_2]. In southern Ethiopia, households with access to a sand dam used 635 litres of water per week in the dry season, compared with 498 litres for households without a sand dam [ev_water_access_deficit_lasa13_1].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_str.conditionality: The evidence pool here is limited to these two sources, so the moderate class should be read as indicative rather than well established.

water_harvesting_conservation__water_str.mechanism: Water-harvesting bunds and furrows raise soil moisture in rangeland by concentrating upslope runoff onto the treated strip. In Iran's Sistan-Baluchistan province, contour furrows 20-25 cm deep were reported to increase soil moisture and boost the productivity of the shrub vegetation they were cut for [ev_soil_moisture_stav20_6]. In Jordan's Badia, gravimetric soil moisture measured in micro-catchment water-harvesting bunds was 20.1 percent against 12.1 percent in the untreated interspace upslope [ev_soil_moisture_tats21_1].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_str.conditionality: The Iranian finding is a review's citation of another study rather than a direct measurement, with the increase not quantified [ev_soil_moisture_stav20_6]. The Jordanian figure is a single sampling date at the peak of the rainy season, compares the bund to the runoff-contributing interspace strip (not to unworked land away from the system), and the water-harvesting bund was built together with planted saltbush shrubs and a grazing exclusion, so the moisture gain cannot be separated from those [ev_soil_moisture_tats21_1]. Both cases are upper-middle-income dryland pastoral settings; direct evidence for lower-income rangeland systems is not yet available.

water_harvesting_conservation__water_str.mechanism: In the Canary Islands, the gavias runoff-harvesting system was found to store nearly 350 mm of water in the top metre of soil even in the driest years, when rainfall was below 100 mm [ev_soil_moisture_roose17_3]. In South Korea, traditional mool-tong water-harvesting structures were found to reduce the occurrence of water deficit from 30% to 20% [ev_water_access_deficit_silv26_1]. In a Canadian potato-growing watershed, terraced fields had a significantly higher soil-moisture index than non-terraced fields (p < 0.001) [ev_soil_moisture_lian19_4].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_str.conditionality: The evidence pool here is small (three sources across three countries), so the strong class should be read with that limited base in mind.

water_harvesting_conservation__water_str.mechanism: In low and lower-middle-income settings, pits, bunds, terraces and check dams increase infiltration and groundwater recharge, raising well levels and spring discharge, and sand dams store water that extends the months of water access. WOCAT compilers for jessour, spate and water-spreading systems, bunds, terraces, check dams, sand dams, ponds and haffirs from Tunisia, Niger, Ethiopia, Kenya, India, Somalia and elsewhere judge them to improve water harvesting, water quantity or water availability.
water_harvesting_conservation__water_str.conditionality: Many literature units are lender-reported or community perceptions and the WOCAT units are practitioner judgements from technology sheets; compilers judge no change in water availability for water spreading in Sudan and semi-circular bunds in Niger [ev_water_access_deficit_wocat_1292_2015_water_availability, ev_water_access_deficit_wocat_1614_2014_water_availability]. Groundwater gains in India could be wiped out by increased pumping, year-round wells did not increase in Burkina Faso, and many Kenyan sand dams lack capacity to supply even one household through the dry season [ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_iegind11_4, ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_kabo04_2, ev_water_access_deficit_ritc21_3].

water_harvesting_conservation__water_str.mechanism: Terraces and check dams hold water where it is needed. A global terracing synthesis finds terraced sites more efficient than slopes at reducing runoff and conserving soil water (e.g., soil moisture recharge), with a mean δsm of 1.2 [ev_soil_water_retention_wei16_1]. A terracing review cites Posthumus and Stroosnijder (2010) finding that the soil stays humid for longer on terraces than on sloping fields, and that ponding on very flat terrace beds increases infiltration [ev_soil_moisture_arna15_7], and a check-dam review reports that check dams that store seasonal runoff solve local scarcity in supply [ev_water_access_deficit_luca21_1].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_str.conditionality: Both sources pool cases from high- and lower-income countries, so the cell does not isolate the low-income target [ev_soil_water_retention_wei16_1, ev_water_access_deficit_luca21_1]. The terracing ratio is an unweighted mean across extracted cases, and soil moisture is read as a component of water stress rather than water stress itself [ev_soil_water_retention_wei16_1]. The check-dam and terrace-moisture findings are secondary citations within reviews, and the same terrace study reports infiltration capacity itself not particularly affected by terracing [ev_water_access_deficit_luca21_1, ev_soil_moisture_arna15_7]. What upstream capture does to water downstream is answered in the catchment water yield rows.

water_harvesting_conservation__water_str.mechanism: Terracing raises soil moisture by turning a slope into a flat surface that lets rain infiltrate instead of running off. A meta-analysis of studies across China found terraced land held 12.4% more soil moisture than sloping land on average [ev_soil_moisture_chen20_1], with gains of 14.0% on cropland specifically [ev_soil_moisture_chen20_11]. In Brazil's semi-arid Northeast, a farmer reported that after receiving a pumped cistern, household water no longer had to be fetched from distant ponds, and the family's clay-pot reserves dried up while animals drew on the cistern instead [ev_water_access_deficit_arsky20_5].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_str.conditionality: The size of the benefit is not consistent across methods: in a Chinese ridge-and-furrow potato trial, no difference in water-use efficiency was found between soil ridges and flat planting averaged over two seasons [ev_rain_water_productivity_wang07_4]. Measured harm (maladaptation) — the practice worsening this outcome for some adopters — appears in 1 source.

water_harvesting_conservation__waterlogg.mechanism: Practices that hold water on the cropped field backfire in wet conditions: in wet years stone bunds in Burkina Faso may cause waterlogging in some parts of the field, millet behind stone bunds can suffer waterlogging when monthly rainfall exceeds 200 mm, and in the Sudanian zone of Cameroon, where rainfall exceeds 1 200 mm per year, sorghum in zaï pits yielded less than on flat-cultivated fields [ev_waterlogging_hazard_zoug14_1, ev_crop_yield_roose94_3, ev_crop_yield_roose93_4]. In an Ethiopian Rift Valley trial waterlogging lasting 3–5 days during early maize growth also affected the mulching and basin treatments [ev_waterlogging_hazard_sime15h2_1, ev_waterlogging_hazard_sime15h2_2]. In southern Africa an FAO study shows by a water-balance calculation that planting basins can depress yields when too much water concentrates in them under high rainfall or in seasons with abnormally high rainfall, and concludes that in sub-humid environments yields could be affected by water-logging in years with adequate rainfall [ev_waterlogging_hazard_faocr11_8, ev_waterlogging_hazard_faocr11_7]. In a Kenyan on-farm trial, ridged plots with fertiliser at the relatively wetter sub-humid Rachuonyo site gave the lowest yields, slightly below conventional practice, which the authors say can probably be explained by waterlogging caused by ridging [ev_crop_yield_rock09_6]. Biazin et al. cite Jensen et al. (2003) from Tanzania: tied ridges helped maize in years of near-normal (500–600 mm) rainfall, but in wet years (700–900 mm) the maize showed waterlogging effects [ev_waterlogging_hazard_biaz12_15].
water_harvesting_conservation__waterlogg.conditionality: Every unit in the row points the same way, so the practice is rated as worsening waterlogging, but none states how large the loss is or what share of a field is affected, so the strength is not quantified. The harm is tied to wet years, high-rainfall zones or sub-humid sites: it comes from using in-field water-holding practices (pits, basins, mulch, ridges, stone bunds) outside their rainfall window, and says nothing about storage or diversion structures, which have no waterlogging evidence left in this row. The Cameroon observation is unpublished work cited by the authors, and the Burkina Faso statements and the Tanzanian tied-ridge result are cited from earlier studies [ev_crop_yield_roose93_4, ev_crop_yield_roose94_3, ev_waterlogging_hazard_zoug14_1, ev_waterlogging_hazard_biaz12_15]. The Ethiopian finding is a field observation with no measured yield loss, and the source names a tillage treatment as the one particularly affected, so only part of the harm can be put on mulch and basins [ev_waterlogging_hazard_sime15h2_1, ev_waterlogging_hazard_sime15h2_2]. The southern African basin finding rests on a theoretical water balance plus extension reports and farmer testimony, and the sub-humid conclusion covers conservation agriculture bundled with reduced tillage [ev_waterlogging_hazard_faocr11_8, ev_waterlogging_hazard_faocr11_7]. The Kenyan ridging loss is the authors' probable explanation rather than a measured waterlogging contrast, and the ridging is bundled with fertiliser [ev_crop_yield_rock09_6]. The Cameroon, Burkina Faso and Kenyan losses are held out of the production classes as performance caveats and counted here as waterlogging evidence.

water_harvesting_conservation__waterlogg.mechanism: In low and lower-middle-income settings, stone bunds can waterlog parts of the field in wet years, millet behind stone bunds can suffer waterlogging when monthly rainfall exceeds 200 mm, and sorghum in zaï pits in the humid Sudanian zone of Cameroon yielded less than on flat-cultivated fields; WOCAT compilers for pits and stone lines in Niger and conservation tillage in Kenya also rate drainage of excess water as worse [ev_waterlogging_hazard_zoug14_1, ev_crop_yield_roose94_3, ev_crop_yield_roose93_4, ev_waterlogging_hazard_wocat_1100_2011_excess_water_drainage, ev_waterlogging_hazard_wocat_940_2010_excess_water_drainage]. Compilers for check dams in Nepal and India, bench terraces in Yemen, water-spreading weirs and check dams in Ethiopia, ripper tillage in Zambia and composted planting pits in Burkina Faso rate drainage as improved [ev_waterlogging_hazard_wocat_1493_2011_excess_water_drainage, ev_waterlogging_hazard_wocat_5210_2019_excess_water_drainage, ev_waterlogging_hazard_wocat_959_2010_excess_water_drainage].
water_harvesting_conservation__waterlogg.conditionality: Harm appears in wet years or high-rainfall zones and is not quantified, and the units that report it are cited statements or an unpublished observation, while the opposing units are practitioner ratings; the Indian farm-pond sheet rates drainage as unchanged [ev_crop_yield_roose93_4, ev_waterlogging_hazard_wocat_1474_2011_excess_water_drainage]. The direction depends on whether a practice ponds water in the field or channels it away.

water_harvesting_conservation__waterlogg.mechanism: WOCAT compilers for the rehabilitation of ancient terraces in Peru, reinforced stone-wall terraces in Cabo Verde and marab floodplain agriculture in Jordan rate drainage of excess water as improved [ev_waterlogging_hazard_wocat_1506_2011_excess_water_drainage, ev_waterlogging_hazard_wocat_1573_2013_excess_water_drainage, ev_waterlogging_hazard_wocat_5770_2020_excess_water_drainage].
water_harvesting_conservation__waterlogg.conditionality: All units are practitioner ratings with no measurement; the Philippine conservation-tillage sheet rates drainage as worse and the Chinese check-dam sheet rates it unchanged [ev_waterlogging_hazard_wocat_1021_2011_excess_water_drainage, ev_waterlogging_hazard_wocat_1455_2011_excess_water_drainage].

water_harvesting_conservation__waterlogg.mechanism: Under rainfed cropping the harm comes where water is held on the cropped field in wet conditions: in wet years stone bunds in Burkina Faso may cause waterlogging in some parts of the field, millet production can suffer waterlogging when monthly rainfall exceeds 200 mm, and in the Sudanian zone of Cameroon, where rainfall exceeds 80 mm per day and 1 200 mm per year, sorghum in zaï pits yielded less than on flat-cultivated fields because of frequent soil waterlogging and the risk of nutrient leaching [ev_waterlogging_hazard_zoug14_1, ev_crop_yield_roose94_3, ev_crop_yield_roose93_4]. In southern Africa, an FAO study shows by a water-balance calculation that planting basins can depress yields when too much water concentrates in them under high rainfall or in seasons with abnormally high rainfall, citing extension reports and farmer testimony of farmers scooping water from the basins [ev_waterlogging_hazard_faocr11_8], and concludes that in sub-humid environments yields could be affected by water-logging in years with adequate rainfall [ev_waterlogging_hazard_faocr11_7]. Tied ridges behave the same way: in Tanzania they benefited maize in years of near-normal rainfall (500–600 mm), but in wet years (700–900 mm) waterlogging effects were observed (Jensen et al., 2003, cited by Biazin et al.) [ev_waterlogging_hazard_biaz12_15].
water_harvesting_conservation__waterlogg.conditionality: Every unit in the row points the same way, so the practice is rated as worsening waterlogging, but none of the harm sources gives a magnitude or the share of a field affected, so the strength is not quantified. The harm comes from practices that keep water on the cropped field (pits, basins, mulch, stone bunds) used outside their rainfall window, in wet years or high-rainfall zones; the row holds no evidence on storage or diversion structures. The Cameroon zaï and Burkina Faso millet losses are held out of the production classes as performance caveats and counted here as waterlogging hazard evidence [ev_crop_yield_roose93_4, ev_crop_yield_roose94_3]. The Cameroon observation is unpublished work cited by the authors, and the Burkina Faso statements are cited from earlier studies [ev_crop_yield_roose93_4, ev_waterlogging_hazard_zoug14_1, ev_crop_yield_roose94_3]. The southern African basin finding rests on a theoretical water balance plus extension reports and farmer testimony, and the author notes there are currently few published data to substantiate it [ev_waterlogging_hazard_faocr11_8]; the sub-humid conclusion goes beyond what the crop model simulates and covers conservation agriculture as basins or ripping with residue retention, so it is bundled with reduced tillage; neither gives a magnitude [ev_waterlogging_hazard_faocr11_7]. The Tanzanian tied-ridge observation is cited second-hand and gives no yield loss [ev_waterlogging_hazard_biaz12_15].

water_harvesting_conservation__waterlogg.mechanism: In upper-middle-income countries the only evidence is WOCAT compiler ratings, and most say the practice improves drainage of excess water: compilers for terraces in Peru and Cabo Verde and for marab floodplain farming in Jordan rate drainage as improved, the Peruvian sheet at the top of the scale [ev_waterlogging_hazard_wocat_1506_2011_excess_water_drainage, ev_waterlogging_hazard_wocat_1573_2013_excess_water_drainage, ev_waterlogging_hazard_wocat_5770_2020_excess_water_drainage].
water_harvesting_conservation__waterlogg.conditionality: The ratings split by sub-practice: the Philippine conservation-tillage sheet rates drainage worse and the Chinese check-dam sheet rates it unchanged [ev_waterlogging_hazard_wocat_1021_2011_excess_water_drainage, ev_waterlogging_hazard_wocat_1455_2011_excess_water_drainage], so the improvement belongs to structures that terrace or spread runoff, not to tillage that holds water in the field. No unit is measured; these are compiler judgements without a magnitude, and none covers severe or extreme waterlogging. The measured and cited harm results under rainfed cropping come from low and lower-middle income countries and are outside this scope.

water_harvesting_conservation__waterlogg.mechanism: Practices that hold water in the field can backfire in wet conditions: stone bunds can waterlog parts of the field in wet years, millet behind stone bunds can suffer waterlogging when monthly rainfall exceeds 200 mm, and in the humid Sudanian zone of Cameroon sorghum in zaï pits yielded less than on flat-cultivated fields [ev_waterlogging_hazard_zoug14_1, ev_crop_yield_roose94_3, ev_crop_yield_roose93_4]. In an Ethiopian Rift Valley trial, waterlogging lasting 3–5 days during early maize growth also affected the mulching and basin treatments, whose waterlogged plants had yellow leaves and stunted growth [ev_waterlogging_hazard_sime15h2_1, ev_waterlogging_hazard_sime15h2_2]. In a Kenyan on-farm trial, ridged plots with fertiliser at the relatively wetter sub-humid Rachuonyo site gave the lowest yields, slightly below conventional practice, which the authors say can probably be explained by waterlogging caused by ridging [ev_crop_yield_rock09_6].
water_harvesting_conservation__waterlogg.conditionality: Every unit points the same way, but the harm is tied to wet years, very wet months or high-rainfall zones, and none gives the size of the yield loss or the share of field affected, so this is a warning about placing water-holding practices where water is already in excess rather than a measured penalty [ev_waterlogging_hazard_zoug14_1, ev_crop_yield_roose93_4]. The Burkina Faso statements are cited rather than measured, and the Cameroon observation is unpublished work cited by the authors [ev_crop_yield_roose94_3, ev_crop_yield_roose93_4]. The Ethiopian waterlogging finding is a field observation with no measured yield loss, and the source names a tillage treatment as the one particularly affected, so only part of the harm can be put on mulch and basins [ev_waterlogging_hazard_sime15h2_1, ev_waterlogging_hazard_sime15h2_2]. The Kenyan ridging loss is the authors' probable explanation rather than a measured waterlogging contrast, and the ridging is bundled with fertiliser; because it comes from using the practice at a wetter site than it suits, it is held out of the production classes as an envelope misfit (a suitability caveat) and counted here as waterlogging evidence [ev_crop_yield_rock09_6].

water_harvesting_conservation__waterlogg.mechanism: In upper-middle-income settings, WOCAT compilers for water-harvesting works in Peru, Cabo Verde and Jordan rate drainage of excess water as improved, the Philippine conservation-tillage compiler rates it worse, and the Chinese check-dam sheet records no change [ev_waterlogging_hazard_wocat_1506_2011_excess_water_drainage, ev_waterlogging_hazard_wocat_1573_2013_excess_water_drainage, ev_waterlogging_hazard_wocat_5770_2020_excess_water_drainage, ev_waterlogging_hazard_wocat_1021_2011_excess_water_drainage, ev_waterlogging_hazard_wocat_1455_2011_excess_water_drainage].
water_harvesting_conservation__waterlogg.conditionality: Every unit is a practitioner rating of drainage on a technology sheet, with no comment and no measured waterlogging or yield loss. The measured harm in the wider pool, in-field capture that waterlogged crops in wet years or high-rainfall zones, comes mostly from low- and lower-middle-income settings and is not in this scope, so this row says only that these structures were judged to drain well where they were documented.

water_harvesting_conservation__wind_cycl.mechanism: A single WOCAT compiler, for stone lines, gabions and rock check dams in Somalia, rates the impacts of cyclones and rain storms as reduced, saying the structures stabilised the landscape and reduced damage from intense rainfall and stormwater runoff [ev_wind_cyclone_hazard_wocat_7778_2026_impacts_of_cyclones_rain_storms].
water_harvesting_conservation__wind_cycl.conditionality: This cell is data deficient, not a finding of no effect: it rests on a single compiler rating with no measurement, and that rating concerns rain-storm damage rather than wind [ev_wind_cyclone_hazard_wocat_7778_2026_impacts_of_cyclones_rain_storms]. A second independent source, or any measured finding on how the practice fares under cyclones or wind storms, is needed before a class can be stated.

water_harvesting_conservation__wind_cycl.mechanism: The WOCAT compiler for mechanised Vallerani micro water harvesting in Jordan rates the impacts of cyclones and rain storms as reduced [ev_wind_cyclone_hazard_wocat_5860_2021_impacts_of_cyclones_rain_storms].
water_harvesting_conservation__wind_cycl.conditionality: This rests on a single practitioner rating with no stated reasoning, and the compilers for conservation tillage in the Philippines and stone-wall terraces in Cabo Verde rate wind velocity as unchanged [ev_windbreak_protection_wocat_1021_2011_wind_velocity, ev_windbreak_protection_wocat_1573_2013_wind_velocity].
